It holds a memorial plaque honoring soldiers killed in the Battle of the Han River Defense Line, which held back North Korean forces from crossing the Han River for six days right after Seoul fell early in the Korean War. The futsal and jokgu courts adjoining the park can be booked through Seoul's public-service reservation system. Nodeul Naru Park is also a great spot to watch the fireworks during the Yeouido Fireworks Festival.

조선일보-뉴지엄-2553942.name: The Chosun Ilbo Newseum
조선일보-뉴지엄-2553942.description: The Chosun Ilbo, founded in 1920, opened the Newseum to trace over a century of its history and offer hands-on media education. Combining the ideas of 'news' and 'museum,' it spans a media experience hall on the 2nd floor and a Chosun Ilbo history hall on the 3rd. The history hall traces the newspaper's story through its first issue and countless other artifacts, offering both a lesson in the history of Korean journalism and a look at how newspapers captured the society of their time and evolved into today's new media. The media experience hall is organized into zones — a Media Square, reporter training room, AR-assisted reporting simulation, broadcast studio, VR news center, and news gallery — giving young visitors a hands-on look at how newspapers and broadcasts are made. Blending print, broadcast, and VR technology, the Chosun Ilbo Newseum is Korea's first media experience hall of its kind.

오미요리연구소-2029564.name: Omi Culinary Institute
오미요리연구소-2029564.description: Omi Culinary Institute teaches Korean cooking using seasonal ingredients sourced from Gyeongdong Market, Cheongnyangni Market, and the Yangnyeongsi herbal market, letting students cook the dishes themselves. It offers a systematic way to learn the depth of Korean cuisine, including its fermentation traditions. Classes use fresh seasonal Korean ingredients and can be tailored for vegetarian, allergy, or religious dietary needs. With many international visitors, classes are taught in English and Chinese. Regular classes cap at 8–10 students; larger groups need to arrange in advance, and bookings are available online. Omi Culinary Institute won a Korea Tourism Organization tourism-venture competition in 2014, was selected as a tourism venture in 2016, won the top prize for outstanding food-tourism programs from the Korean Food Promotion Institute in 2020, and received the Seoul Tourism Award in 2021.

수암사-서울-761264.name: Suamsa Temple (Seoul)
수암사-서울-761264.description: Set on a south-facing, auspicious slope halfway up Suraksan, Suamsa is a temple directly under the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism. It was founded in 621 (Silla's King Jinpyeong's 43rd year) by State Preceptor Wongwang, author of the Five Secular Precepts for the Hwarang knights, who built it in hopes of achieving the unification of the Three Kingdoms. Burned down during the Manchu invasion in the Joseon dynasty, only its stone-cave hall survived until it was rebuilt. The grounds today include the traditionally painted Geungnakbojeon hall (built in 1962), a Samseonggak shrine, a monks' quarters, and a standing Maitreya statue erected in 1972. A large rock beside the Geungnakbojeon bears a carved image of a dragon ascending to heaven clutching a wish-fulfilling jewel, and a red pine within the temple grounds twists as if it too were several dragons ascending. A stone-cave hall here is said to have a mysteriously flowing spring. It can be visited alongside Doansa, Songamsa, and Doseonsa while hiking Suraksan.

구로공단-노동자생활체험관-2553960.name: Guro Industrial Complex Workers' Life Experience Hall
구로공단-노동자생활체험관-2553960.description: Also known as 'Sooni's House, Geumcheon,' this experience hall is part of a Geumcheon-gu heritage project documenting the history of the Guro Industrial Complex and the lives of its workers, built to honor the contributions of Guro factory workers to Korea's industrialization and democratization. It recreates the cramped rooms where female factory workers lived while working at the Guro complex from the late 1960s through the 1980s, letting visitors experience what an evening off work was like for them at the time. Programs include an AR experience following 'a day in Sooni's life,' a walking history tour, tasting old-style snacks, making keyrings, and photo sessions.

구로근린공원-이씨레물리노공원-2591829.name: Guro Neighborhood Park (Issy-les-Moulineaux Park)
구로근린공원-이씨레물리노공원-2591829.description: Guro Neighborhood Park was built in August 2008 as a rest space for local residents. Bordering several cultural and arts venues, including the Guro Community Center, it's a good spot for a family cultural outing. At the park's entrance stands a sculpture marking Guro-gu's sister-city friendship with Issy-les-Moulineaux, France. The park also brings together a large performance hall, an outdoor stage, a fountain, an indoor rest area, and outdoor benches, connecting to a school park created when the adjoining Yeongrim Middle School opened up its fence. Guro Neighborhood Park sits at the start of Art Valley-gil, within about 10 minutes of Guro Street Park and Guro Library. Its most notable cultural venue is the Guro Art Valley Theater on the park's left side. The 150m path from the park to Yeongrim Middle School's front gate was designated a 'Seoul Street for Walking,' lined on both sides with ginkgo trees, making for a pleasant stroll.

고척동-고인돌-2591799.name: Gocheok-dong Dolmen
고척동-고인돌-2591799.description: This Bronze Age tomb sits in Gocheok-dong, Guro-gu, within the grounds of the Sinjeong-ri earthen fortress, a Three Kingdoms-era structure on the hill behind Gocheok High School. First discovered by a Seoul National University survey team in 1998, later study by relevant scholars found no matching stones near the capstone, suggesting it had been moved from its original location. Though modest in scale, a stone chamber has been identified, and the arrangement of its supporting stones points to it being a dolmen. As the only known dolmen in Guro-gu, it offers valuable insight into the Bronze Age culture of the surrounding area alongside the nearby Gocheok-dong artifact scatter site. It lies along the Guro Olle-gil trail, making it easy to visit on a light walk.

오류동역-광장-2778135.name: Oryu-dong Station Plaza
오류동역-광장-2778135.description: Oryu-dong Station Plaza sits in front of Exit 3 of Oryu-dong Station (Line 1) in Guro-gu. To the left, facing the station, exercise equipment, benches, and a walking path give local residents a spot to meet and rest; to the right is a public parking lot. It doubles as an event space for community programs and bazaars and as everyday convenience space for local residents.

묵정어린이공원-2762874.name: Mukjeong Children's Park
묵정어린이공원-2762874.description: Mukjeong Children's Park, in Chungmu-ro, Jung-gu, opened in 1992 and was renovated in 2007, offering a rest spot for nearby residents ever since. With broad green space and a range of play equipment, it gives children plenty of room to run and play, alongside exercise facilities, benches, and sculptures, all set amid pine trees and other well-tended plantings that make for an attractive park.

기억의-터-일본군-위안부-2655928.name: Site of Remembrance (Japanese Military "Comfort Women")
기억의-터-일본군-위안부-2655928.description: The Japanese Military 'Comfort Women' Site of Remembrance, on Namsan in Yejang-dong, Jung-gu, opened in 2016. Built as a memorial park honoring the survivors, it centers on their testimony, records of what they suffered, and documentation of wartime atrocities, holding meaning around human rights and peace. A standing guided program links this site with the nearby Statue of Peace for Japanese Military 'Comfort Women' along a Namsan trail connecting the two, offering visitors a chance to properly understand the 'comfort women' issue and, with a trained guide, take part in age-appropriate activities and discussions on human rights and peace.

명락사-2761662.name: Myeongnaksa Temple
명락사-2761662.description: Myeongnaksa, in Cheongnyong-dong, Gwanak-gu, sits in a commercial district at the edge of the Gwanaksan ridge. For more than 40 years it has focused its outreach on southwestern Seoul and on multicultural families in the area. It has an active youth group and holds regular dharma services every Saturday at 8:30pm. It's located about midway between Bongcheon Station and Seoul National University Station (Line 2).

관음사국기봉-2779550.name: Gwaneumsa Gukgi-bong Peak
관음사국기봉-2779550.description: Gwanaksan rises south of the Han River, straddling the border between Sillim-dong in Gwanak-gu and Anyang and Gwacheon in Gyeonggi-do. Its rocky summit, said to resemble a person wearing a traditional gat hat, gave the mountain its name ('crown-hat mountain'). Easily reached by public transit and known for its imposing rocky ridgeline, it's a perennial favorite among hikers. Among its routes, the path past Gwaneumsa — a temple founded in the Unified Silla period — up to Gukgi-bong ('national flag peak') is known as a short, intense way to experience Gwanaksan's charm. The trail has plenty of rock and some steep sections, but the summit's spectacular view makes the effort worthwhile, with a rest area at a spot named an outstanding scenic viewpoint. Most adults can complete the round trip in about 2 hours.

효민공-이경직-묘역-126914.name: Tomb of Yi Gyeong-jik (Hyomingong)
효민공-이경직-묘역-126914.description: A sindobi is a stele recording the lifetime achievements of a king or high official, erected southeast of their tomb; this one honors Yi Gyeong-jik, a mid-Joseon scholar-official. A student of Yi Hang-bok and Kim Jang-saeng, Yi Gyeong-jik began his official career at the Office of Special Advisers under King Seonjo, later serving as governor of Ganghwa, and held a series of posts including royal secretary and minister of taxation until his death from illness. In 1617, he traveled to Japan as a delegation official, and in 1624, when the Yi Gwal rebellion broke out, he distinguished himself as governor of Jeolla province; during the First Manchu Invasion of 1627, as vice minister of war, he negotiated peace terms with the Qing envoys. The stele, set on a square base with a roof stone, follows the conventions of its era. Erected in 1668, its inscription was composed by Kim Ryu and written by Yi Gyeong-jik's third son. Of historical and academic value, the tomb site is an important resource for studying Joseon-era tomb customs. (Source: Korea Heritage Service)

구강사-2761661.name: Gugangsa Temple
구강사-2761661.description: Gugangsa, in Cheonho-dong, Gangdong-gu, is a temple of the Cheontae Order of Korean Buddhism serving as a hub for Cheontae teaching and outreach in eastern Seoul. Housed in a standalone 5-story building, its main hall sits on the 5th floor, with the Geumgang Kindergarten on the 3rd. Regular dharma services are held at 11am on the fourth Sunday of each month, and it also runs a Buddhist college.

청담근린공원-127269.name: Cheongdam Neighborhood Park
청담근린공원-127269.description: Cheongdam Neighborhood Park is a small, cozy park in the thoroughly urban Cheongdam-dong. Unlike most neighborhood parks built on flat ground, it preserves the original shape of its hillside, blending walking paths and rest areas naturally into the terrain. Following the low trail uphill leads to a playground with basic exercise equipment, often busy with people exercising in the morning. The park has sports facilities, a badminton court, a basketball court, walking paths, a pavilion, a small stream, and a mineral spring, and its grounds also house a youth center and a police substation. With its dense stands of trees, Cheongdam Neighborhood Park offers a rare pocket of clean air in the city.

신사공원-2752552.name: Sinsa Park
신사공원-2752552.description: Sinsa Park, a neighborhood park in Apgujeong-dong, Gangnam-gu, sits between Garosugil and the Jamwon district of Hangang Citizens' Park, drawing many visitors. Designated a park in July 1977, it opened in May 1985, with a variety of trees, rest facilities, and exercise equipment, and underwent a remodel in 2007. Though not large, it has a walking path running between two spacious plazas at either end, plus exercise equipment, drinking fountains, a pavilion, and benches, making it a good spot for both exercise and rest — its decomposed-granite gateball court is especially popular with older visitors.

역삼동성당-2733864.name: Yeoksam-dong Catholic Church
역삼동성당-2733864.description: As the Catholic community in Gangnam grew, this parish was established on August 1, 1984, carved from part of the territories of Daechi-dong and Yangjae-dong parishes. Its first priest was Fr. Kim Gu-hee, with St. Choi Kyung-hwan as patron saint; the parish used a temporary building while preparing to build a permanent church. Construction began on December 25, 1992, on donated land, and five years later the parish completed a vast, beautiful church spanning 3,960 pyeong, dedicated by Cardinal Kim Su-hwan on September 21, 1997.

은곡마을공원-2751890.name: Eungok Village Park
은곡마을공원-2751890.description: This neighborhood park, in the natural village of Eungok in Segok-dong, Gangnam-gu, has a children's play area, a range of exercise equipment, and a fountain. The village name Eungok comes from an older name, Makeun-gol, said to derive from trees planted to block off the village entrance. Entering the park, a variety of trees and flowers greet visitors — cherry blossoms in full bloom in spring, cool shade in summer, and vivid autumn foliage. It's a great spot for photos, and was also a filming location for a tvN drama.

우이령-숲속문화마을-구-우이동-먹거리마을-126495.name: Uiryeong Forest Culture Village (formerly Uidong Food Village)
우이령-숲속문화마을-구-우이동-먹거리마을-126495.description: Set at the foot of Bukhansan, Uiryeong Forest Culture Village preserves both a beautiful natural setting and old-fashioned charm. Covering the area around Uidong and Uidong Park Resort, it's home to a dense cluster of restaurants. The roughly 1.2km stretch from the Bukhansan Ui terminal of the Ui Sinseol light rail line toward the Uiryeong-gil trail makes up this village (formerly known as Uidong Food Village). Since the Ui Sinseol line opened, improved access has brought more visitors. Nearby are resort condominiums, the Uidong Family Campground, and Bukhansan's Insubong Peak, blending facilities and natural scenery.

천왕근린공원-2591838.name: Cheonwang Neighborhood Park
천왕근린공원-2591838.description: Cheonwang Neighborhood Park, in Cheonwang-dong, Guro-gu, has a pond that puts on a beautiful show when its lotus flowers bloom. In summer, it opens a free water-play area, great for visiting with children. Part of the park's green space is also set aside as a camping site where visitors can bring mats or tents, though cooking and overnight camping aren't allowed — check the district office website for details. It's a healing pocket of the city, good for families to relax together in different ways.

150년-수령-느티나무-2611482.name: 150-Year-Old Zelkova Tree
150년-수령-느티나무-2611482.description: This 150-year-old zelkova tree stands as proof that a village existed here even before the area became a large residential complex. Planted about 150 years ago by a resident of the old village of Namal (the historic name for Mok 4-dong), the tree has survived to the present — it was nearly killed by bombing during the Korean War but sprouted new shoots and pulled through, overcoming various hardships to reach its current form. Local tradition holds that anyone who makes a wish here will see it come true, and that harming the tree brings a curse and great misfortune — earning it a place as the village's living guardian spirit. Residents of Mok 4-dong continue to care for and protect the tree together.

안양천-사계절-테마원-2612095.name: Anyangcheon Four Seasons Theme Garden
안양천-사계절-테마원-2612095.description: This themed garden sits within Anyangcheon Eco Park, which stretches along the Anyangcheon Stream. With plants enough to evoke a small European arboretum, the garden paints the park in vivid color. Its rose garden, ornamental-grass garden, and herb garden each show off seasonal blooms at their peak. Free to enter and dotted with photo spots, it's a healing space in the city where people and nature meet. In summer, a children's water-play area opens beside the rose garden, turning it into a themed space the whole family can enjoy. It's 750m from Exit 2 of Dorimcheon Station (Line 2).

클럽케이서울-2782132.name: Club K Seoul
클럽케이서울-2782132.description: Built around meaningful rest and balanced wellness, Club K Seoul is an urban complex combining fitness, golf, Pilates, community programs, and a nutrition center. Its golf center has full GDR simulator bays, vision screen rooms, and lesson bays, with dedicated pro lessons available anytime. The community center hosts running crews, monthly golf meetups, wine classes, and other cultural activities, while the nutrition center offers sports-nutrition-based meals and general food and beverage service.

법안정사-2751294.name: Beoban-jeongsa Temple
법안정사-2751294.description: This large temple in Mok-dong, Yangcheon-gu, was built in 1989 on religious land within a Mokdong apartment complex to mark the 100th anniversary of Korea-France diplomatic relations, giving it a modern, urban design. Easily reached by public transit given its city location, it spans four floors — a scale and grandeur unusual for a modern-built temple.

일상비일상의틈-2994661.name: Special (LG U+ Culture Space)
일상비일상의틈-2994661.description: Officially named '일상비일상의틈' ('the space between the ordinary and the extraordinary'), this complex was built by LG U+ in September 2020 as a cultural hub for younger generations. Rather than a typical carrier store with products on shelves, it's a space built to convey brand values, offering collaborative pop-ups and experiences with a range of partner brands, linking online and offline experience through in-space collaborations and app-based livestreams and events. The building runs from basement level to the 5th floor plus a rooftop, each floor with its own concept. The basement holds LG U+'s next-generation telecom store, offering plan consultations alongside merchandise from its mascot character Colley. The 1st floor hosts celebrity and brand pop-up stores tailored to younger tastes; the 2nd floor is filled with cute keyring displays; the 3rd floor showcases quirky products and character goods brought over from Japan's Tsutaya Electrics Plus; the 4th floor is a lounge space, sometimes hosting small pop-ups and sometimes open simply as a rest area; and the 5th floor carries over 500 kinds of K-pop albums and merchandise, with the breezy rooftop offering a relaxed escape rarely found elsewhere in the city.

신석구-사택-터-2373333.name: Site of Shin Seok-gu's Residence
신석구-사택-터-2373333.description: This is where Shin Seok-gu, one of the 33 national representatives, lived during the March 1st Movement of 1919. Shin (1875–1950) converted to Christianity in 1907, was baptized the following year, and studied theology at Hyupsung Theological College. After working as an evangelist in Gyeonggi and Gangwon provinces, he was ordained a minister in 1917. While serving as head pastor of Supyogyo Church in Seoul from November 1918, he was persuaded to join the 33 national representatives of the March 1st Movement. On March 1, 1919, he read the Declaration of Independence at Taehwagwan, was arrested by Japanese police, and served two years and eight months in prison. In July 1938, he was imprisoned again for resisting forced Shinto shrine worship, and in May 1945 he was arrested for refusing to hold Japanese-mandated victory prayers and raise the Japanese flag, remaining imprisoned until liberation. On April 19, 1949, he was arrested as the alleged leader of an anti-communist secret organization in Jinnampo and imprisoned at Pyongyang Prison, where he was killed during the Korean War.

이충순-자결-터-2373364.name: Site of Yi Chung-sun's Self-Sacrifice
이충순-자결-터-2373364.description: This is where Yi Chung-sun took his own life while confronting Japanese forces, dying for his country. A native of Hongseong, South Chungcheong, Yi entered military service and was commissioned an army sub-lieutenant in 1902. In 1905 he organized a military officers' association and led a national-salvation movement. After the 1907 treaty forced the disbandment of the Korean army, the Seoul garrison was abruptly disbanded on August 1; Yi refused to comply and engaged Japanese forces already deployed in the capital, sustaining serious wounds. Facing capture, he took his own life rather than be taken prisoner. The government posthumously awarded him the Order of Merit for National Foundation, Patriots' Medal, in 1990. A marker stone erected by the city of Seoul stands in the flower bed in front of the JoongAng Ilbo building.

청계광장-2765510.name: Cheonggye Plaza
청계광장-2765510.description: Cheonggye Plaza, at the start of Cheonggyecheon Stream on Sejong-ro in Jung-gu, is a nature-friendly public square. With plenty to see and easy access, it's one of Seoul's signature tourist spots for both residents and international visitors. It features a tri-color candle fountain and a two-tier waterfall that drops 4m, flanked by 'Palseokdam,' a display of eight stones gathered from each of Korea's provinces. At night, the plaza's lighting and water combine for a magical scene that draws crowds even after dark. A 1:100 scale model of the entire Cheonggyecheon course is also on display, and the plaza hosts a range of citizen cultural events and festivals year-round.

천호공원-127376.name: Cheonho Park
천호공원-127376.description: Cheonho Park, in Cheonho-dong, Gangdong-gu, was built in June 1998 on land the city purchased from the former site of the Pilot pen factory. The park is home to the Gangdong District Haegong Library, opened in 2008, named after the pen name of independence activist Sin Ik-hui (Haegong), who was born nearby. As a hub of leisure activity for local residents, it also has an outdoor stage, a pond, and a basketball court, and is especially beautiful each spring when its azaleas bloom in full.

보문사-서울-316104.name: Bomunsa Temple (Seoul)
보문사-서울-316104.description: Bomunsa, registered as one of Seoul's traditional temples, is in Bomun-dong, Seongbuk-gu, founded in 1115 (Goryeo's King Yejong's 10th year) by State Preceptor Damjin. Notably, a text by the scholar-monk Toegyeong Kwon Sang-no (1879–1965) records it as a nunnery dating back centuries, where Buddhist nuns resided and prayed for the nation's peace and the royal family's prosperity. The gap in the historical record went undocumented until 2017, when a complete ridge-beam inscription was discovered during renovation of the Geungnakbojeon hall, confirming the temple's history. The Geungnakbojeon hall in its present form was first rebuilt in 1747 (King Yeongjo's 23rd year), with further renovations in 1824 and 1865. The discovery of the ridge-beam inscription confirmed that Bomunsa has continuously housed practicing nuns since the 1800s, and shows it was a royally sponsored temple, receiving donations ranging from royal consorts and court ladies to the aristocracy and commoners. Bomunsa preserves royal-donated ceremonial items along with a late-Joseon Buddhist painting set (Seoul Tangible Cultural Heritage) and an early-Joseon copy of the Lotus Sutra (a nationally designated cultural heritage), along with numerous other tangible and intangible cultural assets.

북악산-숙정문-129500.name: Sukjeongmun Gate, Bugaksan
북악산-숙정문-129500.description: Sukjeongmun is one of the four great gates of Seoul's city wall, serving as the northern gate of Hanyangdoseong. Originally named Sukcheongmun, it was later renamed Sukjeongmun. It's the only surviving city gate whose wall connects on both sides. Its gate tower was rebuilt in 1976. Long closed to the public for Blue House security, it reopened in April 2006 along with a 0.5km stretch of the western wall and a 0.6km approach road to the north. It was designated Historic Site No. 10 in 1963 as part of Seoul's Hanyangdoseong wall.

응봉체육공원-2757822.name: Eungbong Sports Park
응봉체육공원-2757822.description: This sports park, at the foot of Eungbongsan along Jungnangcheon Stream in Seongdong-gu, has facilities for soccer, tennis, baseball, and other sports. Its artificial-turf soccer field along the open riverside and its brightly renovated basketball court are especially popular, drawing growing numbers of sports-minded residents. Recent renovations added safety fencing and padding for safer basketball play. Booking the soccer field, futsal field, or jokgu court requires reserving through the Seongdong-gu Urban Management Corporation website.

플로팅아일랜드-2745583.name: Floating Island
플로팅아일랜드-2745583.description: Floating Island, part of Sebitseom, the Han River's landmark island complex, has hosted a range of international events and corporate galas since 2014 — from summits and cultural festivals to international exhibitions and fashion shows — becoming one of Seoul's signature event venues, set against its beautiful island backdrop. More than just a banquet hall, it's a place to feel the blend of creativity and cultural richness.

관문사-서울-776082.name: Gwanmunsa Temple (Seoul)
관문사-서울-776082.description: Gwanmunsa, at the foot of Umyeonsan in Seoul, is a cradle and outreach hub of the Cheontae Order in the greater capital region, set amid the natural beauty of Cheonggyesan, Umyeonsan, and Yangjaecheon Stream. Master Uicheon brought the Cheontae school — founded in China around the 6th century by Tiantai Zhiyi — to Korea in order to unify and reform the fractured Buddhism of his time in Goryeo. Gwanmunsa blends modern and traditional Buddhist architectural styles, and its state-of-the-art facilities host a range of domestic and international cultural, academic, and religious events. Through a variety of programs, it helps people worn down by modern life set down their burdens and find peace of mind.

광흥당-2500218.name: Gwangheungdang
광흥당-2500218.description: Set at the foot of Wausan in Mapo, beside the Shrine of King Gongmin, Gwangheungdang is a hanok cultural space running a variety of programs to highlight the value of traditional culture. It excavates and displays local historical records of Mapo-gu and runs educational programs for young people. On Jeongwol Daeboreum (the first full moon of the lunar year), it holds traditional pre-modern folk games and customs — daeboreum games, kite-flying, jishin-balgi (earth-spirit stomping), stone fights, and archery contests. On Coming-of-Age Day it holds a traditional coming-of-age ceremony, and a range of events promote traditional Korean court music, including a gugak festival and Mapo Gugak Ullim performances. It has also developed the annual King Gongmin Shrine Rite into a district-wide unity festival, and runs paid cultural classes in janggu drumming, pansori singing, and gukseondo.

동작청소년센터-2764187.name: Dongjak Youth Center
동작청소년센터-2764187.description: This space in Sangdo-dong, Dongjak-gu, gives young people a stage and rehearsal space for performances, band practice, dance practice, and other music activities. Opened in 2005, it runs guitar and drum lesson programs alongside self-expression, speech, and creative art programs, with rooms available for free rental and space for study groups and small gatherings. Recognized as a model youth training facility, it also opened a Sindaebang-dong Youth Art Hub in November 2020, which continues to operate today.

금천예술공장-2553946.name: Geumcheon Art Factory
금천예술공장-2553946.description: Geumcheon Art Factory is an international artist residency for visual art, created in 2009 by remodeling a former printing factory. It offers Korean and international artists 24-hour-access creative studios, building connections between the public and artists through programs like open studios and the Da Vinci Creative Festival. It has 19 creative studios, a warehouse building for large-scale work, an exhibition space (PS333), and workshop rooms.

구로기계공구단지-2591803.name: Guro Machine Tools Complex
구로기계공구단지-2591803.description: The Guro Machine Tools Complex, in Guro-gu, is a dense cluster of machine-tool and industrial-supply wholesalers. Korea's first organized industrial-supply distribution complex, it houses around 50,000 types of industrial products sorted by block, building, and category, with roughly 1,700 businesses operating across 33 buildings arranged in 4 blocks — Block A for rubber products, Block B for electrical supplies, Block C for machine tools, and Block D for steel and non-ferrous metals. Buildings within each block are connected by bridges for easy movement between them. Machine and tool shops also cluster around the complex, and its location near Guro Station and the Seobu Expressway gives it excellent transit access — the complex sits right in front of Guro Station (Line 1).

음식문화특화거리-깔깔거리-2591826.name: Food Culture Street (Kkalkkal-geori)
음식문화특화거리-깔깔거리-2591826.description: This restaurant street formed near Guro Digital Complex Station (Line 2), home to a cluster of Guro-gu's better restaurants leading the way in clean, streamlined dining that cuts down on food waste. The name 'Kkalkkal-geori' ('spotless street') reflects its idea: restaurants serve food cleanly, and diners finish their meals without leaving food behind. Certified 'Kkalkkal' member restaurants give a 2% discount (as loyalty points) to customers who finish their plates, and offer takeout containers for any leftovers, part of a broader push to improve dining culture. The street has several well-known restaurants and draws many office workers from the surrounding area, getting especially busy during the evening rush.

류순정-류홍-부자-묘역-2591813.name: Tombs of Ryu Sun-jeong and Ryu Hong (Father and Son)
류순정-류홍-부자-묘역-2591813.description: This is the burial ground of early-Joseon scholar-official Ryu Sun-jeong (1459–1512) and his son, military official Ryu Hong (1483–1551). Both father and son were honored as meritorious subjects, and this tomb complex was built in the 16th century. It's the only known two-generation father-son meritorious-subject tomb site in the Seoul area today, and its stone furnishings and layout offer valuable insight into the customs and conventions of Joseon-era meritorious-subject tomb design. Ryu Sun-jeong's tomb is a stacked joint burial with his wife — his above, and that of his wife, of the Andong Gwon clan, below. To the left of the couple's tomb stands a memorial stele erected in 1567 honoring Ryu Sun-jeong's life and achievements. About 150m southwest of Ryu Sun-jeong's tomb, on a hill, lies the burial ground of his son Ryu Hong and later descendants.

육영재단-어린이회관-2743740.name: Yugyeong Foundation Children's Hall
육영재단-어린이회관-2743740.description: The Children's Hall is a welfare center established by the Yugyeong Foundation to improve children's welfare and childcare environments. It houses a range of educational, exhibition, cultural, and sports facilities for children, split between a 10,000㎡ science hall (1 basement, 4 above-ground floors) and a 6,500㎡ culture hall (2 floors), hosting a variety of children's events and hands-on exhibitions. Its indoor playground is free to use, and it opens a sledding rink in winter. Originally established on Namsan in 1970, it moved to its current location in 1975.

맥아더-사령관-한강방어선-시찰지-2373320.name: Site of General MacArthur's Inspection of the Han River Defense Line
맥아더-사령관-한강방어선-시찰지-2373320.description: This is where General MacArthur inspected the Han River defense line shortly after North Korea's invasion, before the U.S. decision to enter the war. Arriving at Suwon Airfield on June 29, 1950, the Far East Command's General MacArthur received a briefing on the situation, then decided to see the front lines for himself, traveling via Siheung to a hill beside the Dongyang Brewery factory in Yeongdeungpo (now Yeongdeungpo Park), facing the Han River front, to observe the battle. There, a soldier defending a position on the hill reportedly told him, 'I'll hold this position until my superior orders me to withdraw' — a statement said to have deeply moved MacArthur. This inspection became an important factor in the U.S. decision to enter the Korean War.

숭인근린공원-1604733.name: Sungin Neighborhood Park
숭인근린공원-1604733.description: Sungin Neighborhood Park, on Dongmangsan in Sungin-dong, Jongno-gu, is also known as Dongmangsan Park. Opened in 1980, this urban park was built to give residents a space for rest, walks, and light exercise, covering 45,615㎡ of nature-friendly space. It has a pavilion, fitness equipment, a management office, and restrooms. The park's peak, Dongmangbong, takes its name from the story of Queen Jeongsun, wife of the deposed King Danjong: after Danjong was exiled to Yeongwol, she built the thatched hermitage Jeongeobwon here and gazed east toward Yeongwol, longing for him — giving the peak its name ('peak of gazing east'). A memorial rite honoring Queen Jeongsun was held in this park in April 2008.

우당-이회영-선생-흉상-2373360.name: Bust of Yi Hoe-yeong (Udang)
우당-이회영-선생-흉상-2373360.description: This bust honors Yi Hoe-yeong, a patriot who devoted himself to Korea's independence. Born the fourth son of Minister of Personnel Yi Yu-seung, Yi led a movement in 1905 to block and nullify the plot behind the Eulsa Treaty, and urged King Gojong to send secret envoys to the Hague Peace Conference. In 1910, following Japan's annexation of Korea, he and all five of his brothers — some 50 family members in total — liquidated their entire fortune and went into exile. In Manchuria, he opened the Sinheung Institute, forerunner of the Sinheung Military Academy, relocating to Hapnihe in 1912 to begin full military-officer training. Until its closure in 1920, the Sinheung academy trained around 3,500 independence-army officers and led the war for independence, later becoming a foundation for the Korean Liberation Army. When the Provisional Government was established in Shanghai, he served as a council member, and later supported the anarchist movement and the Righteous Brotherhood organization while forming the Anti-Japanese National Salvation League, directing militant resistance through its Black Terror unit. While secretly traveling to help unify Chinese and Korean resistance forces against Japan, he was arrested in Dalian and transferred to Lushun Prison, where he died from brutal torture and starvation at age 66. The bust, built by a memorial foundation to honor his achievements, stands in front of the Seoul YWCA, alongside a marker for the former home of Yi Hoe-yeong and his brother Yi Si-yeong.

윤동주시인의언덕-2787181.name: Yun Dong-ju Poet's Hill
윤동주시인의언덕-2787181.description: This hill honoring Yun Dong-ju (1917–1945), the resistance poet most beloved by Koreans during the Japanese colonial era, sits within Cheongwun Park on the slopes of Inwangsan in Cheongun-dong, Jongno-gu. While attending Yonhui College in 1941, Yun boarded at the home of his junior, novelist Kim Song, in Nusang-dong, Jongno-gu; during this time he walked the neighborhoods of Cheongun-dong and Nusang-dong, refining his thoughts and writing some of his best-known poems, including 'Counting Stars at Night,' 'Foreword,' and 'Self-Portrait' — the reason Poet's Hill was built here in Cheongun-dong. It's easy to imagine him, in the evenings, watching the Seoul sunset from near his boarding house and drawing on the ache of his country's dark reality for inspiration. The hill today has a stone inscribed with his poem 'Foreword,' ten pine trees donated by singer Lee Seung-hwan and his fans, and stone steps engraved with his poetry to admire while climbing. The pine known as the 'Yun Dong-ju Pine' is a well-known solo destination for watching the sunset and reflecting quietly. Poet's Hill connects to the Yun Dong-ju Literature Museum, built in July 2012 by remodeling a decommissioned water pumping station, with Changuimun Gate just across the way.

창경궁-홍화문-1605009.name: Honghwamun Gate, Changgyeonggung Palace
창경궁-홍화문-1605009.description: Honghwamun is the main gate of Changgyeonggung Palace; 'honghwa' means 'to spread virtue' — to govern with virtue so as to inspire and transform the people far and wide. Built when Changgyeonggung was first constructed, it burned down during the Japanese invasions of the 1590s and was rebuilt in 1616 (King Gwanghaegun's 8th year). While Donhwamun, the main gate of the neighboring Changdeokgung, has a 5-bay front, Honghwamun was built smaller, with just 3 bays. Honghwamun was also where the king met directly with the people: in 1750, before implementing the Equal Service Tax Law, King Yeongjo came here to hear the views of both aristocrats and commoners on the proposed tax reform. In 1795, King Jeongjo distributed rice to the poor outside Honghwamun to mark the 60th birthday of his mother, Lady Hyegyeong. Honghwamun was designated a Korean Treasure in 1963. It's a two-story, 3-bay by 2-bay building notably facing east, with a hip roof forming a trapezoid when viewed from the front. Its bracket sets use the dense dapo style found both above the columns and between them. The lower level has double doors between each set of columns for passage, while the upper level has a wooden floor with small hinged panels that can be opened and closed. The carved ornaments at either end of the roof ridge add to the building's dignified presence.

대림어린이공원-2753103.name: Daerim Children's Park
대림어린이공원-2753103.description: This park in Daerim-dong, Yeongdeungpo-gu, has children's play facilities, a range of exercise equipment, and rest space. A hub for cultural and leisure activity, it draws many local residents and also hosts community-linked programs and neighborhood festivals as a space for connection and unity. Its well-maintained walking paths make it good for a family outing, and its artificial-turf area offers a safe place to exercise. An underground public parking lot makes it convenient to visit.

오목공원-2611735.name: Omok Park
오목공원-2611735.description: Omok Park, a neighborhood park in Mok-dong near the Yangcheon-gu Office, opened in 1989. Its name comes from 'Omongnae,' meaning 'a hollowed, valley-like stream.' Surrounded by broadcast stations, high-rise office buildings, and apartments, it draws many office workers for a lunchtime stroll or break. The Omok Museum of Art inside the park is worth a quick look, alongside a playground, basketball court, fountain, and rest areas — a meaningful example of an open, ecology-minded park in the city.

올림픽대교-250131.name: Olympic Bridge
올림픽대교-250131.description: Olympic Bridge, connecting Guui-dong in Gwangjin-gu with Pungnap-dong in Songpa-gu, was built to permanently commemorate the 24th Olympic Games — a milestone in Korea's globalization — and to manage traffic around the Olympic venues. It's Korea's first concrete cable-stayed bridge, spanning 1.5km. Its four 88m-tall pylons, referencing the '88 Seoul Olympics, are shaped like the Olympic cauldron; the four pylons represent the four cycles of year, month, day, and hour, as well as the four seasons and four directions, while its 24 cables represent the 24th Olympiad. Alongside the bridge's construction, a road park was built on the southern floodplain, along with a 6m-diameter Olympic rings sculpture and 24 commemorative sculptures symbolizing global unity. Chosen through a public design competition as Korea's first concrete cable-stayed bridge, Olympic Bridge holds a notable place in the history of Korean bridge engineering.

호전다실-2969267.name: Hojeon Tea House
호전다실-2969267.description: Since 2012, Hojeon Tea House has imported, distributed, and taught about teas from around the world. It sources teas from renowned tea-producing regions including China, Japan, Taiwan, India, and Sri Lanka, introducing high-quality teas both in person and online. It has opened a tasting space for traditional (classic) teas in Seochon, next to Gyeongbokgung Palace. A basic tasting includes 3–4 teas and runs about an hour; bookings are taken through Naver Reservations. Beyond tastings, it also runs tea-related classes, working to popularize tea culture and promote a tea culture suited to today's changing tastes.

k-컬처-스크린-대한민국역사박물관-2992823.name: K-Culture Screen (National Museum of Korean Contemporary History)
k-컬처-스크린-대한민국역사박물관-2992823.description: K-Culture Square is a space built to showcase Korea's rich cultural resources through cutting-edge convergent media, including 3D media art, displayed around Gwanghwamun, offering a cultural experience for visitors from Korea and abroad. K-Culture Screen — a public media canvas and digital signage sharing Korea's cultural, artistic, and technological resources with everyone — brings the history, moments, and stories of Gwanghwamun to life through varied content along this busy thoroughfare. Playful, imaginative, three-dimensional media art combined with audience participation completes the true meaning of a public media canvas. There are three K-Culture Screen locations: the National Museum of Korean Contemporary History, the Seoul Metro Art Museum at Gyeongbokgung Station, and the Sejong Center for the Performing Arts. At the National Museum of Korean Contemporary History, the screen is installed at the curved corner of the building's L-shaped exterior wall, showing a range of media-art content daily from 6am to 10pm, looping on an hourly cycle so visitors can enjoy K-Culture media art at any time of day. The museum's screen currently presents 16 themed pieces, each offering content far more intriguing than its title alone suggests. The anamorphic 3D effect is most striking when viewed from the lawn area of Gwanghwamun Square.

녹번서공원-3453040.name: Nokbeonseo Park
녹번서공원-3453040.description: Nokbeonseo Park, in Nokbeon-dong, Eunpyeong-gu, is a nature-friendly park where a variety of plants and trees grow naturally. Flowers and vivid foliage make it especially pleasant in spring and autumn, and it has a nature-study area, exercise equipment, a library, and other facilities.

왕십리맛골목-3444605.name: Wangsimni Food Alley
왕십리맛골목-3444605.description: Wangsimni Food Alley, near Wangsimni Station in Seongdong-gu, is a dense cluster of restaurants serving Korean, Chinese, Japanese, and other cuisines at reasonable prices. Well connected by transit and full of lively energy, it's a popular meeting spot for office workers and students alike.

신도림테크노근린공원-3447960.name: Sindorim Techno Neighborhood Park
신도림테크노근린공원-3447960.description: This park gives local residents an important space for rest and leisure. Located near Sindorim Station, it's easily accessible and blends well with the surrounding residential and commercial areas. With a children's playground and rest areas, it's well suited to family visits.

길음역롯데캐슬트윈골드상가-3451976.name: Gireum Station Lotte Castle Twin Gold Commercial Complex
길음역롯데캐슬트윈골드상가-3451976.description: This commercial complex houses a range of shops, anchored by a large aquarium, cafes, restaurants, a clinic, and convenience stores. Its enclosed, indoor-facing layout is designed to maximize the visual appeal of the shopping arcade.

2025-서울-카페-베이커리페어-3432447.name: 2025 Seoul Cafe & Bakery Fair
2025-서울-카페-베이커리페어-3432447.description: The Cafe & Bakery Fair is a trade show for cafe owners and buyers, showcasing everything needed to run a cafe — coffee beans, roasting machines, equipment, and interior decor. Exhibitors are mostly coffee-machine and equipment vendors and bean suppliers, and visitors can try out and purchase products on display. It's a useful one-stop look at the latest cafe trends for anyone preparing to open a cafe or already working in the industry, with barista and dessert competitions and other side events adding to the draw. New competitions and programs are added each year, so it's worth checking the schedule before visiting.

차민성형외과의원-3591228.name: Chamin Plastic Surgery Clinic
차민성형외과의원-3591228.description: Chamin Plastic Surgery specializes in a range of cosmetic and dermatological procedures, from rhinoplasty revision and nose jobs to facelifts and mini-lifts, forehead surgery, double-chin treatment, and eye surgery, alongside fillers, Botox, and skin boosters. Every step involves direct 1:1 consultation and treatment with specialists in each field, across a structured clinical setup with a procedure center on the 4th floor, a surgery center on the 5th, and a consultation center on the 6th. The Chamin Medical Center also offers internal-medicine care from a gastroenterology specialist, including endoscopy, ultrasound, health checkups, and fecal microbiota transplantation.

연세굿데이치과의원-양재점-3591214.name: Yonsei Good Day Dental Clinic, Yangjae Branch
연세굿데이치과의원-양재점-3591214.description: Yonsei Good Day Dental Clinic offers English-language care, with specialists from university hospitals with 10+ years of experience covering each dental specialty. It offers a range of treatment services including partner-hotel arrangements and tax refund assistance, and both painless local anesthesia and sleep anesthesia for a more comfortable dental experience.

동십자각-1603677.name: Dongsipjagak (Watchtower)
동십자각-1603677.description: Dongsipjagak is a watchtower where Gyeongbokgung's outer wall, connected to Gwanghwamun, turns toward Geonchunmun Gate. Its stone base is thought to date from the early Joseon period, while the tower itself is believed to have been built during the era of the Heungseon Daewongun. Though modest in scale, its harmonious artistry makes it one of Gyeongbokgung's finer structures. Its square floor plan measures three bays on each side, with only a base rail and head rail framing the structure and no walls — fully open on all sides, with a bare earthen floor. Originally functioning as a watchtower at the southeastern corner of the palace wall, it became a freestanding roadside structure once the surrounding palace wall was demolished. A matching Seosipjagak once stood at the wall's western corner for the same purpose, but it no longer survives.

망원한강공원-1059638.name: Mangwon Hangang Park
망원한강공원-1059638.description: Mangwon Hangang Park, part of the Hangang Citizens' Park system that serves as Seoul's riverside retreat, sits on the river's north bank between Wonhyo Bridge and Seongsan Bridge, bordering Mapo-gu. Its floodplain has well-developed lawns and walking paths for rest, alongside exercise facilities and bike paths, making it a nice spot to unwind with friends or a partner. On the water, visitors can windsurf, water-ski, or ride motorboats, and nearby heritage sites like Mangwonjeong Pavilion and Jeoldusan Martyrs' Shrine round out the area, which also connects to the World Cup Stadium and Incheon International Airport.

노을공원-서울-2733971.name: Noeul Park (Seoul)
노을공원-서울-2733971.description: World Cup Park transformed the former Nanjido landfill into five themed parks — Seoul's flagship environmental and ecological park complex. Noeul Park, one of the five, has broad lawns, sculptural artwork, and observation decks offering a relaxed, spacious feel. It's especially known for its beautiful sunsets, drawing many visitors. The park also has a park-golf course, the Noeul Campground, a silkworm ecology zone, a firefly observation hall, and an urban farmers' garden — plenty of hands-on nature experiences to enjoy.

천축사-서울-482112.name: Cheonchuksa Temple (Seoul)
천축사-서울-482112.description: Cheonchuksa is a 1,300-year-old traditional temple directly administered by the Jogye Order (Nowon Traditional Temple No. 9-1). Founded in 673 (Unified Silla's King Munmu's 13th year) by State Preceptor Uisang, it was originally called Okcheonam for its remarkably clear spring water. During the Goryeo dynasty, the Indian monk Jigong reportedly told the monk Naong that the scenery here resembled Vulture Peak in ancient India. Later, in 1398, Joseon founder Yi Seong-gye prayed here for 100 days before founding Joseon; in his 7th year as king, he had the temple rebuilt and gave it the name Cheonchuksa, using characters for 'heaven' and 'India' — meaning 'a peaceful place where the Buddha always resides.' The royal family took a direct hand in Cheonchuksa's history: it was rebuilt by royal order in 1474, and Queen Dowager Munjeong gifted a lacquered royal dragon throne (National Treasure No. 366) that was used as its altar during King Myeongjong's reign. Rebuilt again in 1812 as a royal prayer temple, and renovated in 1959 and several times since, it retains its present form today. In 1964, Cheonchuksa built Korea's first Mumun-gwan (a 'no-door' meditation hall for solitary retreat), and remains a foundational site for pure ascetic practice in Korean Buddhism.

배봉산-2661483.name: Baebongsan
배봉산-2661483.description: Baebongsan is the only mountain-form park in eastern Dongdaemun-gu. Following the 1968 Blue House raid incident, a military base was installed at its summit in 1973, closing the peak to the public for 48 years; after the base relocated in 2015, the summit was restored as parkland, and Goguryeo-era defensive fortifications discovered there were designated Seoul Monument No. 42. A 4.5km loop trail, completed between 2013 and 2018, is accessible to people of all ages and abilities, with well-placed benches for resting along the way. A forest library, artificial climbing wall, X-Games facility, and ochre-clay path round out its cultural and sports amenities, making Baebongsan a signature spot in Dongdaemun-gu.

서울-석촌동-고분군-127466.name: Seokchon-dong Ancient Tombs, Seoul
서울-석촌동-고분군-127466.description: The Seokchon-dong tombs are a burial ground for kings and nobility from Baekje's Hanseong period. Colonial-era surveys reported around 300 tombs across the Seokchon-dong and Garak-dong area, but urban development has left only a western section intact today. Excavations since the 1970s have identified 7 large stone-mound tombs along with more than 30 pit-grave and jar-coffin burials; the largest, Tomb No. 3, is a three-tiered stone-mound tomb 50.8m wide and 4.5m tall, believed to be the tomb of King Geunchogo of Baekje. Surveys by the Hanseong Baekje Museum since 2015 have uncovered a structure of multiple tombs joined around a square base, along with Baekje pottery, gold ornaments, and cremated human remains. This construction style closely resembles Goguryeo-era tombs, making the site important archaeological evidence of the cultural ties between Baekje and Goguryeo.

창덕궁-낙선재-1604941.name: Nakseonjae, Changdeokgung Palace
창덕궁-낙선재-1604941.description: Nakseonjae sits on the border between Changdeokgung and Changgyeonggung palaces. King Heonjong, Joseon's 24th king, built Nakseonjae in 1847 on the site of Changgyeonggung's old Nakseondang, to welcome his consort Lady Gyeongbin, followed the next year by Seokbokheon and Sugangjae. Nakseonjae served as Heonjong's study and reception hall, Seokbokheon as Lady Gyeongbin's residence, and Sugangjae as the residence of the queen dowager at the time. Notably, this was also where the last members of the Korean imperial family — Empress Sunjeonghyo, Crown Princess Yi Bang-ja, and Princess Deokhye — lived and passed away. The buildings of Nakseonjae are left unpainted, in a deliberately understated style, with a rear garden built behind them. Between the buildings and the garden, small stepped stone terraces are planted with flowers, interspersed with elegant chimneys and ornamental rocks — a garden that blends royal dignity with the delicate charm distinctive to the women's quarters.

승가사-서울-126505.name: Seunggasa Temple (Seoul)
승가사-서울-126505.description: Seunggasa was built to honor the sacred achievements of Master Seungga, a Central Asian monk revered as an incarnation of Avalokiteshvara, by the monk Sutae of Silla's Nangjeoksa. A rock-carved statue of Master Seungga (Korean Treasure No. 1000) was enshrined in a niche carved into the cliff at a scenic spot on the south side of Samgaksan. A Goryeo-era rock-carved Buddha (Korean Treasure No. 215) on the cliff behind the temple, built with royal support, is a representative work of the early Goryeo period — kings are said to have come personally to pray before it during times of national crisis or disaster. The monk Hamheo is known to have attained enlightenment here during the early Joseon suppression of Buddhism, and in the late Joseon period the monk Seongwon is said to have attained enlightenment reciting the Great Compassion Dharani before the rock-carved Buddha — one of many eminent monks who trained here. Seunggasa fell into disrepair through the Japanese colonial era and the Korean War, but following the Buddhist reform movement, a succession of abbots from 1955 onward rebuilt the temple grounds, restoring its former reputation to the present day.

성동-ai-미래기술체험센터-2553911.name: Seongdong AI & Future Technology Experience Center
성동-ai-미래기술체험센터-2553911.description: This center lets visitors get hands-on with coding, robotics, drones, 3D printing, and VR/AR — core technologies of the 4th industrial revolution — building both integrative and creative thinking through direct experience and creation. Its hands-on, experience-first teaching approach makes future technology easy and fun to learn, aiming to nurture a new generation equipped not just with technical exposure but real future-ready skills. Programs are open to Seongdong-gu residents, students at local schools, and people working in the district.

안양암-서울-337413.name: Anyangam Hermitage (Seoul)
안양암-서울-337413.description: Anyangam, in Changsin-dong, Jongno-gu, is a Pure Land practice site founded in 1889 by Great Master Seongwol. Its grounds include the main hall along with a Myeongbujeon, Cheonobulbeoljeon (a hall of 1,500 Buddhas), Geumnyunjeon, Gwaneumjeon, a chanting hall, and a portrait hall, holding numerous Buddhist paintings and statues by leading painters of their era, including the monk-artist Gosandang Chukyeon.

서울교통공사-고덕차량사업소-2554065.name: Seoul Metro Godeok Rail Depot
서울교통공사-고덕차량사업소-2554065.description: Seoul Metro runs subway tour programs at each of its rail depots. Visitors tour the depot's equipment and facilities, learning about subway operations and safety procedures — how to open train doors in an emergency, how to use emergency phones and fire extinguishers, and a look inside the driver's cab and passenger car, with explanations of the various subway systems. Bookings must be made online at least 15 days before the desired visit date; tour dates and times vary by depot, so it's worth checking in advance. The Godeok depot offers tours only on the second and fourth Wednesday of each month, with a shuttle departing from in front of Exit 6 of Sangdongil Station at 9:40am for easy access.

홍파동-홍난파-가옥-945987.name: Hongpa-dong Hong Nan-pa House
홍파동-홍난파-가옥-945987.description: The Hongpa-dong Hong Nan-pa House is a brick, Western-style building built by a German missionary in the 1930s, later purchased and lived in by composer Hong Nan-pa. Preserving the character of 1930s Western-style homes in its original form, this house still carries traces of the composer's presence — it's where he wrote several of his best-known works, making it a valuable piece of modern cultural heritage. Hong Nan-pa is listed in Korea's official report on pro-Japanese collaborationist activity under the special law investigating such activity during the colonial period.

서울-우정총국-250358.name: Uijeongchongguk (Post Office Bureau), Seoul
서울-우정총국-250358.description: Uijeongchongguk was the government office that launched Korea's modern postal service, established on the recommendation of Hong Yeong-sik after his 1884 inspection tour of the new postal systems in Japan and the U.S. This building, remodeled in November 1884 from an outbuilding of the Jeoneuigam (royal medical office), served as its headquarters. At the celebration marking the bureau's opening on December 4 that year, Kim Ok-gyun, Park Yeong-hyo, Seo Gwang-beom, and Hong Yeong-sik launched the Gapsin Coup, an attempt to overthrow the Min family government and form a new one — during which all but the main building burned down, and postal operations were suspended. Postal service didn't resume until 1893, under the name Jeonu Chongguk, and continued under a series of successor agencies. After Japan seized control of Korea's communications in 1905, the building served various other purposes — a Chinese-language school, a night school, and the residence of the head of Gyeongseong Central Post Office. After liberation it became a private residence before becoming the Postal Service Memorial Hall in 1972. Renovations for its museum function mean it doesn't fully retain its original appearance, but the hall preserves stamps, documents, and artifacts from Korea's postal history.

세검정-터-126494.name: Site of Segeomjeong Pavilion
세검정-터-126494.description: Segeomjeong is said to have been built either as a rest stop for soldiers during the construction of Bukhansanseong Fortress under King Sukjong (r. 1674–1720), or as a pleasure pavilion built for King Yeonsangun (r. 1494–1506). Its name, meaning 'sword-washing pavilion,' comes from the tradition that during the 1623 coup that deposed King Gwanghaegun, conspirators met here to discuss the king's overthrow and sharpened their swords in preparation. The pavilion has a T-shaped floor plan and a hip-and-gable roof. Rebuilt in 1748 (King Yeongjo's 24th year), it burned down in 1941 and was restored to its historic appearance in 1977. A pavilion symbolizing peace, designed to harmonize with its natural surroundings, Segeomjeong offers a valuable glimpse into the essence of traditional Korean architecture.

어깨동무스토리움-3433029.name: Eogaedongmu Storium
어깨동무스토리움-3433029.description: Eogaedongmu Storium, in Sangam-dong, Mapo-gu, is a free indoor playground and hands-on experience space for children. It offers block play, slides, a ball pit, a mini train village, and other play facilities, along with a library just for young children, making it a great environment for families, including children under 36 months. Reservations are required, and both parking and admission are free.

어린이꿈공원-3442375.name: Children's Dream Park
어린이꿈공원-3442375.description: Children's Dream Park, in Haengdang-dong, Seongdong-gu, is a play park tailored for kids, with a range of facilities. A zip line, trampoline, sand play area, climbing wall, and water-play facilities give children a space to build creativity and adventurous spirit, making it a great destination for family visits.

풍납백제문화공원-3112160.name: Pungnap Baekje Culture Park
풍납백제문화공원-3112160.description: This park is a designated cultural heritage site.

한생연-생명과학박물관-2760301.name: Hansaengyeon Life Science Museum
한생연-생명과학박물관-2760301.description: The Hansaengyeon Life Science Museum, opened in April 2006, is Korea's first museum dedicated to life science, built to expand public science literacy and deepen specialized understanding of the field. It offers a hands-on, experience-centered way to explore life science, presenting experimental exhibits, activities, education programs, and events since its opening, with ambitions to be a life-science museum for both the city and the world. The museum aims not just to teach correct understanding of the human body, animals, plants, insects, and microorganisms, but to explore genetics and life processes scientifically using advanced lab equipment. Rather than a look-only museum, it continually develops hands-on content, and through ongoing collection and research works to offer increasingly accessible and specialized scientific exhibits as a space for lifelong learning.

이목화랑-129928.name: Imok Gallery
이목화랑-129928.description: Imok Gallery, opened in 1976, is one of Seoul's longest-running art exhibition spaces. Inside, visitors can view works in a quiet setting, with exhibition schedules and artist information posted on its website in advance. The gallery discovers, supports, and exhibits work by both established and emerging artists, selling art to help support artists' continued practice. Reflecting its long history, it hosts invitational exhibitions for veteran artists it has worked with for years, alongside shows bridging older and younger generations. To nurture talented young artists, it actively takes part in art fairs and exhibitions, helping introduce their work and supporting the growth of the broader art market.

갤러리에스피-130573.name: Gallery SP
갤러리에스피-130573.description: Gallery SP opened as an affiliated gallery of the Seoul Print Studio, initially focused on distributing its own self-produced prints. It moved to Cheongdam-dong in 1998, developing into a full-fledged gallery exhibiting, curating, and selling contemporary art across painting, sculpture, printmaking, ceramics, and other media. It focuses especially on introducing active mid-career and younger Korean artists, and has steadily expanded its reach by participating in international art fairs, helping raise the profile of Korean artists abroad. As part of its effort to broaden public engagement with art, it has also planned and produced prints through the Seoul Print Studio, distributing them widely through galleries in Korea and abroad.

나루아트센터-130699.name: Naru Art Center
나루아트센터-130699.description: Naru Art Center is a multi-purpose performing-arts space opening a new chapter in Korean arts and culture through a wide range of high-quality performances. It has a large hall hosting classical music, concerts, dance, theater, musicals, opera, and more, and a small, audience-friendly hall where the stage sits close to the seats for an intimate view of smaller productions. Its exhibition hall, for art lovers, uses interior walls and movable partitions to configure the space for different kinds of exhibitions. The Gwangjin Culture Foundation, launched in November 2015, runs Naru Art Center along with the Gwangjin Children's Theater, planning and operating performances, exhibitions, and education programs that combine artistic quality with broad appeal. Naru Art Center is about 250m from Exit 5 of Konkuk University Station (Line 2).

쾨닉-서울-2714028.name: König Seoul
쾨닉-서울-2714028.description: Over the past 20 years, König has become one of Germany's leading galleries for exciting contemporary art. From early on, it focused on artists working across disciplines or through conceptual approaches, many of whom have since become some of the most important names in contemporary art. The gallery now represents around 40 artists, active not only at König but at internationally renowned institutions around the world. By opening a gallery space in Seoul, König continues its commitment to introducing exceptional contemporary art to a global audience.

에스팩토리-2745602.name: S-Factory
에스팩토리-2745602.description: Seongsu-dong, where a factory district dating back to the 1980s now blends stylishly with distinctive spaces run by young artists, has become one of Seoul's newest destinations. Since being designated an 'urban regeneration pilot zone' in 2014, young cultural and artistic figures have gathered around its handmade-shoe street and factory district, and the small cafes, restaurants, and workshops they run have reshaped Seongsu-dong's streetscape. S-Factory now brings together studios, offices, restaurants, cafes, and pop-up stores in one space, hosting rentals, performances, exhibitions, and other cultural events.

서울특별시교육청-영등포평생학습관-130779.name: Yeongdeungpo Lifelong Learning Center, Seoul
서울특별시교육청-영등포평생학습관-130779.description: Run by the Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education, the Yeongdeungpo Lifelong Learning Center offers a range of lifelong-learning programs to improve residents' quality of life and support personal growth. It serves as a community lifelong-learning hub offering equal access to programs including literacy education, learning support for students who've left school, multicultural-family programs, and parent education. To support a culture of reading and serve as the community's knowledge and information hub, it holds around 230,000 items, prioritizing user convenience, and supports a range of cultural activities to help residents enjoy culture and enrich their lives.

서울특별시교육청-정독도서관-1019294.name: Jeongdok Library, Seoul
서울특별시교육청-정독도서관-1019294.description: Jeongdok Library, a Seoul public library, opened in January 1977 on the former site of Gyeonggi High School in Bukchon, Jongno-gu. It holds around 490,000 books and 16,300 non-book items, and its affiliated Seoul Education History Archive holds around 12,000 items documenting the city's educational history. Beyond book lending and reading-room access, it runs monthly author talks, photo exhibitions, and cultural programs like book clubs, puppet shows, concerts, and dance performances. In spring, the cherry blossoms around Jeongdok Library make it a rising date spot, and the nearby Samcheong Park hosts the Samcheong-dong Cherry Blossom Festival.

한전갤러리-130301.name: KEPCO Gallery
한전갤러리-130301.description: KEPCO Gallery is a cultural complex connecting people and communities through art. Its exhibitions span traditional and contemporary artistic value, offering a welcoming space for anyone to experience the depth and enjoyment of art. Its three exhibition halls, totaling 1,110㎡, contribute to the development of Korea's broader arts and culture scene.

역삼도서관-3423015.name: Yeoksam Library
역삼도서관-3423015.description: Yeoksam Library, a public library in Yeoksam-dong, Gangnam-gu, gives local residents access to a range of reading and cultural activities. Convenient transit access and a broad collection make it a draw for students, office workers, and families alike. Beyond book lending, it offers specialized and digital resources and runs programs supporting self-development and learning. Inside, it has a quiet reading area, a children's corner, a computer room, and a multimedia room, giving visitors a comfortable place to study or enjoy cultural activities, alongside lectures, cultural events, and book clubs that help foster community growth and connection.

서울특별시교육청-노원평생학습관-130761.name: Nowon Lifelong Learning Center, Seoul
서울특별시교육청-노원평생학습관-130761.description: Run by the Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education, the Nowon Lifelong Learning Center opened in 1990 as Junggye Library, serving as a public library before being reorganized as the Junggye Lifelong Learning Center in 1999 and renamed the Nowon Lifelong Learning Center in 2007. It connects and blends the community's human and material resources to support personal and community growth as a lifelong-learning hub — more than just gathering and providing information, it functions as a living community-of-practice hub that creates value. Its open reading room and range of lifelong-learning classrooms connect knowledge and information from around the world, making it a space where community-based lifelong learning begins. It has a periodicals room for book lending and lecture halls, seminar rooms, and a reading-discussion room supporting a range of learning activities.

신월음악도서관-2611675.name: Sinwol Music Library
신월음악도서관-2611675.description: Sinwol Music Library, established in February 2006 within the Sinwol 4-dong municipal complex, is a Yangcheon-gu public library built to bring reading culture and knowledge to local residents. Aiming to be a shared space for reading and culture for Yangcheon-gu residents, it offers a collection and programs reflecting residents' diverse interests, contributing to a healthy library culture.

서울특별시교육청-고덕평생학습관-130782.name: Godeok Lifelong Learning Center, Seoul
서울특별시교육청-고덕평생학습관-130782.description: Godeok Lifelong Learning Center, which opened in 1984 as Godeok Library, has served as a community hub improving quality of life through reading culture and a range of lifelong-education services, renamed the Godeok Lifelong Learning Center in 1999. It offers lifelong-learning classes for both adults and children in the community, spanning foreign-language courses, arts and culture classes, humanities courses, and IT skill-building, along with an annual autumn lifelong-learning festival and ongoing exhibitions. Facilities include a reference room, children's room, digital media room, lecture rooms, self-study rooms, a learning-device room, and a smart library, plus a dedicated calligraphy-practice space. The center holds around 180,000 items — general books and magazines on every topic in its reference room, and books and magazines for young children in its children's room. Its digital media room holds non-book media like DVDs and audiobooks alongside computers and laptops available for on-site use. It also runs vacation reading programs, age-targeted book clubs, and interlibrary loan services, among other reading-related offerings.

아트스페이스3-2993324.name: Art Space 3
아트스페이스3-2993324.description: Art Space 3 is a gallery introducing original, boundary-pushing contemporary Korean art. The number '3' in its name reflects its aim to balance and harmonize three groups: artists, viewers, and the gallery itself. Starting in Insa-dong before relocating to Seochon in 2018, it has held a series of abstract-art group exhibitions charting the current state of Korean contemporary art. Its main exhibition hall, with both white and bare-cement walls and ceiling heights varying between 4m and 8m, was designed to allow for playful, varied exhibition layouts. A split-level space connected to the main hall houses an archaeological exhibition room showing 16th-century Joseon-era residential remains, unearthed during the building's construction — a dedicated space for the residential relics and artifacts found on-site, spanning Joseon to the modern era. The result is a distinctive space where cutting-edge contemporary art coexists with historic cultural heritage.

동산방화랑-129903.name: Dongsanbang Gallery
동산방화랑-129903.description: Dongsanbang Gallery bridges traditional painting and contemporary art in its exhibitions. Since opening, it has played a central role among Korean galleries, presenting traditional Korean painting alongside modern and contemporary art reflecting the values of each era. It curates shows introducing major figures in modern and contemporary art as well as talented emerging artists, and also presents Asian art, including Chinese art. It mainly holds exhibitions and permanent shows centered on Korean-style painting, alongside Western and Eastern painting, sculpture, printmaking, and permanent exhibitions of Korean and Chinese woodblock prints. It also curates shows introducing artists with fresh, creative visions and works to discover promising up-and-coming talent through dedicated exhibitions for younger artists. As a first-generation Korean gallery, it maintains close relationships with established masters, mid-career artists, and rising talent alike.

서초구립반포도서관-2363243.name: Seocho-gu Banpo Library
서초구립반포도서관-2363243.description: Opened in 2013, Seocho-gu Banpo Library sits amid apartment complexes in the city, giving residents a comfortable, always-accessible place to read. Guided by the motto of a library for everyday reading, an e-library accessible anywhere, and a library where culture and art coexist, it connects with the community through specialized, distinctive reading and cultural programs that help build children's and teens' creativity, offer residents lifelong-learning and cultural opportunities, and grow alongside the community.

흰물결갤러리-2783567.name: Huinmulgyeol Gallery
흰물결갤러리-2783567.description: Huinmulgyeol Gallery sits on the ground floor of the Huinmulgyeol Art Center. Its founder, a longtime practicing lawyer, is said to have studied instruments, acoustics, and lighting design himself to build a space where people could enjoy art comfortably. Across three exhibition levels (ground floor, mezzanine, and 2nd floor), it displays paintings, sculptures, installations, and photography full of artistic spirit. Since opening in 2007, it has earned praise for its flexible use of 13 moving walls to reconfigure the space, and has held around 70 curated exhibitions to date.

서울대학교-박물관-129839.name: Seoul National University Museum
서울대학교-박물관-129839.description: Seoul National University Museum, established alongside the university's founding in 1946, continues an ongoing program of research, conservation, excavation, and collection. It holds around 8,000 items spanning archaeology and history, traditional art, and anthropology and folklore, including five items designated Korean Treasures. Since the 1960s, it has led more than 150 archaeological excavations, achieving significant scholarly results, and it holds special exhibitions each year alongside a general-education lecture series every semester.

유엠갤러리-130424.name: UM Gallery
유엠갤러리-130424.description: UM Gallery, now on Sinsa-dong's Garosugil, opened in August 1990 alongside its sister gallery, Musim Gallery in Cheongju. A space for contemporary-art dialogue, UM Gallery curates shows inviting accomplished artists working across painting, sculpture, printmaking, and installation. It also discovers experimental, noteworthy young artists and gives them room for free creative work. Having started with Korean monochrome painting in the 1990s, it now exhibits conceptual artists and has established itself as a specialist gallery centered on art-historically significant figures, while continuing to seek out promising emerging talent. Running galleries in both Seoul and Cheongju, it works to connect the regional and Seoul art markets and expand them further, with a goal of entering the global art market through international art fairs.

서울특별시교육청-구로도서관-130771.name: Guro Library, Seoul
서울특별시교육청-구로도서관-130771.description: Guro Library, across from Yeongrim Middle School, is a public library opened to provide information and support education and cultural activity for the local community. Beyond collecting and organizing materials for users, it has become a library deeply connected to residents by giving them access to a broad range of information online, in step with today's fast-changing information age. Reflecting the district's transformation into a digital industrial complex, Guro Library specializes in collecting and offering IT-related materials, alongside a range of reading-education and cultural-event programs. It has a general reference room, children's room, digital periodicals room, reading rooms, and club rooms. Guro Library is about 550m from Exit 4 of Daerim Station (Line 2).

금나래아트홀-1105871.name: Geumnarae Art Hall
금나래아트홀-1105871.description: Geumnarae Art Hall is a multi-purpose venue equipped to host classical music, theater, musicals, and other genres of performance. Its state-of-the-art sound system delivers excellent acoustics that reach every seat in the house, and its quick scene-change capability allows for dynamic staging. It also has a gallery space for art exhibitions, photo exhibitions, hands-on exhibits, and craft displays.

알부스갤러리-2783540.name: Albus Gallery
알부스갤러리-2783540.description: Albus Gallery, in Hannam-dong, Yongsan-gu, opened in May 2017 as Korea's first gallery dedicated to illustration art. Its name comes from the Latin word 'albus,' meaning white — the color that underlies every image. Evoking a rolled sheet of blank white paper, Albus Gallery aims to be like an open book on a white page, showcasing the individual stories artists bring to life through their work. It introduces illustration art that has historically struggled to gain recognition as fine art, working to build a culture where adults and children alike can enjoy not just picture-book and children's-book illustration, but any beautiful image that tells a story. Designed from the outset as an illustration gallery by architect Choi Wook, the building spans one basement and four above-ground floors. Its basement exhibition hall, built around a sunken garden, and its dedicated storage vault connect to the ground floor via a garden and internal stairway, with the main exhibition halls on the 1st and 2nd floors. The 2nd-floor main hall is designed with variety in mind — an 8m-high exhibition space lit by a skylight reaching to the 3rd floor, and another area looking out over a stand of trees across the way. Beside the 3rd-floor office, where birdsong rings out clearly, there's also an exhibition space for viewing picture books and artist videos.

대학로자유극장-3012777.name: Daehangno Freedom Theater
대학로자유극장-3012777.description: Daehangno Freedom Theater was opened in March 2005 by Nanta producer PMC Production, in Daehangno, to support the development of Korean-made musicals. Since its opening production, Nanta, in 2005, it has staged a lineup centered on original Korean musicals — including Dalgona, Music in My Heart, and Murder Case — establishing itself as a space offering audiences a fresh kind of cultural experience. The theater continues to experiment across genres and bring polished musical productions to audiences today. Its underground small theater puts the stage close to the audience for a vivid, immersive experience. It's 200m from Exit 1 of Hyehwa Station, right in the heart of Daehangno, surrounded by plenty to see and do.

청화랑-129930.name: Cheong Gallery
청화랑-129930.description: Cheong Gallery opened in 1987 in front of the Blue House in Jongno-gu with the goal of making the art market more accessible, curating and exhibiting a wide range of work. After relocating to Cheongdam-dong in 1994, it began participating in major international art fairs, helping introduce Korean artists abroad, while also discovering and nurturing new talent through domestic art fairs. Cheong Gallery represents artists ranging from veteran masters to mid-career and promising newcomers, curating a monthly exhibition and taking part in print-art fairs, gallery art fairs, the Cheongdam Art Festival, SIAF, and more, alongside curated group shows and invitational exhibitions. It's 500m from Exit 8 of Cheongdam Station (Line 7).

예스24라이브홀-3085122.name: YES24 Live Hall
예스24라이브홀-3085122.description: YES24 Live Hall, opened in 2006, is a dedicated concert venue bringing a range of live performances to audiences. Designed by the team behind Japan's legendary Shibuya AX venue, it spans roughly 1,500 pyeong, with professional-grade equipment supporting both seated and standing shows. YES24 Live Hall regularly hosts concerts by Korean and international artists as well as corporate and school events, with a cafeteria on the 2nd floor for a quick break. It's about 400m from Exit 2 of Gwangnaru Station.

금보성아트센터-3085035.name: Kum Bosung Art Center
금보성아트센터-3085035.description: Kum Bosung Art Center, in Pyeongchang-dong, spans two basement floors and two above-ground floors. Its director acquired the former Grolier Gallery in 2012 — a commercial gallery focused on non-figurative art since the 1970s — renaming it 'Gallery Pyeongchang-dong' and holding exhibitions inviting unknown artists. Kum Bosung Art Center, which opened a year later, was originally the Kim Heung-soo Museum of Art. A banner reading 'A resting place for free spirits carrying the burden of creation' always hangs at the center's entrance. It's known among artists as a 'sanctuary for galleries,' since it lends its space free of charge — including promotional support — to artists in financial difficulty or just starting out. Director Kum Bosung has also pursued international collaborations, including the Ahrc Korea project, and established the Korea Artist Award to raise the profile of Korean artists — given to an artist aged 60 or older who has produced 5,000 or more works, with substantial prize money attached. Beyond that, the center also awards a 'Creative Artist of the Year' prize to emerging artists, supporting their freedom to keep creating.

아트파크-130636.name: Art Park
아트파크-130636.description: Art Park offers a chance to experience art as healing through a range of exhibitions.
