Opened in 2003 in the cultural district of Samcheong-dong and relocated to Palpan-dong in 2020, it discovers young artists pursuing creative new directions and curates and exhibits their work. Since 2004, it has advised on the art program at Severance Hospital, and later curated exhibitions for Severance Art Space, offering opportunities for artistic healing and fresh creative experiences. It also takes part in major art fairs at home and abroad, introducing the work of young artists internationally. Beyond exhibitions, it advises on and curates a range of cultural projects, including the establishment of public and private art museums, art collection, museum architecture, and installation.

한생연-실험누리과학관-3080852.name: Hansaengyeon Silheom Nuri Science Museum
한생연-실험누리과학관-3080852.description: Silheom Nuri Science Museum, in Daechi-dong, opened in 2010 as a hands-on private science museum offering a range of experiments to try. Equipped with specialized lab equipment for life science, chemistry, and physics, it runs experiment programs suited to elementary, middle, and high school levels. It offers 15 experiment topics plus two special programs — building your own microscope and making a solar-powered robot — each running about 60 minutes. Since visits are managed on a reservation-only basis, advance booking lets visitors pick their preferred time slot.

웨스트브릿지-라이브홀-3082429.name: West Bridge Live Hall
웨스트브릿지-라이브홀-3082429.description: West Bridge, across from the Seogyo-dong Catholic Church near Hongdae, is a professional live concert hall on the building's basement level 3. It's equipped with sound systems and performance gear, has a green room, and seats 150, expanding to a 300-person capacity for standing shows.

삼모아트센터-3082034.name: Sammo Art Center
삼모아트센터-3082034.description: Sammo Art Center aims to expand access to culture, with a focus on classical music. Its Lavinia Hall performance space, seating around 100, mainly hosts invitational concerts and youth concerts. Ravenna Hall, a 30-seat space used for seminars and lectures, hosts Sammo Art Center's own music, arts, and humanities lectures, and can also be rented for corporate seminars or staff training. Cafe Intermission, a rest spot for before and after performances, rounds out the center's amenities. Sammo Art Center is about 200m from Exit 3 of Sillim Station, with parking available at the Sammo Tower building where it's located.

슈피겐홀-3081150.name: Spigen Hall
슈피겐홀-3081150.description: Spigen Hall, on the basement 2nd floor of Spigen Korea's HQ building, is a 200-seat venue for showcases, performances, and seminars. With LED screens, a range of sound equipment, and various AR devices developed through collaboration with VR companies, it's a distinctive venue for performances seeking a fresh kind of experience. Beyond standard offline shows, Spigen Hall also supports streaming and hybrid online-offline events. It's about a 5-minute walk from Exit 3 of Seolleung Station or Exit 7 of Samsung Central Station. There's no dedicated parking, so visitors need to use a nearby paid lot.

관악아트홀-3081147.name: Gwanak Art Hall
관악아트홀-3081147.description: Gwanak Art Hall, run by the Gwanak Culture Foundation, is a multi-purpose cultural space with a 700-seat performance hall and a gallery. The basement has a stage-production workshop and lecture rooms, and the 1st floor has a roughly 200㎡ exhibition hall. The 2nd and 3rd floors house a large, split-level performance hall equipped for high-quality concerts, musicals, and other productions. Gwanak Art Hall sits near the plaza at the Gwanaksan hiking-trail entrance, about 300m from Exit 1 of Gwanaksan Station.

scc홀-3080870.name: SCC Hall
scc홀-3080870.description: SCC Hall, across from the Seoul Arts Center — a hub of Korean arts and culture — is a split-level, 204-seat venue. A multi-purpose hall, it hosts recitals and chamber-music concerts as well as lectures, corporate events, and small receptions. Its main facilities are the stage, seating, lobby, and outdoor terrace. The fan-shaped stage was designed to connect naturally with the audience, with acoustics engineered for resonance, reflection, and reverberation. The seating uses premium fabric chairs arranged for maximum comfort while watching a performance. The lobby doubles as a reception or event space, with a screen monitor letting people outside watch the stage performance too. A dedicated outdoor terrace, finished in natural wood, offers a relaxed spot to enjoy the performing arts.

kt-g상상마당-대치아트홀-3080833.name: KT&G Sangsangmadang Daechi Art Hall
kt-g상상마당-대치아트홀-3080833.description: KT&G Sangsangmadang Daechi Art Hall is a professional venue equipped for theater, concerts, musicals, and other genres. Originally opened in 2006 as a 422-seat professional performance hall called KT&G Sangsang Art Hall — part of KT&G's cultural and artistic corporate social responsibility efforts — it was integrated into the wider KT&G Sangsangmadang network in 2017 and renamed Daechi Art Hall. It has hosted major works in Korean theater, including the play Liar and the musicals Hedwig and the Angry Inch and Singles, and continues to generously support new and original productions to help advance Korea's performing-arts scene.

광림-아트센터-bbch홀-3080576.name: Kwang Lim Art Center BBCH Hall
광림-아트센터-bbch홀-3080576.description: Kwang Lim Art Center BBCH Hall, in Apgujeong-dong, Gangnam, is a large venue for musicals, theater, concerts, and classical performances, built around the idea of a space for both rest and culture. Run by the Kwang Lim Church's Forest of Light Foundation, the Kwang Lim Art Center operates a classical-music venue, Jangcheon Hall, and a musical-dedicated venue, BBCH Hall. Housed within the church building, the 998-seat musical hall sits on floors 6–9 of the Social Service Hall, while the 613-seat Jangcheon Hall is in the basement of the Wesley Building. BBCH Hall, though a large musical venue, is more compact than comparable theaters, so sightlines are rarely an issue.

윤당아트홀-3080550.name: Yundang Art Hall
윤당아트홀-3080550.description: Yundang Art Hall, overlooking Seongsu Bridge, is a new-concept venue combining musicals, theater, concerts, and art exhibitions. Its high-quality performance and exhibition programs have established it as a hub for cultural exchange. Yundang Art Hall has both a theater and a gallery. The theater hosts a range of musicals, plays, and concerts, with 260 seats in Theater 1 and 150 in Theater 2. The gallery covers painting, sculpture, photography, and other media, with curated exhibitions focused on discovering and nurturing artists.

갤러리jj-2642151.name: Gallery JJ
갤러리jj-2642151.description: Gallery JJ, opened in 2013, curates in-depth exhibitions and offers art consulting tracking contemporary shifts in the Korean and international art world. Located in dynamic Gangnam, it helps drive the growth of contemporary art and culture, keeping close watch on artistic merit and market trends while promoting artists through fairs like Kiaf and other domestic and international art fairs, art lectures, and various gallery programs that connect with the public. It aims to remain a space where people gather around art and the issues of their time, and a cultural space that keeps broadening public engagement with visual art.

디뮤지엄-2704340.name: D Museum
디뮤지엄-2704340.description: D Museum, near Seoul Forest Station, relocated from Hannam-dong to Seongsu-dong to improve accessibility, expanding its role into a multi-purpose cultural hub with strengthened performance and education programs alongside its exhibitions. Building ongoing networks with artists at home and abroad, it introduces high-caliber contemporary art and design through international cultural exchange, builds culture together with the local community through neighborhood-linked projects, and runs a range of education and cultural programs year-round for everyone from children to seniors — working toward becoming an inspiring destination where anyone can enjoy and experience art, and a landmark of culture and art in Seoul.

성균관대학교-인문사회과학캠퍼스박물관-129838.name: Sungkyunkwan University Humanities & Social Sciences Campus Museum
성균관대학교-인문사회과학캠퍼스박물관-129838.description: This museum, on the basement level of the 600th Anniversary Memorial Hall at Sungkyunkwan University, houses and exhibits valuable artifacts passed down over centuries. Its galleries are divided into a permanent exhibition hall and a special exhibition hall. The permanent hall offers an immersive experience of Confucian culture, while the special exhibition hall researches and displays rare materials held exclusively by the museum. Centered on artifacts illustrating Joseon-era Confucian culture, it displays ceramics, calligraphy, paintings, books, documents, scholar's implements, musical instruments, clothing, accessories, furniture, and other cultural and everyday objects reflecting the spirit and legacy of past scholars. It also holds an annual special exhibition, featuring rare historical materials.

서울-중구문화원-130209.name: Jung-gu Culture Center, Seoul
서울-중구문화원-130209.description: The Jung-gu Culture Center, opened in 1995, provides cultural programs for residents of Jung-gu, Seoul. Through research into local history and the collection and preservation of cultural records, it works to carry forward and develop the district's traditional culture, hosting annual events like a festival marking Admiral Yi Sun-sin's birth, historical-heritage tours, and the Cheonggyecheon Culture & Arts Plaza, while building a new sense of local culture. It runs traveling programs on traditional etiquette for residents' convenience, holds sketch contests and gugak (traditional music) and dance competitions to give local youth a chance to experience and showcase their talent, and runs a variety of culture classes to spread cultural opportunities widely. Its rentable gallery hosts a range of exhibitions and events; with affordable rental fees, it has seen a growing number of group shows by office workers and university students as well as exhibitions by emerging and mid-career artists. It also runs a paid annual membership program, giving members access to heritage-site tours, priority delivery of the center's publications, and priority invitations to events.

한국영상자료원-2751316.name: Korean Film Archive
한국영상자료원-2751316.description: The Korean Film Archive, which began in 1974 as the Korea Film Preservation Center, is a public institution under the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism, located in the Sangam DMC complex. It collects, preserves, and provides access to all manner of film-related materials, and runs a range of public facilities to make film culture easy and enjoyable for everyone. Its Cinematheque KOFA screens classic, art-house, and independent films from Korea and abroad, while the Korean Film Museum lets visitors experience the history of Korean cinema firsthand. Its film library holds Korea's largest collection of film-related materials, and the archive also runs research and publishing projects, mobile cinema screenings, and various online services including Korean classic-film VOD.

tinc-2833824.name: TINC (THIS IS NOT A CHURCH)
tinc-2833824.description: THIS IS NOT A CHURCH (TINC) is a multi-purpose space in the former Myeongseong Church in Samseon-dong. Retaining the character of its former life as a worship space, it's open to a range of uses — exhibitions, performances, filming, workshops, and more. The main hall, on the 3rd floor, is defined by the natural sunlight that shifts across the space through the day, and hosts many performances and exhibitions that lean into natural light rather than artificial lighting design. The original chapel's stage has been preserved intact, allowing for distinctive staging during exhibitions and performances, and the chapel's benches remain available for audience seating.

어반아트-130637.name: Urban Art
어반아트-130637.description: Urban Art has introduced influential Korean and international contemporary artists and their work since 1995. An early mover in specializing within the art market, it built a solid foundation as a consulting firm dedicated to contemporary art. Drawing on that expertise, it became an official art dealer for Sotheby's, the global auction house, in 1999. It has also been actively engaged internationally, curating exhibitions of competitive Korean and international contemporary artists and introducing talented Korean artists abroad through major fairs like Art Basel and Art Miami. Beyond its role as a gallery, Urban Art has expanded further into the art business — since 2003, it has also run a public studio for landscape-art research and design alongside importing quality landscape installations from abroad.

수애뇨339-2739467.name: Suaenyo339
수애뇨339-2739467.description: Art space Suaenyo339 is a multi-purpose venue offering art exhibitions, music performances, a cafe, and private gatherings. The building was designed by Choi Si-young, head of Living Axis; Suaenyo was his first cultural space. The first floor, Cafe Suaenyo, combines a performance venue and cafe, with high-quality sound and stage lighting that let the space transform at any time — its seating, set slightly below floor level, is a signature feature. The second floor, Art Space Suaenyo339, is an exhibition space curating and hosting a range of art genres, notable for its outdoor 'sunken garden' exhibition area, a feature setting it apart from typical gallery spaces. The third floor, Suaenyo Room, is a fully equipped space for private parties and gatherings, with kitchen facilities and sound equipment, suited for small celebrations, company briefings, or launch parties, with a spectacular view at sunset.

조형갤러리-129907.name: Johyung Gallery
조형갤러리-129907.description: Opened in Gwanhun-dong in 1990 and relocated to a larger space in the Taehwa Building in Insa-dong in 2002, Johyung Gallery introduces a range of art through group exhibitions, curated shows by established artists, and rentable exhibition space. Its main exhibition area is a 15m-square room, with additional 4m and 6m sections, and a 3m ceiling height. The square layout and high ceiling give the space a clean, unobstructed view of every work on display, and its large scale allows for distinctive, custom exhibition formats.

분재박물관-130179.name: Bonsai Museum
분재박물관-130179.description: The Bonsai Museum, opened in September 1988 by the Korea Bonsai Research Institute, is a museum dedicated to spreading bonsai culture. It displays around 5,000 bonsai pieces cultivated and collected over more than 20 years by the institute, along with around 1,000 historical documents and photographs related to bonsai. Among its collection are more than 200 artistically significant bonsai works, including a 300-year-old maple and a juniper over 500 years old, alongside black pine, various fruit trees, plum, and crepe myrtle bonsai. Visitors can appreciate the beauty of nature captured in miniature and the shifting beauty of bonsai through time and season; the museum also has a tree-design school offering bonsai education, and a tree clinic that treats sick trees. Its programs focus on bonsai education for both public officials and the general public, with weekly beginner and technical classes for the public and six annual training sessions for related government staff.

외교사료관-130156.name: Diplomatic Archives
외교사료관-130156.description: The Diplomatic Archives is a special records center under the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, responsible for diplomatic-records policy and preserving diplomatic documents. It runs a document reading room, a history-of-diplomacy exhibition hall, a hands-on experience hall, and a special exhibition hall, both for public access to declassified diplomatic records and to promote awareness of Korea's diplomatic history. The history exhibition displays major treaties, documents, photographs, and mementos by era, from the 1876 opening of Korea's ports to the present, while the experience hall offers kids and teens a friendlier way to engage with diplomacy — a mock international conference podium, diplomacy quizzes, and photo ops as 'foreign minister' among its activities. The special exhibition hall regularly hosts themed shows on diplomacy. Non-profit school groups can book guided tours, offered twice each weekday morning and afternoon, and Saturdays feature a 'Diplomat School' program for children and teens.

금천문화원-130377.name: Geumcheon Culture Center
금천문화원-130377.description: The Geumcheon Culture and Arts Hall, run directly by the Geumcheon-gu Office, hosts performances, education programs, lectures, and cultural events, offering residents a range of participatory programs that promote local culture and community connection. The resident Geumcheon Culture Center preserves and develops the district's distinct local culture and runs various cultural programs; its 1st-floor lobby features a ginkgo tree, Geumcheon-gu's symbol, and a senior-run cafe supporting local job creation. Through ongoing cultural programming in its basement performance hall and lecture rooms, along with facility upgrades, it aims to become a landmark for the wider Geumcheon-Siheung area.

서울특별시교육청-융합과학교육원-남부분원-2751303.name: Southern Branch, Seoul Convergence Science Education Center
서울특별시교육청-융합과학교육원-남부분원-2751303.description: The Seoul Convergence Science Education Center serves as Seoul's hub for science education — building students' interest in science through hands-on inquiry activities, supporting teachers' professional development with training and teaching materials, and offering the general public opportunities for science-based learning. The center has a main branch and Namsan, Eastern, and Southern branches. The Southern Branch serves kindergarten through middle-school students in Seoul's southern districts, offering ecological experience and science-inquiry education, gifted education in math and science, and job-training courses for teachers supporting classroom instruction. It includes an early-childhood science play room, a natural-history exhibition hall, chemistry and life-science labs, an earth-science lab, a physics lab, elementary and middle-school invention classrooms, and a nature-observation garden, running programs including early-childhood science play classes, creative-science classes, Saturday family ecology classes, and other special programs.

구로꿈나무장난감나라-오류점-2591885.name: Guro Dream Tree Toy Land, Oryu Branch
구로꿈나무장난감나라-오류점-2591885.description: Playing with toys is as natural and essential to growing children as breathing or eating, but as playgrounds disappear and good, engaging toys grow scarce, Toy Land eases the financial burden on parents by lending out a variety of toys, giving families more chances to play together. Dream Tree Toy Land — the first of its kind to open among Korea's 232 local districts — is available for a 15,000-won annual membership fee to anyone registered as a Seoul resident, employed at a Seoul-based company, or raising a child up to age 8 (or 12 for children with disabilities). Borrowing itself is free. Each child can borrow up to 2 toys for 14 days, with one 14-day extension allowed, and reservations can be made for toys currently checked out.

식민지역사박물관-2605803.name: Museum of Colonial History
식민지역사박물관-2605803.description: The Museum of Colonial History is Korea's first museum dedicated to the history of Japanese colonial rule, documenting and exhibiting the history of imperial Japan's exploitation, the crimes of Koreans who collaborated with it, and the proud history of anti-Japanese resistance. This valuable cultural and historical space was made possible by donations and contributed materials from countless citizens, including Koreans living abroad. The 5-story building has exhibitions, a museum shop, and an event hall as a multi-purpose cultural space on the 1st floor; the 2nd floor lets visitors view archival footage and experience colonial-era daily life; the 3rd floor houses the Institute for Research in Collaborationist Activities; the 4th floor is an archive; and the 5th floor a lecture room. The rooftop has an observation deck overlooking Namsan and Yongsan, along with a rest area.

호림박물관-신림본관-129799.name: Horim Museum, Sillim Main Branch
호림박물관-신림본관-129799.description: The Horim Museum was established from cultural heritage and funds donated by Horim Yoon Jang-seop (1922–2016), for the preservation and development of Korea's national culture. Yoon founded the Seongbo Cultural Heritage Foundation in July 1981, then opened the Horim Museum in Daechi-dong, Gangnam-gu, in October 1982. The museum later expanded and rebuilt in Sillim-dong, Gwanak-gu, reopening in May 1999, and in June 2009 opened a Sinsa branch within the Horim Art Center in Sinsa-dong, Gangnam-gu — a rising cultural hub — to bring the museum closer to art-loving citizens. The Horim Museum holds around 20,000 items of cultural heritage across ceramics, metalwork, woodwork, painting and calligraphy, and books, including 62 items designated National Treasures or Treasures, and 11 designated Seoul Tangible Cultural Heritage. Its collection is highly regarded for both its breadth and quality, and serves as important foundational material for the study of Korean art history. Since opening, the Horim Museum has held exhibitions on a wide range of themes drawing on its exceptional collection, working to spread awareness of the beauty and value of Korean art, and continues collecting and exhibiting toward becoming a forward-looking cultural space that helps shape new art culture.

위니아트-건국대학교-새천년관-대공연장-130259.name: Wee Nyart (Konkuk University Millennium Hall Main Theater)
위니아트-건국대학교-새천년관-대공연장-130259.description: Wee Nyart was founded in 1997 under the philosophy of bringing quality performances to more people. As the first organization in Korea to run a dedicated cultural venue, it has pursued a distinctive path delivering not just quality performances but comprehensive customer satisfaction spanning price and service. Over more than a decade, it has worked to establish a mature Korean performing-arts culture and fulfill its proper social role. A multi-purpose venue, it hosts a wide range of cultural events spanning solo recitals to full orchestras, and classical to popular music. Fully equipped as a conference facility, it's also well suited to hosting international conferences and seminars.

광진문화원-130223.name: Gwangjin Culture Center
광진문화원-130223.description: Gwangjin Culture Center, established in 1996, works to carry forward and develop the culture of Gwangjin-gu. It runs local cultural events, arts and culture classes, research into local history, and its own gugak (traditional music) performance troupe, among other efforts to promote culture in the district. It also runs around 300 arts and culture classes, spanning generations and social groups, to connect residents and build a stronger local culture-education scene, and supports a range of club activities. The center's traditional-music troupe includes a samulnori percussion group, a children's gayageum ensemble, and a children's nanta drumming group, with about 30 members active across the groups. Gwangjin Culture Center is about 330m from Exit 1 of Gangbyeon Station (Line 2).

한양대학교-박물관-130958.name: Hanyang University Museum
한양대학교-박물관-130958.description: Hanyang University Museum, opened in 1979, has continuously excavated, collected, preserved, and researched valuable cultural heritage. Since 2003, it has held an annual special exhibition and runs a range of hands-on cultural programs, lectures, and museum-education projects, serving as a cultural platform and multi-purpose arts space reaching beyond campus into the wider community. The building spans 5 floors, though its exhibition space effectively begins on the 2nd floor, which traces the past and present of various electronic devices. The 3rd floor holds a special exhibition hall hosting themed shows on rotating topics. The 4th floor's ceramics, calligraphy-and-painting, and folklore room presents a carefully selected display of the museum's representative pieces, showing the intricate craftsmanship and everyday life of the people of their time. The 5th-floor archaeology and history room introduces the range of sites and artifacts the museum has surveyed since its first excavation, of the Misari prehistoric site, in 1979.

한생연-휴먼탐구과학관-2753817.name: Hansaengyeon Human Exploration Science Museum
한생연-휴먼탐구과학관-2753817.description: The Hansaengyeon Human Exploration Science Museum, in Banpo-dong, Seocho-gu, first opened in August 2018 and relocated from its original location near Express Bus Terminal Station to Gubanpo Station in September 2023. The museum focuses on helping children explore the human body, learning the structure and functions of our bodies and the science behind growth and disease, as a way to understand and develop their own health, growth, and future. Its connected science-education programs, in particular, are built around '3iN' (inspiration, integration, innovation), aligned with the spirit of the 4th industrial revolution and today's integration of humanities and sciences, focusing on developing children's scientific thinking and exploring future careers. Its linked science-education programs cover ages from early childhood through high school, tailored by grade level, using science materials and teaching aids developed in-house by Hansaengyeon's own education team.

매헌-윤봉길의사-기념관-753972.name: Maeheon Yun Bong-gil Memorial Hall
매헌-윤봉길의사-기념관-753972.description: Maeheon Yun Bong-gil is a national hero who, on April 29, 1932, threw a bomb at a ceremony in Shanghai's Hongkou Park marking the Japanese emperor's birthday and Japan's victory in the Shanghai Incident, targeting the assembled Japanese military and colonial leadership on the platform and announcing Korea's national spirit and will for independence to the world. Yun devoted the entirety of his short 25 years to his country; sentenced to death by a military court, he was executed in Japan on December 19, 1932, less than a year after his act. To properly honor Yun's life and achievements, the Maeheon Yun Bong-gil Memorial Foundation built this memorial hall in Yangjae-dong's Citizens' Forest in Seocho-gu on December 1, 1988, funded by public donations. Ownership transferred to the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs in 2016, and the exhibits were modernized in 2017–2018, reopening in 2018 to mark the hall's 30th anniversary. The central hall holds a statue of Yun Bong-gil seated before a Korean flag — the actual flag used at the April 27, 1932, oath ceremony of the Korean Patriotic Corps. Exhibition Hall 1 covers Yun's timeline, birth, upbringing, and personal effects; Exhibition Hall 2 covers his arrival in Shanghai, joining the Korean Patriotic Corps, his death, and a memorial space, with additional AR/VR experiences letting visitors 'meet' Yun Bong-gil.

노원문화원-130371.name: Nowon Culture Center
노원문화원-130371.description: Nowon Culture Center, established October 22, 1997, is a non-profit organization working to enrich residents' cultural lives through arts and culture programs and local-history research. Under the vision of realizing life's value through culture, it runs a range of culture classes strengthening and sharing the district's cultural identity and capacity through community networks. Alongside its classes, it also offers space-rental services to bring arts and culture education into daily life. It also trains cultural-tourism guides to help visitors easily and enjoyably learn about Nowon-gu's cultural and tourism resources.

동덕여자대학교-박물관-1628531.name: Dongduk Women's University Museum
동덕여자대학교-박물관-1628531.description: This museum, on Dongduk Women's University's Wolgok campus, showcases women's accessories and daily life in late Joseon alongside the university's founding and history. Established in 1977, its exhibition space includes two permanent halls — one on Joseon women's history and artifacts, and one on the university's history — plus a modern and contemporary art gallery and a donation room. A dedicated storage vault with specialized equipment safely preserves and manages a large collection of artifacts and artworks. The women's-history gallery displays representative Joseon-era women's accessories and clothing, sewing materials, and various household items, while the Chungang Memorial Hall traces the 115-year history of Dongduk Women's University and documents its founder, Chungang Cho Dong-sik.

서울무역전시컨벤션센터-setec-250469.name: Seoul Trade Exhibition & Convention Center (SETEC)
서울무역전시컨벤션센터-setec-250469.description: SETEC is an exhibition and convention facility serving a wide range of needs — trade shows, expos, international conferences, events, and cultural performances. It offers exhibition space suited to international-standard events, along with a range of supporting and convenience facilities. Located at a key transit point in Gangnam, SETEC has three exhibition halls and five conference rooms, capable of hosting both large-scale exhibitions and small- to mid-sized conferences, with around 70 exhibitions held each year. Parking is limited and gets crowded during exhibitions, so it's more convenient to use public transit — Line 3 or the Bundang Line — or nearby public parking lots.

남산골공원서울천년타임캡슐광장-229910.name: Namsangol Park Seoul Millennium Time Capsule Plaza
남산골공원서울천년타임캡슐광장-229910.description: Marking 600 years since Seoul became Korea's capital, this time capsule holds 600 items representing contemporary Seoul life, sealed away to be passed on as cultural heritage to descendants 400 years from now, at the 1,000-year mark. The capsule — shaped after the Bosingak Bell, 1.3m in diameter, 1.7m tall, and weighing 2.5 tons — was specially built by the city of Seoul on November 29, 1994, to mark the 600th anniversary. It holds around 600 items spanning politics, economics, society, and culture — a snapshot of life at the time. The Namsangol time-capsule plaza where it's buried is shaped like a roughly 1,500-pyeong meteor crater, a basin-like depression 42m across, with the capsule buried at its round, sunken center. The city also landscaped the surrounding area with marble slabs inscribed with congratulatory messages from mayors around the world in their own languages, 12 pillars encircling the basin symbolizing the cycle of time, and ginkgo trees, known as 'living fossils.' Items selected through two rounds of public submission were sealed in a mix of formats: 30% actual objects, 5% scale models and blueprints, 25% CD-ROM or microfilm, and 40% video recordings — everything from rice and barley seeds, 2,000 aerial photographs of Seoul, traditional medicine, school textbooks, spoons, bus tokens, and disposable lighters, to microfilm of a newspaper whose front page covered the Seongsu Bridge collapse — together capturing a detailed portrait of daily life in Seoul at the time.

피크닉-2762842.name: Piknic
피크닉-2762842.description: Piknic, on the hill connecting Seoullo 7017 and Namsan, is a multi-purpose cultural space with an exhibition hall and cafe spanning one basement and three above-ground floors. The 1st floor is a cafe, the 2nd an exhibition hall, the 3rd a restaurant, and the 4th a rooftop, with a gift shop just outside the building. Remodeled from a former pharmaceutical-company building, its artistic blend of past and present has made it popular among fans of Seoul's newest hotspots. It has hosted exhibitions by renowned cultural figures including Ryuichi Sakamoto and Jasper Morrison. The cafe's long tables facing the garden, along with its large chandelier and speakers, make a strong impression. It's 160m from Exit 3 of Hoehyeon Station (Line 4).

바라캇-서울-2835583.name: Barakat Seoul
바라캇-서울-2835583.description: Barakat Gallery, with roots stretching back to the 1860s and a 150-year tradition, holds a museum-grade collection of around 40,000 ancient artworks. Starting with a collection of biblical-era artifacts gathered in Jerusalem, the Barakat family has expanded its collection across five generations to span Mesopotamian, Egyptian, Greek, Roman, Byzantine, Islamic, European, Asian, African, and pre-Columbian civilizations — bridging East and West across history. The Barakat collection stands out not just for its enormous scope across eras and regions but for the beauty, historical value, rarity, and condition of its pieces. Barakat Gallery has partnered with leading museums worldwide, contributing significantly to research and education in culture, art, and archaeology. It currently has locations in London, Los Angeles, Hong Kong, and Seoul. Barakat Seoul, opened in 2016, showcases the Barakat collection through both permanent and special exhibitions, aiming for boundary-crossing shows that bridge ancient artifacts and contemporary art, blending art and daily life. Alongside its artifact-focused programming, it also runs Barakat Contemporary separately, bringing together works spanning eras and regions to broaden interpretive possibilities through the collision and crossover of different cultures.

호원아트홀-3085116.name: Howon Art Hall
호원아트홀-3085116.description: Howon Art Hall, in the career-support center building at Howon University, has a main theater, a small theater, and a studio. The main theater is a 462-seat, tiered venue; the small theater, in the basement, seats 100, also tiered; and the studio is a black-box-style venue with an operator's booth on the 2nd floor. It mainly hosts Howon University students' graduation performances, offering a vivid look at student talent. Howon Art Hall is about 700m from Exit 3 of Dunchon-dong Station.

국제아트홀-3080613.name: Gukje Art Hall
국제아트홀-3080613.description: Gukje Art Hall, opened in 2017, is a venue dedicated to classical music performance and recording. Its 186 tiered, fixed seats sit behind a stage built larger than the seating area to optimize acoustics. The close proximity of the seats to the stage helps draw the audience into the performance, and the venue is near Apgujeong Hyundai Department Store and Apgujeong Station. Parking is available at the building's own lot behind the hall or at the Apgujeong public lot next to the department store. Gukje Art Hall is right in front of Exit 5 of Apgujeong Station.

cxc아트뮤지엄-2947987.name: CxC Art Museum
cxc아트뮤지엄-2947987.description: CxC Art Museum is a new cultural space created jointly by Cabinet Club, part of local-culture platform Urban Play, and CCOC, a company charting a new paradigm for exhibition culture. Reimagining a roughly 1,000㎡ former food court on the 3rd floor of Star City, it's a multi-purpose cultural space combining an exhibition hall, art shop, bakery, cafe, workshop, and gathering space. CxC Art Museum, which officially opened November 18, 2022, marked its launch with an inaugural exhibition of work by Helga Stentzel, a visual artist based in London known for reimagining everyday objects with witty ideas, whose work has recently gained a strong following among younger audiences. Working across illustration, photography, video, and stop-motion animation, she has collaborated with major global brands and won a UK 'Food Art Creator of the Year' award in 2020.

이스탄불문화원-231962.name: Istanbul Culture Center
이스탄불문화원-231962.description: The Istanbul Culture Center was founded by a Turkish resident in Gangnam in 1998, to promote mutual understanding between Korea and Turkey. It offers Turkey-related books, video materials, and other documents for reading, and displays publications introducing news from Turkey. It also runs academic exchange programs including fellowships, Turkish-language classes, and various programs supporting tourism development between Korea and Turkey. It holds one-day classes to make Turkish culture more accessible, teaching visitors to cook Turkish dishes or make traditional crafts as a hands-on way to understand the culture. The Istanbul Culture Center is about 290m from Exit 2 of Seocho Station.

갤러리-서림-129927.name: Gallery Seorim
갤러리-서림-129927.description: Gallery Seorim, on Hakdong-ro in Gangnam-gu, was first opened as Seorim Gallery in Insa-dong in 1984 by the poet Kim Seong-ok, as a commercial art gallery. During its Insa-dong years, in 1991, Kim was a key organizer, together with Park Yeo-sook Gallery, of the Cheongdam Art Festival, held in what was then a cultural blank spot in Gangnam — helping establish Cheongdam-dong's identity as an arts district. In April 2008, the gallery relocated from Insa-dong to Cheongdam-dong and was renamed Gallery Seorim. It continues to exhibit a range of artists' work today, offering visitors a chance to experience a variety of art.

성수아트홀-3084413.name: Seongsu Art Hall
성수아트홀-3084413.description: Seongsu Art Hall, near Ttukseom Station in Seongsu-dong, is a 350-seat performance venue and multi-purpose cultural space. Equipped with modern sound, lighting, and stage technology, it hosts concerts, musicals, theater, dance, and other genres. The theater itself is on the 3rd floor — check in at the 2nd-floor ticket booth, then take the stairs up. Aiming to be a popular-culture space that brings happiness to visitors, its 2nd-floor lobby houses Seongsu Chaekmaru, a small reading nook, and a cafe open to performance-goers and local residents alike. Posters from past cultural events decorate its walls, adding an extra bit of visual interest, and the venue runs a variety of its own cultural events as a space for everyday arts and culture for the local community.

광야아트센터-3080599.name: Gwangya Art Center
광야아트센터-3080599.description: Gwangya Art Center, in Apgujeong, is a roughly 210-seat performance venue. It began in 2017 in Daehangno as Small Theater Gwangya, a dedicated Christian-musical venue, before relocating to Apgujeong in 2019 with upgraded seating and amenities, becoming today's Gwangya Art Center. Though it mainly features Christian arts and culture, it also functions as a multi-purpose cultural venue hosting other kinds of performances. The venue spans the 3rd and 4th floors of the building as a split-level space, with dressing rooms and offices alongside the performance hall. Parking is available at the King Kong Building, where the center is located. It's about 300m from Exit 4 of Apgujeong Rodeo Station.

예술가의집-2739475.name: Artist's House
예술가의집-2739475.description: Artist's House is an open, mediating space supporting artists' creative work and fostering connection between artists and between artists and the public. The building, once the main building of Keijō Imperial University during the Japanese colonial era, is designated Historic Site No. 278, designed by Park Gil-ryong (1898–1943), a pioneer of Korean architecture. It later served as the headquarters of the Arts Council Korea before becoming Artist's House in December 2010. Today, the 1st floor houses ARKO Young Art Lab for young artists, the 2nd floor is an open lounge where anyone can relax and try drip coffee, and the 3rd floor is rentable space for artistic creation.

상상톡톡-미술관-1106194.name: Sangsang Tok-tok Children's Art Museum
상상톡톡-미술관-1106194.description: Sangsang Tok-tok is a children's-only art museum, remodeled from an existing gallery within the Dream Forest Art Center in Beon-dong, Gangbuk-gu. Set within a forest, the museum lets children build imagination and creativity by experiencing both art and nature firsthand. The two-story space is decorated with a distinctive interior designed to spark children's curiosity — beloved animal and plant characters, staircases shaped like a forest, and railings made from pipes. Its 2nd-floor terrace even releases artificial rain, letting kids don yellow raincoats and umbrellas to play in a shower — part of the museum's approach of hands-on, felt experience rather than look-only exhibits. It also has a rest area and nursing room for families, and all of its child play spaces use eco-friendly materials for safety.

빛의-시어터-3085292.name: Theatre of Light
빛의-시어터-3085292.description: Theatre of Light reimagines the former Walkerhill Grand Theater space, building on its strengths to create a new cultural and artistic venue. Using high-resolution projectors and speakers to reimagine what an art exhibition can be, Theatre of Light rotates through the work of master artists, with docent-guided tours included. It's located at Walkerhill Hotels & Resorts; a free shuttle bus to the hotel runs from near Exit 2 of Gwangnaru Station or Exit 1 of Gangbyeon Station.

용산도시기억전시관-2714284.name: Yongsan Urban Memory Exhibition Hall
용산도시기억전시관-2714284.description: The Yongsan Urban Memory Exhibition Hall is a space for reflection on the Yongsan Tragedy — a fatal 2009 incident during redevelopment of the 'District 4, International Building Area' — and a record of Yongsan's transformation across many historical layers. It documents the 2009 Yongsan Tragedy, the history of Yongsan's urban development, and an archive and planning space looking toward the future Yongsan Park, serving as a channel for public dialogue on how that park should be shaped.

k현대미술관-2773265.name: K Museum of Contemporary Art
k현대미술관-2773265.description: K Museum of Contemporary Art, at the heart of Apgujeong-dong in Gangnam-gu, is a private museum spanning 6 floors and 4,959㎡ of exhibition space. Aiming to be an experimental, cross-disciplinary platform for contemporary art and a forum for dialogue in today's society, it respects bold creative attempts by artists from Korea and abroad, introducing experimental exhibitions to the public. To make art approachable for every age group, it offers barrier-free programs and workshops letting anyone from children to adults engage directly with art and take part themselves.

여의샛강도서관-3458646.name: Yeouisaetgang Library
여의샛강도서관-3458646.description: Yeouisaetgang Library, on Yeoui-daero in Yeongdeungpo-gu, is a public library offering books and e-books across a wide range of subjects, along with a maker space equipped with 3D printers and other maker tools. The 1st floor has a book cafe and reading room, and the 2nd floor has a reading room with floor-to-ceiling windows offering a beautiful view. It holds around 12,000 items in total, including about 5,000 children's books, offering a range of reading material for both kids and adults.

은평문화원-130374.name: Eunpyeong Culture Center
은평문화원-130374.description: Eunpyeong Culture Center was established to meet residents' cultural needs through Eunpyeong's distinctive traditional culture and a range of cultural programs, aiming to build a cultural space accessible and enjoyable for all residents while shedding new light on the district's overlooked history. Its flagship event is the Geumam Culture and Arts Festival, honoring the benevolent rule of King Yeongjo, Joseon's 21st king — an event for local elementary schoolers to explore local heritage sites and write about the humanity behind his benevolent philosophy. Its 'Evergreen' culture classes offer photography, beginner English, folk painting, watercolor, nanta drumming, singing, calligraphy, and tai chi, among other courses.

용산문화원-130372.name: Yongsan Culture Center
용산문화원-130372.description: Yongsan Culture Center is a dedicated cultural and arts institution running cultural events, uncovering cultural resources, arts education, and other programs for Yongsan-gu residents. Established under the Local Culture Center Promotion Act with authorization from the Seoul mayor's office in 1997, it operates as a non-profit corporation supported by the Ministry of Culture, the city of Seoul, and Yongsan-gu. Through programs like a youth sketch contest, free family-film screenings, a family writing contest, heritage-site tours, an invitational exhibition for Yongsan artists, a family culture festival, exhibitions of class participants' work, and publications on local history and culture, alongside a range of culture classes for adults and children, it contributes to Yongsan's cultural development and offers residents access to culture.

마포문화원-130369.name: Mapo Culture Center
마포문화원-130369.description: Mapo Culture Center works to build a lifelong-learning space where every Mapo-gu resident can become an active participant in arts and culture, creating a cultural venue accessible and enjoyable for everyone in the district. Its classes range from creative art, pansori singing, and violin for children to tailored programs for seniors — a smart-senior fitness class and a senior modeling class — alongside classes in classical Asian literature, everyday English, everyday Japanese, and folk-song drumming. It also holds local arts festivals and events, contributing to the growth of local tourism.

서울특별시교육청-용산도서관-130355.name: Yongsan Library, Seoul
서울특별시교육청-용산도서관-130355.description: Yongsan Library, run by the Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education, opened in April 1981 in the Duteopbawi neighborhood of Huam-dong, at the foot of Namsan. Spanning one basement and five above-ground floors, it has a reference room, digital and periodicals room, children's room, and self-study room, supporting residents' reading, lifelong learning, and leisure. Reflecting the area's relatively high foreign-resident population, it runs multicultural programs including Korean-language classes for foreign residents, and its children's room stocks leveled English books and multilingual titles. It also runs a signature poetry program — a creative-poetry contest, poetry-writing classes, and a gallery of winning entries — offering multiple ways to engage with poetry, alongside a small gallery and film screenings among its cultural programs. Its affordably priced 1st-floor cafeteria is popular with local residents, and its 5th-floor rooftop garden, with a sweeping view over Seoul, has become a noted spot for watching the sunset in the city.

성신여자대학교-3448679.name: Sungshin Women's University
성신여자대학교-3448679.description: Founded in 1936, Sungshin Women's University aims to nurture talented individuals who contribute to society through women's education. It began as Sungshin Girls' High School and later grew into a university, offering strong programs across the arts, humanities, social sciences, natural sciences, and engineering.

cts아트홀-1250301.name: CTS Art Hall
cts아트홀-1250301.description: CTS Art Hall, run by Christian broadcaster CTS, is a 404-seat multi-purpose venue. A multimedia cultural space, it hosts everything from musicals, worship concerts, ballet, and recitals to popular-music concerts and Christian events. It provides basic sound-operation support and equipment rental, along with performer green rooms, rest areas, and seating for guests with disabilities. The same building also has the roughly 330㎡ CTS Convention Hall, mainly used for corporate events, presentations, seminars, and lectures, with grand pianos and round tables available to rent. The CTS parking facility uses three tower systems, with room for up to 110 vehicles beyond regular parking.

kia360-3080558.name: Kia360
kia360-3080558.description: Kia360 is an experience center built around a 360-degree track, designed to help visitors understand Kia's brand and design philosophy and spark new ideas and inspiration. Through a range of hands-on experiences, visitors can learn about the Kia brand in depth and even test-drive vehicles. It's divided into three zones: the Brand & Design Zone, exploring the brand and its design; the EV Life Zone, for experiencing electric vehicles; and the Kia User & Heritage Zone, which digitally recreates the brand's history and past models.

동덕아트갤러리-130155.name: Dongduk Art Gallery
동덕아트갤러리-130155.description: Dongduk Art Gallery has hosted a range of exhibitions tracking trends in Korean art, giving artists a platform to present new work and the public a chance for open artistic appreciation. Renamed Dongduk Art Gallery in 1997, it moved to the basement of the newly completed Dongduk Building that same year, and began engaging with the international art world through exchange exhibitions with veteran artists from China and Taiwan alongside Korean artists. After a full renovation completed in early 2017, it now runs a range of curated exhibitions and related education programs, building ongoing networks with artists at home and abroad to help Korean artists reach international audiences and to introduce high-caliber contemporary art.

이한열기념관-130961.name: Lee Han-yeol Memorial Museum
이한열기념관-130961.description: The Lee Han-yeol Memorial Museum was built in 2004, funded by compensation the state paid to his mother and public donations, to preserve and restore the belongings of student activist Lee Han-yeol; it reopened as a private museum in 2014. It preserves and researches Lee's personal effects and records of the June Democratic Uprising of 1987, educating visitors on the history of Korean democracy through its exhibitions. A totem sculpture, 'Dream Sotdae,' by artist Choi Byung-soo stands on the rooftop; a mural by artist Kim Ya-cheon decorates the garden wall, and a mosaic mural by artist Lee Kyung-bok greets visitors at the exhibition-hall entrance. The wall connecting the 3rd and 4th floors of the exhibition space holds the funeral portrait carried in the procession that led his memorial march, and the 4th-floor permanent exhibition displays the clothes and shoes he wore when he fell, along with photographs and personal items. Visitors can also see a timeline of Lee's life, photographs captured by Reuters correspondent Chung Tae-won of the moment he was struck, items and writings from his school years, and records of the June Democratic Uprising.

백암아트홀-333121.name: Baekam Art Hall
백암아트홀-333121.description: Baekam Art Hall, opened in 2004 across from the Gangnam Fire Station on Teheran-ro, is a theater with a flexible stage suited to a range of performances — theater, musicals, concerts, dance, and more. It has a range of performance-support facilities, including individual and group dressing rooms and a rehearsal room with a digital piano and practice mirrors. The split-level venue has seating (including accessible seats) on the 1st floor and additional seating on the 2nd. Located in Samseong-dong, a part of Gangnam popular with younger crowds, it hosts many shows geared toward audiences in their 20s and 30s. Parking is limited, so public transit — Line 2 — is the more convenient way to visit.

우석뮤지엄-2553390.name: Useok Museum
우석뮤지엄-2553390.description: Useok Museum opened in February 2014, marking the 15th anniversary of the passing of seal-carving artist and calligrapher Useok Choi Gyu-myeong (1919–1999), alongside Gallery Chung, which displays his calligraphy. Useok Museum exhibits around 450 of Useok's seal-carving works, along with the scholar's implements he favored and the antique art he collected. Gallery Chung, showing his calligraphy, rotates through a collection of over 1,000 calligraphic works, and through a range of curated exhibitions helps illustrate how seal-carving and calligraphy connect with and develop alongside contemporary art.

전쟁과여성인권박물관-1907518.name: War and Women's Human Rights Museum
전쟁과여성인권박물관-1907518.description: The War and Women's Human Rights Museum remembers and teaches the history endured by survivors of Japan's wartime military sexual slavery system, working toward resolving the issue. It's a museum committed to the ongoing problem of wartime sexual violence, standing in solidarity and taking action toward a world free of war and violence against women. The long-held hope of the survivors — that children could grow up in a safe, peaceful world — resonated with citizens at home and abroad, leading to a fundraising campaign that culminated in the museum's opening on Children's Day, May 5, 2012. Through exhibitions of systematically collected and preserved records, the museum publicizes and preserves the memory of Japan's wartime sexual-slavery system and the movement to resolve it, working toward a world without war and violence.

서울특별시교육청-남산도서관-130352.name: Namsan Library, Seoul
서울특별시교육청-남산도서관-130352.description: Namsan Library, run by the Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education, was Seoul's first public library, opening in 1922; it moved to its current, newly built location in 1964, and was renamed Namsan Library the following year, 1965. The reinforced-concrete building, completed in 1964, was designed by architect Lee Hae-seong and, recognized for its preservation value, was registered as a Seoul Future Heritage in 2013. Namsan Library's vast collection of 500,000 volumes is organized across four subject-specific reference rooms — humanities and social sciences, natural sciences, literature (including a Korean-literature archive), and reading-therapy and language studies.

경기여고-경운박물관-서울-2552251.name: Gyeonggi Girls' High School Gyeongun Museum (Seoul)
경기여고-경운박물관-서울-2552251.description: The Gyeongun Museum was founded in 2003 through the shared effort of Gyeonggi Girls' High School alumnae. Starting with its inaugural exhibition, 'Early Modern Dress and Korean Culture,' it has held 40 curated exhibitions working to spread awareness of the beauty and academic and historical value of its collection of late-Joseon royal dress and modern and contemporary clothing and textiles. Beyond its curated exhibitions and published catalogs, the museum's high-quality academy lectures, exhibition-linked hands-on education, and recreations of Korean Empire imperial ceremonial robes — including the emperor's 12-symbol robe and empress's ceremonial dress, the yellow dragon robe, and black formal robes — are all the result of skill donated by alumnae volunteers. The Gyeongun Museum stands as a beautiful cultural space where history and tradition live on and where generations connect and converse.

국토발전전시관-2764516.name: National Land Development Exhibition Hall
국토발전전시관-2764516.description: Run by the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, this exhibition hall traces the story of Korea's national land development. Its galleries are organized into three halls: Guksemsae-eup Hall, Guknuri Hall, and Gukdonghaeng Hall. Guksemsae-eup Hall presents Korea's national land development plans and policy history by era; Guknuri Hall, focused on transportation, presents the history of major national infrastructure — public transit, roads, railways — and Korea's balanced regional development from 2000 to 2020, introducing policies and collection items that resonate with the public. Gukdonghaeng Hall traces Korea's construction history on the world stage, showcasing global landmarks built with Korean engineering and technology, along with the sometimes turbulent history of Korean companies expanding into overseas construction markets.

헬로우뮤지움-2488585.name: Hello Museum
헬로우뮤지움-2488585.description: Korea's first private children's art museum, Hello Museum reopened in Seongsu-dong, Seoul, in October 2019. It presents a new model for children's art museums built around future-oriented values for the next generation, establishing itself as a community-based eco-museum closely tied to local residents' lives. It runs exhibitions and education programs designed to build children's ecological sensitivity while enriching the lives of the wider community connected to those children.

더서울라이티움-2753089.name: The Seoul Lightium
더서울라이티움-2753089.description: The Seoul Lightium, a Seoul landmark whose spatial design was created directly by renowned lighting architect Jean Nouvel, is located at Galleria Foret, at a convenient transit hub linked to Seoul Forest. Hall 1 hosts a permanent media-art exhibition; Halls 2 and 5 host multi-purpose exhibitions and cultural events; Hall 3 hosts exhibitions by independent craft artists; and the Atrium hosts arts and culture exhibitions. A range of seasonal exhibitions is planned throughout the year, and the venue is also available to rent for expos, seminars, and product-launch events.

서울옥션-강남센터-2791398.name: Seoul Auction Gangnam Center
서울옥션-강남센터-2791398.description: Seoul Auction, founded in 1998, was Korea's first art-auction house. Through both offline and online auctions, it presents a wide range of items spanning Korean classical and modern-contemporary art, collectibles, wine, jewelry, and architecture. Alongside its Pyeongchang-dong headquarters and Gangnam Center, it also has exhibition spaces in Busan and Hong Kong, hosting a range of cultural events, exhibitions, and academy programs beyond auctions. Following its Pyeongchang-dong location, Seoul Auction opened its Gangnam Center in Sinsa-dong, Gangnam-gu, in January 2019. The building was designed by French architect Jean-Michel Wilmotte, known for the Seoul Auction headquarters in Pyeongchang-dong, Incheon International Airport, and more recently the Centre Pompidou Seoul, spanning 8 above-ground and 5 basement floors with an auction hall, exhibition spaces, and event hall. Located in the heart of Apgujeong, Seoul Auction's Gangnam Center has established itself as a multi-purpose cultural space where the public can enjoy art in everyday life and get closer to the experience of an art auction. It's also equipped with an ideal system for hosting a variety of rental events, transforming to suit different purposes.

서울특별시교육청-동대문도서관-130783.name: Dongdaemun Library, Seoul
서울특별시교육청-동대문도서관-130783.description: Dongdaemun Library, run by the Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education, opened in March 1971 and holds around 250,000 items. It runs a range of programs supporting residents' access to knowledge and personal growth. It opened an electronic-information room in 1996, and by July 1997 all its holdings became available for checkout. It has two general reference rooms, a children's room, an audiovisual room, a lecture room, and a self-study room, totaling 510 seats. Materials can be found and used on the spot in each room, with lending and holds also available. It also offers an evening reserve-pickup service for visitors who come to browse and collect materials after hours.

에스파스-루이비통-서울-3080501.name: Espace Louis Vuitton Seoul
에스파스-루이비통-서울-3080501.description: Espace Louis Vuitton Seoul is an urban art space exhibiting a range of artworks, one of the Fondation Louis Vuitton's galleries alongside its locations in Tokyo, Munich, Venice, Beijing, and Osaka. It was established under the foundation's mission to broaden international access to its collection and offer the public a chance to view it. It hosts special exhibitions of work by artists including Gerhard Richter and Andy Warhol.

샤롯데씨어터-130886.name: Charlotte Theater
샤롯데씨어터-130886.description: Charlotte Theater was Korea's first dedicated musical theater. Seating 1,260, it was built by the Lotte Group to help advance Korea's musical-theater industry, breaking ground in 2004 and opening on October 28, 2006. A match for any theater in the world, Charlotte Theater boasts an elegant, refined interior and exterior evoking a classic European atmosphere, fully equipped with state-of-the-art systems as a dedicated musical venue. For opera performances, it even rents out opera glasses so audiences can enjoy the performers' expressions and the lively stage up close, in greater detail.

강동문화원-130376.name: Gangdong Culture Center
강동문화원-130376.description: Gangdong Culture Center was established in 1999 to develop, spread, preserve, transmit, and promote the local culture of Gangdong-gu. Though its operations were limited in its early years, it has been notably active since forming a new leadership team in 2005, including conducting a survey of heritage sites across Gangdong-gu. Gangdong Culture Center runs a range of cultural activities for residents, including the Dunchon writing and sketch contests and exhibitions, a philharmonic orchestra, and a mixed choir, alongside programs for socially vulnerable groups and projects tied to the Amsa-dong archaeological site in Seoul, working to enrich the local community's cultural life. Its signature culture classes include Gangdong Culture University, offering lectures on classic literature, psychology, and other topics, and line-dancing classes.

국립어린이과학관-2545920.name: National Children's Science Museum
국립어린이과학관-2545920.description: Korea's first national science museum dedicated to children, built to nurture creative, integrative thinkers for the future, opened in December 2017. It has state-of-the-art exhibition spaces including three science playgrounds — a Sensory Playground, Imagination Playground, and Creation Playground — built around scientific principles that let kids play and learn at the same time, along with a planetarium and observatory, and a 4D theater engaging all five senses. It also plans and runs a range of tailored programs, including science-creation classes where kids learn alongside their parents and community-linked science-culture festivals.

창희보석예술관-1560179.name: Changhee Jewelry Art Museum
창희보석예술관-1560179.description: Changhee Jewelry Art Museum, run by Cho Chang-hee Jewelry (formerly J-Gem), exhibits jewelry artwork. It displays work made over roughly 35 years by master jeweler Cho Chang-hee, using his artistic sensibility and craftsmanship to transform gems, fossils, wood, and metal into art. Rather than a typical museum that simply explains the type and properties of raw gemstones, it presents these materials as living artworks with their own stories, letting visitors glimpse 50 years' worth of jewelry design and craftsmanship techniques along the way. The collection includes rare specimens like a 300-million-year-old fossilized tree, a 200kg stalactite, and a 350kg citrine quartz specimen, with around 50 works on display ranging from 30cm to 3m in size.

응암정보도서관-2010617.name: Eungam Information Library
응암정보도서관-2010617.description: Eungam Information Library, opened in 2009, is Eunpyeong-gu's flagship public library. Its original building is being rebuilt as part of the district's essential community infrastructure, so the library is currently operating temporarily on the 2nd and 3rd floors of a nearby commercial building. The 2nd floor holds the reference collection and foreign-language and Korean books for all ages, and the 3rd floor has a culture-class room for book discussions and lectures. It runs a range of cultural events tailored to the interests and character of the local community, offering a variety of enriching cultural experiences.

양천문화회관-1113537.name: Yangcheon Culture Hall
양천문화회관-1113537.description: Run by the Yangcheon Culture Foundation, Yangcheon Culture Hall is an arts and culture space for local residents that has established itself as the cultural heart of Yangcheon-gu. Through a range of performances, exhibitions, and cultural programs, it offers residents artistic inspiration. Its modern facilities and excellent sound and lighting equipment support a wide range of performance genres. By developing high-quality performances, festivals, and exhibitions, it aims to uncover new cultural possibilities for Yangcheon-gu and serve as a hub for promoting local culture and residents' access to it.

양천구-영어특성화도서관-2616589.name: Yangcheon-gu English Specialized Library
양천구-영어특성화도서관-2616589.description: On the 7th floor of Yangcheon-gu's Haenuri Town, the English Specialized Library is a remodel of the district's former children's English library and English experience center. It holds around 50,000 books, of which 19,500 are English-language titles spanning early picture books for young children to English originals for adult readers on a range of subjects. Of those 19,500 English books, 2,530 were donated by local residents, companies, and religious organizations. Beyond the stacks, the space includes a children's English reference room, two language rooms, two program rooms, a storytelling room, and a reading room for materials from sister cities abroad, making it a rich space for both English education and general knowledge for children.

양천구-갈산도서관-2611626.name: Yangcheon-gu Galsan Library
양천구-갈산도서관-2611626.description: Galsan Library, a cultural retreat for residents of Sinjeong 7-dong, is Yangcheon-gu's central library, offering quality books and a range of cultural programs to spark residents' interest in reading and build healthy reading habits. Its broad collection provides a strong environment for study and reading, with facilities for finding the latest information and comfortable reading spaces. It also runs a range of programs for children and teens, making it popular with family visitors. An easily accessible library for everyone, it plays an important role in sharing knowledge and information.

모차르트-콘서트홀-130503.name: Mozart Concert Hall
모차르트-콘서트홀-130503.description: Mozart Hall, seating 201, was designed as an ideal venue for piano recitals and small chamber-music performances. Its oval shape was chosen to harmonize the concert hall and lobby seamlessly. The interior, built around acoustic design, combines the dual tones of wood and stone, and its dedicated performance seating, spaced at 95cm, was designed with both acoustics and comfort in mind. The stage can be reconfigured depending on the type of performance, with 125 fixed seats and 76 movable seats in the audience area. Specially designed vibration-dampening pads float the performance space above the building's foundation and isolate it from the walls and ceiling, completely blocking structural vibration from the rest of the building. Combined with silencers on the HVAC ductwork and Korea's first Active Noise Control (ANC) system, the hall achieves an interior noise level of NC5 — far quieter than the international performance-hall standard of NC20 or below, and unmatched by any other venue in Korea.

긱-라이브하우스-1019327.name: Geek Live House
긱-라이브하우스-1019327.description: Geek Live House is a live club on the streets of Hongdae, part of the fabric of Korean indie music culture. A performance-focused specialist club, it was founded in February 2003 by professional musicians as a sanctuary of the indie scene. With professional musicians behind it, its stage, sound, and lighting are all top-tier. It features a wide range of shows, from curated indie-band performances to both professional and amateur rentals. With seated and standing capacity combined, it holds around 150 people and hosts 3–4 indie-band performances a day. A place to experience the current state of Korean indie music and a slice of Hongdae club culture firsthand, it has been refitted to support livestreamed performances. With professional staff and equipment, it offers a fresh, stylish, well-produced experience, and functions as a multi-purpose space for music-content production, online lectures, and live-commerce broadcasts.

농업박물관-2762852.name: Agricultural Museum
농업박물관-2762852.description: The Agricultural Museum, Korea's first museum dedicated to agriculture, was established in 1987 to preserve traditional farming artifacts donated by farmers for future education. It exhibits artifacts, records, farm tools, and transport equipment tracing the development of Korean agriculture from prehistoric times to the present. In 2005, the original museum building was demolished and rebuilt, adding a range of new exhibitions and hands-on education programs as part of a major renovation, and since its 30th anniversary in 2017, it has continued offering richer, more varied exhibitions and hands-on programs teaching the value and honesty of farming.

갤러리-마노-130581.name: Gallery Mano
갤러리-마노-130581.description: Gallery Mano, first opened in Gahoe-dong in 2003, relocated to Apgujeong-ro in front of Dosan Park in 2016. It carefully researches and discovers both established mid-career artists representing contemporary Korean art and fresh, original younger talent, curating exhibitions that showcase their range. Its exhibition philosophy is to closely study artists' work and invite those pursuing original, distinctive practices to exhibit. In keeping with the shared vision of artists, gallery, and audience, Gallery Mano works to enrich people's lives through work spanning every genre — painting, sculpture, photography, printmaking, media, video, and design.

지식재산전문도서관-719514.name: Intellectual Property Library
지식재산전문도서관-719514.description: The Intellectual Property Library, run by the Korea Institute of Intellectual Property, collects and provides access to IP-related information and specialized materials from around the world, serving as a hub for academic research and information exchange in the field. It works to gather diverse IP policy information and build cooperative networks through information exchange with domestic and international IP-related institutions, and collects and provides specialized materials including costly and rare IP publications, online databases, and e-journals. In 2018, it won the top prize in the specialized-library category (Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism Award) in the National Library Operations Evaluation, recognized for the excellence and expertise of its operations.

세종호텔-세종갤러리-129912.name: Sejong Hotel Sejong Gallery
세종호텔-세종갤러리-129912.description: Sejong Gallery has offered rich opportunities for art appreciation since its inaugural exhibition in 1961, an invitational show for Korean art master Kim Heung-soo. It reopened in the Sejong Hotel's 1st-floor lobby in 1992, curating and hosting a range of exhibitions featuring bold, accomplished artists. It has also expanded the idea of an exhibition beyond the gallery itself, turning the hotel's public areas and restaurants into gallery space, to strong response — becoming a firmly established cultural venue where collectors, art lovers, and international hotel guests from Japan, Europe, the U.S., and beyond can all freely enjoy art. In 2003, aiming to open a new, higher-caliber chapter in art culture, Sejong Gallery also built a window gallery viewable from outside, and in the second half of 2012 underwent a major renovation, transforming into a new hotel-based multi-purpose cultural space. In 2013, its basement space was remodeled into a gallery, opening as a second gallery space. Today, Sejong Gallery spans the ground floor, basement, and window gallery, offering a distinctly different spatial experience from a typical flat gallery layout, with varied exhibitions suited to each space.

성북문화원-130213.name: Seongbuk Culture Center
성북문화원-130213.description: Seongbuk Culture Center was established in 1996. Since then, its research into Seongbuk's local history, its Seongbuk Village Archive project, traditional-arts and other culture classes, and content development including the Seongbuk-dong Cultural Heritage Night Tour have helped lay the foundation for local culture in Seongbuk-gu. To support residents' cultural development, it runs programs across five categories — visual art and calligraphy, musical instruments and music, dance, everyday culture, and children's programs. Class registration is available both online and in person.

김대중도서관-699241.name: Kim Dae-jung Library
김대중도서관-699241.description: The Kim Dae-jung Library opened in November 2003 as Asia's first presidential library. It was established with materials donated by former President Kim Dae-jung, Korea's 15th president and Nobel Peace Prize laureate — the library building, roughly 16,000 records, some 10,000 books, and his Nobel Peace Prize award money — donated to Yonsei University, in line with Yonsei's founding philosophy. The Kim Dae-jung Library works to honor his lifelong dedication to democracy, human rights, peace, and the fight against poverty, aiming to become a world-class institution for education, research, and historical archiving.

서울시립-난지미술창작스튜디오-2745725.name: Seoul Nanji Art Studio
서울시립-난지미술창작스튜디오-2745725.description: The Seoul Nanji Art Studio is a residency-support space for artists. Remodeled from a former leachate-treatment facility between Nanji Hangang Park, Noeul Park, and Haneul Park, it's centrally located in Seoul with excellent access. Its 25 studios, research rooms, a circular exhibition hall, and outdoor workspace continuously support programs training and supporting accomplished artists and researchers from Korea and abroad.

손기정문화도서관-2904906.name: Sohn Kee-chung Culture Library
손기정문화도서관-2904906.description: The Sohn Kee-chung Culture Library sits behind the Sohn Kee-chung Memorial Hall. Its red-brick building, with an emotive, attractive exterior, draws many visitors. Ivy climbing the red walls, along with the artwork-filled garden and facade, adds to the pleasure of exploring the space. The interior is just as stylish and atmospheric as the exterior, making it a comfortable place to read or relax. It also stocks a range of periodicals, letting visitors freely browse magazines in their areas of interest. Each space in the Sohn Kee-chung Culture Library is designed around a particular theme, adding to the pleasure of exploring it.

유금와당박물관-2554142.name: Yugeum Roof-Tile Museum
유금와당박물관-2554142.description: The Yugeum Roof-Tile Museum holds a collection of East Asian roof-tile ends and bricks, Chinese pottery figurines, and various other ceramic and earthenware items. It runs two exhibition halls: the east hall is a permanent exhibition letting visitors see Korean roof-tile ends organized by era, while the west hall is a special exhibition space hosting an annual themed show on roof-tile ends and pottery figurines, organized by era or topic. It also runs education programs linked to its roof-tile-end and pottery-figurine collections, offering an engaging way to learn about East Asian history.

갤러리-미즈-130568.name: Gallery Miz
갤러리-미즈-130568.description: Gallery Miz introduces contemporary Korean art to the world. It participates in major art fairs in New York, LA, Beijing, and Hong Kong, and through curated and invitational exhibitions has helped drive the development of Korean art. Its MIZ Artists program, in particular, is dedicated to ongoing support for discovering young artists — through the program, around 20 artists, including Kim Ji-hyun, have gone on to play central roles in the Korean art world. Gallery Miz envisions its exhibitions as part of broader international cultural exchange, including introducing art from the developing world, and aims to gradually expand into the online art market as the 21st century's information age progresses. It also plans a range of programs, including a '21st Century Cultural Family' initiative and various curated series exhibitions.

갤러리-구루지-2591878.name: Gallery Guruji
갤러리-구루지-2591878.description: Gallery Guruji, on the 1st floor of the Guro Community Center, is Guro-gu's flagship gallery, hosting curated and rentable exhibitions to expand residents' access to culture. 'Guruji' is the name of a village that once stood around the site of the Guro Community Center — the oldest village in Guro-dong, so named because it sat in the lowest, most sunken part of the area, like the hollow center of a plate.

gb가빈아트홀-3080840.name: GB Gavin Art Hall
gb가빈아트홀-3080840.description: GB Gavin Art Hall, opened in 2017, is a roughly 300-seat venue built to offer more refined cultural and artistic performances. Built by Seoul Arts College, it's a multi-purpose venue suited to dance, musicals, concerts, conferences, and more. The 300-seat, split-level venue can hold up to 500 people for standing shows. Beyond performances, it can be used for seminars or receptions, with a cafe and outdoor terrace supporting a comfortable viewing experience.

윤동주문학관-2739477.name: Yun Dong-ju Literature Museum
윤동주문학관-2739477.description: While attending Yonhui College's literature department, poet Yun Dong-ju boarded at the home of novelist Kim Song (1909–1988) in Nusang-dong, Jongno-gu, and often climbed Inwangsan with his friend and fellow boarder Jeong Byeong-uk, refining his poetic sensibility amid nature. Some of his best-known poems — 'Counting Stars at Night,' 'Foreword,' and 'Self-Portrait' — were written during this period. The Yun Dong-ju Literature Museum was built in 2012 to remember the path walked by Yun Dong-ju, the resistance poet most beloved by Koreans, and his outlook on the world. It's a meaningful remodel of a decommissioned water pumping station and water tank on the slopes of Inwangsan. It won the 2012 Korea Public Architecture Award and the 2014 Seoul Architecture Award, and was designated a national memorial site for patriotism in 2015, drawing attention both for its architectural value and its historical meaning.

별책부록-2783339.name: Byeolchaekburok (Appendix Bookshop)
별책부록-2783339.description: Tucked into a quiet residential corner of Haebangchon in Yongsan-gu, this independent bookstore has a distinctively warm atmosphere. Its white-and-wood interior is bright while still letting each individual book stand out. It carries a range of independent publications from Korea and abroad, design and art books, secondhand books and records, and design objects from small, distinctive brands with a slightly unusual but special sensibility — drawing visitors looking for something outside the bestseller-driven shelves of large chain bookstores or brand-name shopping malls, something closer to their own personal interests and taste. It also runs a range of programs, from book talks to modest but enjoyable hobby and practical-skills classes. Since 2016, it has also operated as a publisher, putting out its own film-review magazine.

양천문화원-130215.name: Yangcheon Culture Center
양천문화원-130215.description: Yangcheon Culture Center was established on February 28, 1997, bringing together the shared vision of Yangcheon-gu's artists, educators, local historians, and businesspeople, aiming for community development and cultural promotion. A purely civilian-run special corporation, it works to preserve and create local culture and improve residents' quality of life. It offers classes designed to build residents' cultural and artistic awareness, skills, and appreciation, fostering wholesome emotional development, mind-body training, and personal enrichment, and holds local festivals and events including the Yangcheon Culture and Arts Festival and the Lunar New Year Full Moon folk festival, alongside efforts to discover and support local artists.

래미안-갤러리-1845434.name: Raemian Gallery
래미안-갤러리-1845434.description: Raemian Gallery is a brand experience center for Samsung C&T's housing brand, Raemian. Its exterior, drawing on the beauty of Korea's landscape, embodies Raemian's philosophy of harmonizing tradition and modernity, nature and cutting-edge design. Amid the surrounding square, vertical buildings, it uses vertical patterns of pine and willow trees — symbols of the Korean landscape — to evoke a traditional, irregular form as if the building's four sides were wrapped in a bojagi cloth. Its glass front blends naturally with the surrounding park and nature, expressing Raemian's architectural vision as an open, welcoming space. Raemian Gallery runs a range of seasonal exhibitions the whole family can experience and enjoy together, along with a space demonstrating Raemian's vision of a permanent housing experience and 'Homenic,' its convenient home-service concept. It also has model rooms showcasing the latest housing designs, a complex model, and a sales-consultation space, plus Art Hall, a multi-purpose cultural space hosting seminars, performances, and other programs.

한생연인간과로봇과학관-2759936.name: Hansaengyeon Human and Robot Science Museum
한생연인간과로봇과학관-2759936.description: The Hansaengyeon Human and Robot Science Museum is in Jamsil, Songpa-gu, Seoul. A specialist robotics science museum, it presents the arc of human life in exhibition form while letting visitors directly observe and try out the basic principles of various robots, the history of robotics, and cutting-edge robots. It's one of seven themed science museums run by Hansaengyeon, a company founded to guide young people into the world of science and help them find happiness and achieve their dreams through it.
