It operates as a hybrid of guided general viewing with exhibit explanations and hands-on experience programs; advance booking is required. It was selected for Seoul's student career-exploration program by the Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education in 2015.

본화랑-747530.name: Bon Gallery
본화랑-747530.description: Bon Gallery opened in 1988 in Gwanhun-dong, in today's Insa-dong cultural district. While centering established and mid-career artists and their mature, accomplished work, it also aims to reach the public with a younger, more contemporary sensibility by discovering emerging artists. Through curated exhibitions of well-known artists, engaging themed shows full of stories, and small 'encounter' exhibitions filled with dreams and love, it has fulfilled its role as a traditional gallery through careful artist selection, artwork management, and customer service. It has also discovered and introduced emerging and regional artists and supported group exhibitions by various art organizations, contributing to the growth and broader reach of Korea's art market. Since 1997, it has run a permanent exhibition space for Baeksan Kim Jeong-ok, Korea's only National Intangible Cultural Heritage master potter, and his successor Unam Kim Kyung-sik, helping spread awareness of the beauty and excellence of traditional Korean ceramics.

세종대학교-세종아트갤러리-2949775.name: Sejong University Sejong Art Gallery
세종대학교-세종아트갤러리-2949775.description: Sejong Art Gallery, a roughly 460㎡ space in Sejong University's Gwanggaeto Hall, opened in 2006, offering exhibition opportunities for talented young emerging artists, and has more recently begun curating a range of exhibitions for ambitious, accomplished mid-career artists as well.

우리소리도서관-3457702.name: Uri-sori Gukak Library
우리소리도서관-3457702.description: Uri-sori Library, tucked into the hanok alleys of Ikseon-dong, Jongno-gu, is Korea's only library dedicated to gugak (traditional Korean music). Opened in December 2017, it works to spread the beauty of gugak and offers a range of programs and materials that make traditional music easy for anyone to enjoy.

배봉산숲속도서관-3456336.name: Baebongsan Forest Library
배봉산숲속도서관-3456336.description: Baebongsan Forest Library is a distinctive space combining nature and a library at the heart of Seoul, letting visitors enjoy books amid the calm of the forest even in the middle of the city. The library preserves Baebongsan's natural scenery while offering the healing experience of reading surrounded by trees. A walking trail through the forest leads right to the library, giving visitors a relaxed setting to read or study in nature. Baebongsan Forest Library also runs a range of programs and events letting local residents and visitors enjoy culture and nature together — its children's programs and forest-experience activities, in particular, teach kids the importance of both nature and books. Its collection spans a wide range of subjects, making it an appealing space for anyone who loves culture and knowledge. More than a place to simply read, it's a cultural space offering a distinctive reading experience intertwined with nature — a healing spot blending books and the outdoors, ideal for a break from a busy schedule that combines both rest and learning.

구로미래도서관-3455122.name: Guro Future Library
구로미래도서관-3455122.description: Guro Future Library is a new space for Guro-gu residents' pursuit of knowledge and culture. Going beyond a typical library, it serves as a cultural hub for the community through forward-looking facilities and a range of programs, working through its activities to make Guro-gu an even better place to live.

논현문화마루도서관-3432213.name: Nonhyeon Culture Maru Library
논현문화마루도서관-3432213.description: Nonhyeon Culture Maru Library, in Gangnam-gu, is Korea's first library specializing in the arts, offering local residents a distinctive experience blending books and art. It features modern, light-filled architecture, cozy reading spaces, and a range of programs for everyone from children to adults. Its art-related materials and exhibition space are a particular highlight, and it has established itself as a community hub where residents share culture and creativity.

조은숙아트앤라이프스타일-3076665.name: Jo Eun-sook Art & Lifestyle
조은숙아트앤라이프스타일-3076665.description: Jo Eun-sook Art & Lifestyle, established in 2008, is a gallery exhibiting contemporary art across painting, sculpture, craft, and art furniture. With a distinctively imaginative interior and a sensibility for stylish everyday design, it runs permanent exhibitions of art furniture and ceramics for daily use. Visitors can also purchase distinctive ceramic pieces like designer cups, alongside a look at pieces meant for everyday use. Jo Eun-sook Art & Lifestyle is conveniently located about 500m from Exit 3 of Apgujeong Rodeo Station.

김세중미술관-3080721.name: Kim Se-jung Art Museum
김세중미술관-3080721.description: The Kim Se-jung Art Museum honors the intense life and artistic spirit of sculptor Kim Se-jung, a first-generation postwar sculptor who pioneered contemporary Korean sculpture and contributed to the development of Korean art. A formally registered private museum, it hosts exhibitions by established, veteran artists while discovering and introducing promising young and mid-career talent. Open to the wider community, it's a place where art-loving local residents and visitors alike can experience the joy of art. It first opened in a remodel of the home where sculptor Kim Se-jung and his wife, poet Kim Nam-jo, once lived, formally registered as 'The Joy of Art' in 2015 and renamed the Kim Se-jung Art Museum in 2017. It has two exhibition halls, an outdoor sculpture garden, a seminar room, and a cafe space. At the center of the museum grounds stands a centuries-old oak tree, preserved from the original residence, creating a beautiful backdrop for the space.

김영삼-도서관-3442973.name: Kim Young-sam Library
김영삼-도서관-3442973.description: The Kim Young-sam Library was established to honor the achievements and democratic spirit of former President Kim Young-sam. Located in Sangdo-dong, Dongjak-gu, it archives and preserves materials documenting his life and the democratization movement. The library includes an exhibition hall, reading room, and lecture hall, and is used as a center for historical research and education.

한생연융합교육과학관-3012716.name: Hansaengyeon Convergence Education Science Museum
한생연융합교육과학관-3012716.description: The Hansaengyeon Convergence Education Science Museum is a specialist science-education institution for children and teens, dedicated to science-education research and spreading science culture. Founded on October 18, 1993, it began with specialized workshops offering science education for young people. Starting in Jongno, it now runs seven science museums — in Mokdong, Banpo, Gangnam, Jamsil, Bundang, and Hongcheon — each with a different theme. It offers a range of age-appropriate programs, including early-childhood, lower- and upper-elementary, and vacation programs. Themed science museums: Jongno Center (Convergence Education Science Museum), Banpo Center (Human Exploration Science Museum), Gangnam Center (Silheom Nuri Science Museum), Jamsil Center (Human and Robot Science Museum), Mokdong Center (Life Science Museum), Bundang Center (Micro Science Museum), Hongcheon Center (Nature Science Experience Center).

국회도서관-3428697.name: National Assembly Library
국회도서관-3428697.description: The National Assembly Library, run by Korea's National Assembly, collects, preserves, and provides access to materials needed for legislative work. Established in 1948, it offers a range of information and materials to lawmakers and the general public alike, and also supports research and education. It's located in Yeouido, Seoul.

성동책마루도서관-3429640.name: Seongdong Chaekmaru Library
성동책마루도서관-3429640.description: Seongdong Chaekmaru is a book-cafe-style rest space; its materials are for in-library reading only, not checkout.

관악청소년센터-131453.name: Gwanak Youth Center
관악청소년센터-131453.description: Gwanak Youth Center offers Gwanak-gu residents recreational sports and culture-class programs, providing a range of youth programs and cultural spaces to help nurture healthy, well-rounded young people. Its facilities include an indoor pool, a small theater, club rooms, culture classrooms, a gym, and piano lessons, among other cultural amenities.

북한산-자락길-2406564.name: Bukhansan Jaraggil Trail
북한산-자락길-2406564.description: The Bukhansan Jaraggil is a walking trail through Bukhansan, running 4.5km from Sillakeorini Park in Hongeun-dong past the Hongnok badminton courts and Samha Unsu bus terminal to Okcheonam Hermitage — a fully barrier-free trail. Designed with special care for people with limited mobility — the elderly, wheelchair users, pregnant visitors, and those with strollers — the entire route keeps a grade under 10%, and 90% of its length is laid with wooden decking for a nature-friendly walking path. (Source: Seodaemun-gu Culture and Tourism website)

사당청소년센터-131534.name: Sadang Youth Center
사당청소년센터-131534.description: Sadang Youth Center, guided by the vision of 'a peaceful everyday life and a happy life for youth, together with the community,' is a youth facility offering a range of programs to help local young people take ownership of their own lives and grow into creative, democratic citizens who help shape their community.

서울청소년수련관-131138.name: Seoul Youth Center
서울청소년수련관-131138.description: Seoul Youth Center is a community-based youth training facility offering cultural, artistic, and athletic activities to support young people's character development and balanced growth, instilling sound values and civic awareness to help them grow into contributors to the nation's development. Built in 1970 by the Youth Protection Countermeasures Committee (predecessor of the Korea Youth Association) and donated to the city of Seoul, it's run by the Korea Youth Association.

장충체육관-990140.name: Jangchung Gymnasium
장충체육관-990140.description: Jangchung Gymnasium, in Jangchung-dong 2-ga, Jung-gu, was Korea's first indoor multi-purpose arena, opening on February 1, 1963. Beyond domestic and international sports matches, it hosts international competitions, concerts, madangnori (traditional outdoor theater), and other cultural events. The building's exterior is circular, topped with a dome roof. Its circular indoor court supports volleyball, basketball, and handball, with the main seating and lower flexible seating arranged around the court and upper-tier seating above, all focused toward the center — designed to avoid visual blind spots from any seat.

시립목동청소년센터-131137.name: Mokdong Municipal Youth Center
시립목동청소년센터-131137.description: The Mokdong Municipal Youth Center listens closely to young people's voices, running programs together with them for youth activities and welfare. It also works to protect young people's rights and participation, ensuring their safety, aiming to be a true home base for youth. It provides beneficial youth-activity programs and high-quality cultural and leisure space for the young people who are the true stakeholders of the community, schools, and the center itself.

목동종합운동장-2782166.name: Mokdong Sports Complex
목동종합운동장-2782166.description: Mokdong Sports Complex, in Yangcheon-gu, was built to expand access to recreational sports and support amateur baseball in western Seoul, beginning with a baseball stadium in 1987 before adding a main stadium and indoor ice rink. 'Mokdong Stadium' usually refers to the main stadium, which mainly hosts track-and-field and soccer competitions and various sports events; the baseball stadium hosts professional games as well as elementary, middle, high school, and university amateur baseball; and the ice rink hosts ice hockey, figure skating, and other ice-sports competitions and cultural performances. The multi-purpose field hosts soft baseball and futsal matches. Amenities include an indoor shooting range and a gym, plus a central plaza and other rest areas for residents' morning exercise.

마곡-실내배드민턴장-2755467.name: Magok Indoor Badminton Center
마곡-실내배드민턴장-2755467.description: Run by the Gangseo-gu Facilities Management Corporation, the Magok Indoor Badminton Center spans 2,853㎡ with 14 courts and 650 spectator seats. A dedicated badminton facility, it combines instruction from former professional players with specialized facility management. Bright interior lighting and flooring create a comfortable environment, and it has large changing rooms, showers, and restrooms. A 30-minute cleaning break runs at 2pm on weekdays. Daily admission and lesson fees offer special discounts for nearby residents and Gangseo-gu residents.

강동그린웨이-가족캠핑장-1017568.name: Gangdong Greenway Family Campground
강동그린웨이-가족캠핑장-1017568.description: Set in the forested Iljasan Nature Park in the heart of Gangdong-gu, the Gangdong Greenway Family Campground minimizes environmental impact while preserving the site's natural character, offering families a nature-friendly campground for their health and happiness. Under Seoul's urban park ordinance, it's open to any Seoul resident, not just those in Gangdong-gu. Deck sites with pre-installed tents let visitors camp even without their own gear. Online booking is required before use.

서울시립보라매청소년센터-131408.name: Seoul Boramae Youth Center
서울시립보라매청소년센터-131408.description: Seoul Boramae Youth Center is currently run, under a city contract, by the Seoul Catholic Youth Association. It offers youth activities, life-respect programs, youth counseling, and educational support. The center focuses on climate and environmental issues and disaster safety to support young people's sustainable development and growth. To help realize young people's rights as environmental citizens and empower them to build safe lives and environments on their own initiative, the center runs a strategic initiative called Plan N. Its youth activities include a Youth Steering Committee, letting young people directly advise on and evaluate the center's operations and programs, along with a range of clubs and activity programs. Opened in 1986, Seoul Boramae Youth Center has spent decades running programs spanning counseling, activities, education, and welfare for young people. Building on that experience, its counseling office supports children and teens facing psychological difficulties, helping them grow up healthy, with a range of specialized counselors on staff to offer tailored support for a variety of psychological challenges.

충효길코스-1코스-고구동산길-2674964.name: [Chunghyo-gil Trail, Course 1] Gogu-dongsan-gil
충효길코스-1코스-고구동산길-2674964.description: Dongjak-gu has long been known as a district of loyalty and filial devotion, and its streets are dotted with historical and cultural spaces reflecting that spirit — the origin of the name Dongjak Chunghyo-gil ('loyalty and filial devotion trail'). Walking this trail lets visitors enjoy the ease of a natural green space in the heart of the city while reflecting on that spirit. The Chunghyo-gil has 7 courses in total; Course 1, Gogu-dongsan-gil, starts at the reservoir park and runs to the summit of Gogu-dongsan, along Seodalsan's cedar path and its ecological bridge, ending at the Sangdo entrance — 3.2km in total, taking about an hour. Exit 2 of Nodeul Station (Line 9) leads directly to the information center marking the start of the trail; check the overview map there to get oriented before setting off on Gogu-dongsan-gil. Picking up a trail map booklet at the information center makes the route easier to follow. Partway along Gogu-dongsan-gil is the back gate of Chung-Ang University, beyond which the trail enters Seodalsan — home to a phytoncide forest, a forest library, a forest kindergarten, and a wildflower garden, among other highlights.

창동문화체육센터-131958.name: Changdong Culture & Sports Center
창동문화체육센터-131958.description: Changdong Culture & Sports Center, opened in 2005, is a public sports facility with a pool, gym, and a range of sports programs. It has rentable facilities including a performance hall, gymnasium, futsal field, and GX studio. For visitors' convenience, it has changing rooms, showers, and other amenities, plus a dedicated warming room by the pool to help swimmers regulate their body temperature. It carefully selects its instructors to keep program satisfaction high, and class registration is first-come, first-served.

안양천-물놀이장-2591870.name: Anyangcheon Water Play Area
안양천-물놀이장-2591870.description: In the hot summer months, the Anyangcheon Water Play Area opens as an urban escape where children and families can beat the heat and enjoy a fun summer. With a large pool and a range of water-play facilities, it's enjoyable for everyone from kids to adults. Designed with safe water depths, it lets children play with peace of mind, with trained lifeguards on duty at all times. Shade structures and benches nearby also make it a comfortable place to rest. Beyond the water play area, a bike path and walking trail nearby make it a great spot for exercise and a stroll too. The Guro-gu Anyangcheon Water Play Area is an ideal choice for anyone looking to cool off with a refreshing swim during the summer heat.

세븐럭카지노-강남코엑스점-131903.name: Seven Luck Casino (Gangnam COEX Branch)
세븐럭카지노-강남코엑스점-131903.description: Seven Luck Casino's Gangnam COEX branch, at the heart of Gangnam, is a Korean-style casino blending an Asian atmosphere with state-of-the-art facilities. Established to attract tourists, it's open to foreign passport holders only — a passport is required to verify age and nationality. It has 82 table games and 121 of the latest slot and electronic machines, offering roulette, baccarat, sic bo, Caribbean stud poker, slot machines, and more. Located near the COEX Center and a cluster of top hotels, duty-free shops, a large movie theater, and department stores, it makes for an easy combination of sightseeing, shopping, and entertainment.

북한산-둘레길-10구간-내시묘역길-1197225.name: [Bukhansan Dulle-gil, Section 10] Naesi Tomb Trail
북한산-둘레길-10구간-내시묘역길-1197225.description: The Bukhansan Dulle-gil connects and refines a network of existing paths into a gentle, low-elevation loop trail around the base of Bukhansan. Of its full 71.5km — including the sections within Seoul and the Uiryeong-gil trail — 45.7km opened on September 7, 2010, with the remaining 25.8km opening on June 30, 2011. Designed for people to walk in harmony with nature, the trail is organized into 21 themed sections spanning streamside paths, dirt paths, forest paths, and village paths — a trail meant to be easily accessible to everyone while preserving Korea's precious natural landscape and offering a way to experience its history, culture, and ecology. Section 10 of the 21 themes, Naesi Tomb Trail, offers a chance to rediscover the role and lives of the royal eunuchs who guarded the king like a shadow, holding the code of unwavering loyalty above all else. Along this section, visitors can also see the site of 'Yeogiso,' where legend holds a courtesan drowned herself in a pond after failing to reunite with a lover conscripted to help build Bukhansanseong Fortress, as well as the thrilling 'Dulle-gyo,' a suspension bridge set 8m above the ground. The section runs 3.5km, taking about 1 hour 45 minutes.

난지캠핑장-2750941.name: Nanji Campground
난지캠핑장-2750941.description: Nanji Campground is in Nanji Hangang Park, Mapo-gu, Seoul. It's reached by heading toward Nanji Hangang Park past the northern end of Gayang Bridge on Gangbyeon-buk-ro. Campers driving must use the public parking lot, since cars aren't allowed inside — gear needs to be carted in by hand or cart. Run by the city, admission is affordably priced. It has 180 campsites. The rental-tent area has 26 four-person tents and 78 six-person tents, with admission included in the rental fee; mats are provided inside sized to each tent's capacity. Six-person tents equipped with heating and cooling carry a separate electricity fee. The group-tent area has 16 medium, 20 large, and 40 extra-large Mongolian-style tents, which — unlike the rental tents — require a separate admission fee, plus an additional electricity charge for tents with heating and cooling.

북한산-둘레길-4구간-솔샘길-1196871.name: [Bukhansan Dulle-gil, Section 4] Solsaem-gil
북한산-둘레길-4구간-솔샘길-1196871.description: The Bukhansan Dulle-gil connects and refines a network of existing paths into a gentle, low-elevation loop trail around the base of Bukhansan, opened in two stages in 2010 and 2011 across a full 71.5km. Organized into 21 themed sections spanning streamside, dirt, forest, and village paths, it's designed to be accessible to everyone while preserving nature and offering a way to experience history, culture, and ecology. Section 4, Solsaem-gil, takes its name ('pine spring path') from the dense pines and clear spring that have long marked the area. Along this section, the trail passes through the Bukhansan Ecological Forest, a signature urban park in Seongbuk-gu known for its well-tended wildflower garden along a small flower-lined path. The section runs 2.1km, taking about an hour.

더클라임-클라이밍-마곡점-3076152.name: The Climb Magok Branch
더클라임-클라이밍-마곡점-3076152.description: The Climb is an indoor climbing gym designed to make climbing easy and fun even for first-timers. Korea's largest bouldering-gym chain, it operates 10 locations across Seoul and Gyeonggi-do that members can use interchangeably. Beyond climbing itself, it also offers climbing-related fitness training, with structured instruction from a professional coaching staff that includes instructors with graduate degrees in climbing research and current national team members.

더클라임-클라이밍-양재점-2753381.name: The Climb Yangjae Branch
더클라임-클라이밍-양재점-2753381.description: The Climb makes climbing easy, fun, and safe even for first-timers. Korea's largest bouldering-gym chain, it operates 10 locations across Seoul and Gyeonggi-do that members can use interchangeably, with structured instruction from a professional coaching staff that includes instructors with graduate degrees in climbing research and current national team members.

인서울27-골프클럽-2757125.name: In Seoul 27 Golf Club
인서울27-골프클럽-2757125.description: In Seoul 27 Golf Club is Seoul's only public golf course, an ideal leisure destination with excellent transit access and a range of amenities. The site once posed a bird-strike risk as land near the airport turned into bird habitat; after the Korea Airports Corporation selected an operator to build a golf course along with a soccer field, tennis courts, and other resident sports facilities, the golf course finally opened in 2019. It has three courses — EAST, WEST, and SOUTH — laid out long and straight like an airport runway. Booking through the website is required before use.

한강레져스포츠-2783331.name: Han River Leisure Sports
한강레져스포츠-2783331.description: Right next to the E-Land Cruise pier in Yeouido, Han River Leisure Sports offers motorboat rides, jet skiing, water skiing, wakeboarding, banana boats, and other water-sports activities on the Han River. Being able to enjoy water sports right in the middle of the city without having to travel far makes it especially popular. Motorboats and jet skis are great for cutting across the wide Han River at thrilling speed while enjoying the cool river breeze. Wakeboarding, which lets riders feel the river's current with their whole body, is another draw — beginners can try it after a simple lesson. Flyboarding, hard to find elsewhere, is also available: strapped to a board powered by a small jet engine, riders shoot up above the water and move freely through the air, evoking the feeling of flying like a superhero from the movies. A national flyboarding team member personally leads lessons here, making for an especially memorable experience.

남산국치길-2778449.name: Namsan Guk-chi-gil (National Humiliation Trail)
남산국치길-2778449.description: This roughly 1.7km history-trail runs through the Yejang slope of Namsan in Seoul, built by the city in August 2018 to mark this section's painful history, including the 1910 forced annexation of Korea by Japan. Named 'Guk-chi-gil' ('trail of national humiliation'), it's meant to remember the site where Korea lost its sovereignty and to help heal that wound. The trail begins at Namsan Yejang Park, former site of the Korean Residency-General building where the annexation treaty was signed, and follows an L-shaped floor marker connecting several sites: the former site of the Korean Residency-General (where independence activist Kim Ik-sang once threw a bomb), the site of the Nogi Shrine, the Gabo War Memorial erected by Japan after its victory in the First Sino-Japanese War, the site of the Gyeongseong Shrine, and finally the former Joseon Shrine. At the end of the trail stands the Seoul Comfort Women Memorial, installed by the city on August 14, Comfort Women Memorial Day.

워커힐숲길-2773297.name: Walkerhill Forest Trail
워커힐숲길-2773297.description: Walkerhill Forest Trail, in Gwangjin-gu, is a 774m walking path near the Grand Walkerhill Hotel, running from the hotel's parking lot to Achasan Eco Park. Known for its cherry blossoms in spring, it's especially famous as a foliage destination, with roadside trees turning vivid colors along the route. Its well-paved road also makes it a popular scenic drive as well as a walking trail.

한강드론공원-3080519.name: Han River Drone Park
한강드론공원-3080519.description: The Gwangnaru model-aircraft field in Gwangnaru Hangang Park, opened in June 2016, is a dedicated drone-flying space. It has a fixed-wing drone zone (160m by 30m), a racing-drone zone, and a rotary-wing drone zone; advance online booking gives 3 hours of free use. Flying a drone requires prior flight authorization, so pilots need to apply for flight permission and any video-recording permission through the Drone One-Stop civil service system. Drones must have the owner's name and contact information attached, and insurance is required in case of accidents. Nearby attractions include Gwangnaru Bicycle Park, several themed forests, Gwangnaru Rose Park, and a pool.

양천구-둘레길-하천형코스-2612154.name: [Yangcheon-gu Dulle-gil] Riverside Course
양천구-둘레길-하천형코스-2612154.description: The Yangcheon Dulle-gil weaves together mountains, city streets, and streams, offering a people-centered, worry-free loop trail designed for a slow, deliberate walk that lets visitors see, feel, and enjoy the district's culture and history. It's organized into a mountain course through Yangcheon's hillsides, an urban course through the city center, and a riverside course centered on Anyangcheon Stream, with GPS-mapped accessibility and safety information available via website and mobile app. The riverside course runs 5.1km total along Anyangcheon, split into sections: Yanghwa Bridge–Yangpyeong Bridge (1.1km), Yangpyeong Bridge–Mokdong Bridge (1.0km), Mokdong Bridge–Omok Bridge (1.2km), Omok Bridge–Sanjeong Bridge (0.8km), and Sanjeong Bridge–Ogeum Bridge (1.0km).

청계천-자전거도로-2783315.name: Cheonggyecheon Bike Path
청계천-자전거도로-2783315.description: This newly refurbished bike path follows the refreshing flow of Cheonggyecheon Stream in Seoul, running from Yongdap-dong to Cheonggye Plaza. Gently graded for cyclists, it's a great route for a family ride. The Cheonggyecheon bike path is especially appealing for its constantly shifting scenery — starting near Dongdaemun's fashion malls, arguably the heart of K-fashion, past the secondhand bookstore street that long served as a treasury of knowledge for struggling scholars and students, a restored shantytown section evoking Cheonggyecheon's old streetscape, and Sewoon Sangga, Korea's first mixed-use residential-commercial building and once the country's only comprehensive home-appliance market — all passing by, one after another, as you ride.

키즈돌핀-서대문dmc점-3082446.name: Kids Dolphin Seodaemun DMC Branch
키즈돌핀-서대문dmc점-3082446.description: Kids Dolphin Seodaemun DMC is a dedicated children's swim school using an eco-friendly saltwater pool. Small classes of up to 4 students per instructor teach proper stroke form and technique, tailored to each child's individual level and pace. Lessons focus not just on physical development but on building sociability, character, and leadership. With a dedicated-teacher system, homeroom teachers and specialized assistants personally guide children through changing, showering, using the restroom, and the swim lesson itself, offering a full 'All Care System' that supports kids all the way to their front door. The pool stays between 31–33°C, keeping it warm even in winter, with depths tailored to children for safe learning. Kids use child-specific shampoo and body wash, and assistant teachers help with lotion after showering. For waiting parents, there's a cozy cafe-style viewing area, and the class is also livestreamed online or via smartphone so parents can watch in real time even without visiting.

다이브라이프-2773417.name: Dive Life
다이브라이프-2773417.description: Dive Life, in Seocho-gu, Seoul, is a dedicated freediving and scuba-diving education center. Its own pool — 3m deep, 5m by 8m — lets visitors practice freely and take professional lessons in freediving and scuba diving. It offers specialized courses and experience programs for a range of skill levels and ages. A viewing window lets people outside the pool watch divers below the surface, so visitors at the center's cafe can watch the scuba divers at work. Booking and payment are handled through Naver Reservations, with 2-hour slots available per person.

천왕산-가족캠핑장-2792594.name: Cheonwangsan Family Campground
천왕산-가족캠핑장-2792594.description: Cheonwangsan Family Park Campground, in Oryu 2-dong, Guro-gu, is about a 30-minute walk from Cheonwang Station (Line 7). Built partway up the modest, neighborhood-hill-like Cheonwangsan, it lets visitors enjoy the campground alongside the surrounding urban nature park. Its 30 deck sites have top-quality showers, restrooms, and a dishwashing area, and it rents out everything needed for camping — tents, cooking gear, heating and cooling equipment — so visitors can show up empty-handed.

우이동-가족캠핑장-2908314.name: Uidong Family Campground
우이동-가족캠핑장-2908314.description: Uidong Family Campground, right next to a subway station, offers a great view despite being an urban campground — Bukhansan's Baegundae Peak rises directly overhead, the site borders Ui Valley, and several well-known cafes are nearby. Run by the city of Seoul, it's a fairly large facility with 20 deck sites and 11 glamping units. It's not an auto-campground, but wagons are available to help move gear from the parking lot to your site, so it's not too inconvenient. A range of camping gear and heaters can be rented, and groceries are well stocked. Above all, its affordable price and great accessibility have made it a popular choice. Nearby attractions include Bukhansan hiking and Dulle-gil trails, the April 19th National Cemetery, and a historical pilgrimage trail.

초안산캠핑장-2734171.name: Choansan Campground
초안산캠핑장-2734171.description: Choansan Campground is easily reached from the city center. Dense forest and clean air let visitors experience nature even within the city. It has a playground and lawn plaza for kids, along with a range of camping zones — an auto-camping zone, a healing-camping zone, and cabin houses. Well-equipped amenities make it approachable even for camping beginners.

목동아이스링크-실내-130978.name: Mokdong Ice Rink (Indoor)
목동아이스링크-실내-130978.description: Opened December 1, 1988, Mokdong Indoor Ice Rink has been the cradle of Korea's rapid growth in winter sports, serving as a training ground for Seoul's top young skating prospects. It hosts domestic and international ice-sports competitions and has an international-standard ice-hockey rink. The facility has two rinks, one above ground and one below, so the underground rink opens to the public whenever the main rink hosts a special event, keeping the facility available at all times. Amenities include a skate shop, sharpening room, lounge, and convenience store.

고덕사회체육센터-130999.name: Godeok Community Sports Center
고덕사회체육센터-130999.description: Godeok Community Sports Center, opened in 1988, works to improve local residents' health and quality of life. Its facilities include a pool, gym, aerobics room, secondary gymnasium, spin studio, and lecture rooms, with a range of programs including swim lessons, general fitness classes, gym training, spin classes, and culture classes.

북악하늘길-스카이웨이-하늘한마당-하늘마루-1037031.name: [Bugak Skyway] Haneul Hanmadang–Haneulmaru
북악하늘길-스카이웨이-하늘한마당-하늘마루-1037031.description: The Bugak Hanul-gil is a walking trail connecting the ridge and slopes of Bugaksan in Seongbuk-gu, Seoul. This section was the route used in 1968 by Kim Shin-jo and 30 other North Korean commandos attempting to raid the Blue House, and was closed to the public for 42 years before reopening. Untouched for decades, it's now densely forested with a rich, varied ecosystem. The Bugak Hanul-gil has three walking trails plus the Skyway. Each course shows off a different view and character, and the trail's ups and downs give it a roller-coaster-like thrill. The highlight of the Bugak Hanul-gil is the spectacular view from its various overlooks — step onto one, and the forest opens up to reveal Seoul's broad sky. The Skyway section runs from Haneul Hanmadang through Bugakjeong Pavilion and Damojeong Pavilion to Sup-sok-maru and finally Haneulmaru, a total of 3,200m.

북악하늘길-3산책로-북카페-숲속다리-1037027.name: [Bugak Hanul-gil, Trail 3] Book Cafe–Forest Bridge
북악하늘길-3산책로-북카페-숲속다리-1037027.description: The Bugak Hanul-gil is a walking trail connecting the ridge and slopes of Bugaksan in Seongbuk-gu, Seoul. This section was the route used in 1968 by Kim Shin-jo and 30 other North Korean commandos attempting to raid the Blue House, and was closed to the public for 42 years before reopening. Untouched for decades, it's now densely forested with a rich, varied ecosystem. The Bugak Hanul-gil has three walking trails plus the Skyway, each with its own view and character, with ups and downs that give the trail a roller-coaster-like thrill — and the highlight throughout is the spectacular view from its various overlooks. Trail 3 runs from the Book Cafe through Dongmaru to the Forest Bridge, a total of 640m.

정립회관-수영센터-131313.name: Jeongrip Center Swimming Pool
정립회관-수영센터-131313.description: The Jeongrip Center Swimming Pool, reopened in August 2006 after a full rebuild, offers local residents swimming and a range of water-sports activities — a great place for fitness and health management. The pool welcomes users from children to adults, with swim-lesson programs, private lessons, and open swim hours available. Entry is open from age 6, with ages 6–7 required to be accompanied by a guardian for safety.

kbs스포츠월드-131326.name: KBS Sports World
kbs스포츠월드-131326.description: As Korea's largest comprehensive sports center, running a rich lineup of programs across 14 different sports, KBS Sports World stands as a genuinely representative Korean sports facility. Its wide-ranging programs — spanning swimming and 13 other sports — contribute to public health and residents' quality of life. Programs in swimming, fitness, bowling, golf, and more help energize community sports and build residents' physical fitness.

강서청소년회관-131140.name: Gangseo Youth Center
강서청소년회관-131140.description: Gangseo Youth Center is a space for young people. Its mission is to help teens grow into leaders of the 21st century through character development and emotional growth, and to contribute to community cultural development through a range of culture classes, academic support, sports, and social programs. Through various programs and activities, it supports young people's engagement with culture, art, sports, and career exploration, helping them grow up healthy. It offers freely accessible space and a range of education programs that build social skills and support personal development.

북악하늘길-2산책로-하늘교-성북천발원지-1037020.name: [Bugak Hanul-gil, Trail 2] Haneulgyo Bridge–Source of Seongbukcheon
북악하늘길-2산책로-하늘교-성북천발원지-1037020.description: The Bugaksan Hanul-gil connects the ridge and slopes of Bugaksan, which rings the Blue House, and links up with the trail running along the scenic driving route Bugak Skyway into the mountain's interior. Long closed to civilians, it retains a pristine, untouched natural ecosystem. The mysterious energy of its deep forest offers a peaceful, quiet hike. The Bugaksan Hanul-gil has three courses in total. Trail 2 passes through the site of fierce fighting during the January 21, 1968 Incident, running from Haneulgyo Bridge to the source of Seongbukcheon Stream. Once closed to civilians after the commando infiltration, it has been reborn as a walking trail — along Trail 2, hikers can see bullet marks still visible at Hogyeongam Rock, the site of the incident's fiercest fighting, and the source of Seongbukcheon Stream, home to a pond with a range of wildlife. From the Haneul Observatory, visitors get a wider view over central Seoul than from the summit of almost any other mountain in the city.

와이키키레저-2783318.name: Waikiki Leisure
와이키키레저-2783318.description: Waikiki Leisure, on the banks of the Han River in Seoul, offers water skiing and motorboat rides alongside wakeboarding, wake surfing, and other water sports. Unlike widely known water skiing, wakeboarding and wake surfing ride the wake left behind a passing boat instead of ocean waves. A demanding full-body workout, the sport has built a passionate global following despite being barely a decade old. In Korea, it can be enjoyed year-round from April to November, adding to its appeal. At Waikiki Leisure, the wakeboarding and wake-surfing team 'JUSTSURF' runs dedicated lessons, offering instruction tailored to every level from beginner to advanced.

광운대학교-아이스링크-131607.name: Kwangwoon University Ice Rink
광운대학교-아이스링크-131607.description: Kwangwoon University's Donghae Culture & Arts Center Ice Rink was the first international-standard (60m by 30m) ice rink built at a Korean university, completed in 1997 and opened to the public in 1998 to help develop winter sports in northern Seoul. It's used for recreational sports and health among students and local residents, and for discovering future winter-sports talent. It offers a range of lessons — daily, private, and group — to give as many people as possible a chance to learn winter sports. Facilities include a sharpening room, spectator seating, lockers, and an exhibition room, plus amenities like a snack shop and cafe.

슈터스클럽-3074766.name: Shooters Club
슈터스클럽-3074766.description: Shooters Club is an affordable indoor shooting range in the city. It offers a range of airsoft guns, including realistic recoil air pistols, single-shot rifles, bolt-action sniper rifles, and 120-round automatic rifles. A key draw is that it's open year-round with no closed days. Alongside the range, Shooters Club also runs a gun shop across the way selling airsoft guns. It's about 130m from Exit 11 of Gangnam Station, making it easy to visit.

서울시립망우청소년센터-2762808.name: Seoul Mangu Youth Center
서울시립망우청소년센터-2762808.description: Seoul Mangu Youth Center, opened in 2006, has been run under contract by Seoul YMCA since 2016, working closely with the local community. It aims to be an open educational space where young people take ownership of their own lives, learn the value of life and peace, and participate actively in the community, while also supporting residents' healthy lifestyles. It offers a range of programs to help young people grow up healthy, supporting career exploration, cultural activities, and hands-on learning to build self-development and social skills. It also partners with the local community on volunteer work and social-participation opportunities. In a safe, comfortable environment, it helps young people pursue their dreams and talents — an important center supporting them in preparing for the future and building sound values.

롯데백화점-본점-에비뉴엘-273806.name: Lotte Department Store Main Branch Avenuel
롯데백화점-본점-에비뉴엘-273806.description: Avenuel, run by Lotte Department Store, is a garden-and-gallery-concept luxury department store in Jung-gu, Seoul. Connected to the Lotte Department Store main branch, it's a high-end store carrying only international fashion and jewelry brands. It has its own dedicated photo zone and a distinctive interior. Floors from B1 to 5 house luxury boutiques including Chanel, Gucci, and Louis Vuitton; floors 6–8 have a movie theater showing the latest releases; the 9th floor has a gallery hosting a range of themed exhibitions and restaurants; and the 10th floor has a skin clinic and spa. A new kind of department store offering both shopping and a range of services.

강서농산물도매시장-2741626.name: Gangseo Agricultural Wholesale Market
강서농산물도매시장-2741626.description: Gangseo Agricultural Wholesale Market, in Oebalsan-dong, Gangseo-gu, is Seoul's second major produce wholesale market for the southwestern region, selling agricultural, seafood, meat, and manufactured goods. It was Korea's first market to introduce a market-dealer system alongside the standard auction system, so both distribution methods now operate side by side. The market also houses specialized retail and wholesale food-ingredient shops, the Suhyup Gangseo Fish Market selling seafood shipped directly from producing regions, and the Seoul Agro-Fisheries & Food Corporation. The general public can also buy produce and fruit here, and its location near Magok Station makes it easy to reach.

견지동-불교용품거리-132205.name: Gyeonji-dong Buddhist Supplies Street
견지동-불교용품거리-132205.description: Gyeonji-dong Buddhist Supplies Street grew up around the entrance to Jogyesa, head temple of the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism, extending toward Gongpyeong intersection and part of Insa-dong, with around 30 shops specializing in Buddhist books and religious supplies. Here visitors can buy Buddhist texts, wooden moktak percussion instruments, prayer beads, monk's robes, Buddha statues, incense, and more. Gyeonji-dong Buddhist Supplies Street was designated a Seoul Future Heritage site after being proposed by citizens and experts, following fact verification and review by the Future Heritage Preservation Committee, under a principle of citizen-led discovery and preservation.

마장-축산물시장-1253230.name: Majang Meat Market
마장-축산물시장-1253230.description: Majang Meat Market handles meat shipped hourly from livestock farms nationwide, along with imported meat, with mandatory country-of-origin and price labeling that gives consumers strong confidence in what they're buying. As food directly connected to public health, the market has even been recognized by the Korean Medical Association as a trustworthy source. Offering higher-quality meat at lower prices, Majang Meat Market sells for up to 30% less than large supermarkets. Rather than following the layout of a traditional old-style market, it uses advanced systems to keep pace with Korea's fast-changing retail environment and customer expectations, allowing trade to happen efficiently and independently.

둔촌역전통시장-2751863.name: Dunchon Station Traditional Market
둔촌역전통시장-2751863.description: Right next to Exit 3 of Dunchon Station (Line 5), Dunchon Station Traditional Market is a straight, alley-style traditional market. Beloved by local residents for over 30 years, its narrow lanes are packed with around 80 shops selling everything from daily necessities to food, with a wider-than-usual selection of seafood setting it apart from other markets.

우석공예사-132522.name: Useok Handicrafts
우석공예사-132522.description: Useok's ginkgo-leaf products are made under strict inspection standards and quality control, earning praise in export markets including Japan. Mainly producing items for weddings, dowries, and gifts or souvenirs for abroad, the shop brings out the beauty of traditional Korean craft in ways many people never knew existed, earning acclaim for its refined, presentable quality and wide range of designs.

태릉시장-2761478.name: Taereung Market
태릉시장-2761478.description: Taereung Market, between Jungnang Station and Junghwa Station in Jungnang-gu, began as street stalls that sprang up on a covered road in 1987 and operated as a traditional market for over 30 years before its environment was improved under Seoul's 2021 Taereung Market Specialty Street project. Shops occupy the ground and 2nd floors of the Taereung Esemville mixed-use building, while the stalls in front of the apartments have been converted into Seoul's mobile-shop format, lined up in a straight row along the main road. It's also known as Taereung Enterpia.

남구로시장-2591755.name: Nam-Guro Market
남구로시장-2591755.description: Nam-Guro Market, in Guro-dong, is a traditional market that grew up organically in the 1960s, boasting 50 years of history. Its main offerings include produce, meat, seafood, and Chinese groceries; with such a long history, it has many well-known eateries and distinctive shops offering a range of food to enjoy. Laid out in a single straight line without any small side alleys, it's very easy to shop. One distinctive feature is its strong Chinese presence — many Chinese food shops and Chinese customers. Even non-Chinese food and goods are labeled in both Korean and Chinese throughout the market. About 10% of its roughly 200 shops sell Chinese food and are run by Chinese residents, and in fact 70–80% of market visitors are Chinese.

한순례한복침구-987669.name: Han Sun-rye Hanbok & Bedding
한순례한복침구-987669.description: Han Sun-rye Hanbok is a custom hanbok (traditional Korean dress) shop that designs everything in-house, from color to cut. Rooted in traditional beauty, it tailors each design to the wearer's face, body shape, mood, taste, and personality, making anyone stand out. With deep expertise, it carries forward and develops traditional hanbok while staying at the forefront of modern trends, expressing a Korean sensibility through contemporary materials and varied designs.

동화상가-2762868.name: Donghwa Sangga (Garment Accessories Market)
동화상가-2762868.description: Donghwa Sangga, on Jangchungdan-ro in Jung-gu, is a 5-story market specializing in every kind of garment accessory — fabric, buttons, metal fittings, heat-transfer prints, labels, zippers, hot-fix crystals, embroidery, and more. Opened in 1968, it has over 50 years of history. It's accessible via Exit 8 of Dongdaemun Station (Line 4), behind Pyeonghwa Market, or Exit 14 of Dongdaemun History & Culture Park Station (Line 2).

대도종합상가-985952.name: Daedo General Market
대도종합상가-985952.description: Daedo General Market is a shopping complex within Namdaemun Market selling everyday household goods. It carries a range of imported items, distinctive housewares, men's accessories, and wholesale tableware, and has the largest concentration of interior-decor and ornamental shops within Namdaemun Market. Each shop displays a wide array of items, with distinctive decor pieces and kitchenware varying shop to shop, making for enjoyable browsing.

영일시장-2763905.name: Yeongil Market
영일시장-2763905.description: Yeongil Market, in Mullae-dong, Yeongdeungpo-gu, is an alley-style traditional market specializing in produce, though it also sells fish, meat, dried goods, and groceries found at any general market. Its scale shrank after street stalls were removed in 2007, but nearby restaurants, supermarkets, and traditional-market merchants still come here to buy goods wholesale. The market is busiest between midnight and 4am, though retail sales are also available; many shops close after 4pm. It's about 500m from Exit 6 of Mullae Station (Line 2) or 600m from Exit 6 of Yeongdeungpo Station (Line 1).

노룬산골목시장-2751406.name: Norunsan Alley Market
노룬산골목시장-2751406.description: Norunsan Market, established in the 1970s, is Gwangjin-gu's oldest and most well-maintained alley-style traditional market. A short walk from Konkuk University Station, it's easy to reach, and its nostalgic tteokbokki and traditional snacks are especially popular. Walking further toward the north end of Yeongdong Bridge connects directly to Yeongdong Bridge Alley Market, letting visitors explore both at once. Packed with satisfying food, it's a popular market for all ages, and its alleyway shops give visitors a warm, nostalgic traditional-market feel.

신평화패션타운-2762844.name: Shin Pyeonghwa Fashion Town
신평화패션타운-2762844.description: Across the street from Dongdaemun's Pyeonghwa Market in Jung-gu, this 5-story fashion complex has around 1,200 shops and 3,000 merchants. The 1st floor's outer ring holds sportswear and accessory shops, with underwear and lingerie and sock shops inside. The 2nd floor sells women's and men's formal wear; the 3rd, young casual wear and suits; and the 4th floor, women's clothing, jeans, and T-shirts through export-focused shops, drawing buyers from China, Japan, Taiwan, India, the Philippines, Mongolia, and beyond. Built in December 1969 as Shin Pyeonghwa Market, it was renamed Shin Pyeonghwa Fashion Town in January 1999.

남평화상가-2761466.name: Nam Pyeonghwa Market
남평화상가-2761466.description: Nam Pyeonghwa Market, established in 1980 on Jangchungdan-ro in Jung-gu, is a wholesale market specializing in bags and clothing, commonly called 'Nam Pyeonghwa Market,' though the building's own signage reads 'Fashion Nam Pyeonghwa.' Around 700 shops operate across its 3-story building, opening for business at 8pm. Floors 2 and 3, casual-clothing shops, run from 8pm to 6am, while the bag wholesalers on the 1st floor and basement run from midnight to noon. It's accessible via Exit 7 of Dongdaemun Station (Line 4) or Exit 6 of Dongdaemun Station (Line 1).

청평화패션몰-2761460.name: Cheong Pyeonghwa Fashion Mall
청평화패션몰-2761460.description: Cheong Pyeonghwa Fashion Mall, on the banks of Cheonggyecheon Stream at the Cheonggye 7-ga intersection in Jung-gu, is a 6-story wholesale clothing complex opened in 1983, with around 1,300 shops. It's the largest of Dongdaemun's wholesale markets, still widely known by its familiar name, 'Cheong Pyeonghwa Market.' Women's clothing is its main line, alongside dedicated shops for uniforms and group-order clothing. As a daytime market, Cheong Pyeonghwa operates from 11pm to noon. Its location near Dongmyo Station makes it convenient to visit.

인현시장-2522037.name: Inhyeon Market
인현시장-2522037.description: Inhyeon Market, in Inhyeon-dong 2-ga, Jung-gu, grew up organically from the late 1950s through the early 1960s and carries over 50 years of history. The neighborhood is also known as the former home of Prince Inseong, King Seonjo's seventh son. Tucked into the back alleys of Chungmuro — known for its film district and printing alleys — Inhyeon Market can be found weaving around the high-rise buildings of the modern downtown, a traditional market where past and present coexist. Chungmuro's printing alleys stretch across three neighborhoods — Inhyeon-dong, Euljiro, and Pil-dong — and tucked in among them is the small alley market of Inhyeon. Just 2m wide and 202m long, its 110 densely packed shops sit near tourist spots like Myeongdong and Namsangol Hanok Village, drawing an estimated 20,000 visitors a day, though the market has also weathered hard times due to its aging infrastructure and merchants. Inhyeon Market shrank to its current form in the late 1960s when Sewoon Sangga was built nearby; today, its hidden gem restaurants and low prices have made it a familiar spot for nearby printing workers and small merchants. It's also known as a favorite after-work destination for downtown office workers looking to unwind, earning it the nickname 'paradise of flavor.' More recently, young entrepreneurs and artists have opened youth-run shops in Inhyeon Market, adding a fresh new energy to the mix.

이태원시장-1253279.name: Itaewon Market
이태원시장-1253279.description: Itaewon Market, in Itaewon-dong, Yongsan-gu, is one of Seoul's most representative markets. Itaewon is known for its blend of diverse cultures and international atmosphere, and the market reflects that same diversity. It's lined with shops ranging from traditional Korean crafts to modern, uniquely designed goods, making it a great place to browse clothing, accessories, furniture, and handicrafts in search of something distinctive. Because Itaewon is home to residents from many different countries, it also has a wealth of restaurants and cafes serving cuisine from around the world, offering a distinctive cultural experience.

신곡종합시장-2760228.name: Singok General Market
신곡종합시장-2760228.description: This small traditional market in Sinwol-dong, Yangcheon-gu, opened in 1976 and still has 30 shops in operation today. Retaining much of its old-market character, it has a warm, nostalgic atmosphere, selling produce, fruit, side dishes, and daily necessities. For nearby residents, it's a warm gathering place, almost like a neighborhood living room.

신영시장-서울-2611323.name: Sinyeong Market (Seoul)
신영시장-서울-2611323.description: Sinyeong Market, in Sinwol 1-dong, has plenty to enjoy, see, and eat. Beyond the fun of picking out cheap, fresh vegetables, fruit, and fish at the traditional market, it also offers a market cafe as a rest spot for coffee and tea. The New Zero Market is run jointly by the Yangcheon Regional Self-Sufficiency Center and the merchants' association, its community-based cafe helping both to energize the traditional market and to build a foundation for self-sufficiency among Yangcheon-gu's low-income residents. The Haneul Culture Center offers residents hobby activities and doubles as a gathering and hobby space for market customers, residents, and merchants.

가락농수산물종합도매시장-132215.name: Garak Agricultural & Fisheries Wholesale Market
가락농수산물종합도매시장-132215.description: Garak Market is Korea's largest agricultural and fisheries wholesale market. Since its produce and seafood markets first opened in 1985, it has grown into the country's premier agricultural and fisheries distribution hub. As additional direct-sale markets were added, it grew to its current scale, spanning roughly 164,000 pyeong with 17 market buildings. Handling around 2.3 million tons annually (roughly 7,500 tons a day) — the largest trading volume of any market in the world — it accounts for 49% of Seoul's demand and 40% of the total volume handled across Korea's 32 public wholesale markets, playing a central role in Korea's agricultural and fisheries distribution.

풍납도깨비시장-2758811.name: Pungnap Dokkaebi (Goblin) Market
풍납도깨비시장-2758811.description: Pungnap Dokkaebi Market is Songpa-gu's second-largest market after Seokchon Market. It started as a 'goblin market' — vendors laying out mats to sell goods by day and vanishing by evening — but has increasingly become a permanent fixture. Close to the Cheonho-dong Rodeo Street, it draws heavy foot traffic from local residents and young people, selling produce, seafood, meat, clothing, manufactured goods, and food, especially valued by Pungnap-dong residents. It offers parking and a grocery-delivery service. Nearby are the Pungnap Earthen Fortress and Pungnap Fortress Park, plus the Han River Park, making it a good stop for picking up food before an outing. Its low prices and wide range of tasty food keep it popular, with discount events and cultural programs running around holidays and each season.

마천시장-2759129.name: Macheon Market
마천시장-2759129.description: Macheon Market, also known as Macheon Jungang Market, is a traditional market — the only building-based traditional market in Songpa-gu with over 30 years of history. Located in the heart of a residential area of houses, apartments, and small shops, it's convenient for local residents, and market-renewal work is underway to revitalize it and improve customer convenience. It's home to a few well-known, budget-friendly spots, including a cauldron-fried chicken shop featured on TV and a well-known jokbal restaurant.

남대문-문구상가-985961.name: Namdaemun Stationery Market
남대문-문구상가-985961.description: Namdaemun Stationery Market is a street packed with shops specializing in stationery, toys, and packaging supplies. Known as 'Mungugol' ('stationery alley'), it's filled with clever, inventive stationery and toys, and draws many Japanese visitors interested in novel inventions. School supplies, fancy goods, office supplies, and art supplies are organized by building and floor, making one-stop shopping easy. Compared to other wholesale markets, more items here can be bought individually rather than in bulk. Some shops also run online stores.

동묘벼룩시장-2765213.name: Dongmyo Flea Market
동묘벼룩시장-2765213.description: Dongmyo Flea Market emerged in the late 1980s, and while its scale has shrunk relative to its reputation, it remains a destination for all kinds of rare and unusual finds. Its offerings span clothing, shoes, and wallets to watches, electronics, old books, and movie posters. Prices here are so low it can feel almost like everything's free. Surprisingly, the most popular category is secondhand clothing — merchants typically contract annually with apartment-complex recycling bins to buy up discarded clothes at 250–300 won per kilogram. Most items sell for around 1,000 won, though fur or leather can run into the tens of thousands of won, and designer pieces sometimes fetch over 100,000 won. As word has spread, bargain hunters travel from outside Seoul, and online shop owners come to buy in bulk. With around 250 street vendors setting up stalls, weekend afternoons are the best time to shop. It runs partially on weekdays and all day on weekends, about a 5-minute walk from Exit 3 of Dongmyo Station (Line 1).

충신시장-2759976.name: Chungsin Market
충신시장-2759976.description: Chungsin Market, in Chungsin-dong, Jongno-gu, is a roughly 50-year-old alley market situated between Dongdaemun Market and Daehangno. Before earning its formal name, it was simply a street-vendor alley, gradually gaining official market status as foot traffic increased. It has quieted down since the loss of the Naksan Apartments across the street, once its main customer base, but a growing number of fabric merchants unable to secure space in Dongdaemun Market have set up shop here, forming a new fabric-market street.

종로귀금속거리-132421.name: Jongno Jewelry Street
종로귀금속거리-132421.description: Jongno Jewelry Street is Korea's largest specialized jewelry district. Centered on Yeji-dong since the 1960s, it has expanded to cover the whole of Jongno, carrying a long tradition as a jewelry district. Getting off at Jongno 3-ga Station and heading down the alley beside the Danseongsa building leads straight to an alley lined with countless jewelry shops. With around 3,000 shops handling roughly 70% of Korea's total jewelry trade, business here is brisk. Jewelry can be bought for around 20–40% less than typical retail prices, drawing many engaged couples shopping for wedding jewelry. The Danseongsa building in particular dedicates floors 3 through basement 1 (of 11 total) to a jewelry center housing around 500 jewelry shops. It's also a popular shopping stop for international visitors.

상계중앙시장-2758191.name: Sanggye Central Market
상계중앙시장-2758191.description: Sanggye Central Market, in Sanggye 5-dong, Nowon-gu, opened in 2010. Its fate hung in the balance amid Seoul's redevelopment boom, which put pressure on many older markets in designated redevelopment zones. Following a market-modernization project — underground utility work, an arcade installation, and complete parking facilities — it's now a beloved neighborhood market for local residents. It's about a 5–7 minute walk from Exit 2 of Sanggye Station (Line 4).

대학천-책방거리-132202.name: Daehakcheon Bookstore Street
대학천-책방거리-132202.description: Daehakcheon Bookstore Street is a longstanding alley where new books can be bought cheaply, historically serving as a middleman connecting publishers and small bookstores nationwide. Unlike the widely known secondhand bookstore street along Cheonggyecheon, Daehakcheon's bookstore street isn't as well known to the general public — but it connects around 1,500 publishers and 3,000 bookstores across the country, with books from large and small stores alike often passing through its distributors. It mainly circulates book sets, standalone titles, and magazines, with a few shops specializing exclusively in martial-arts novels and comics. At its peak in the booming 1980s, it had over 80 shops; the rise of the internet and other distribution channels has thinned that number considerably, but the sheer volume of secondhand books still on hand makes for good browsing.

방신전통시장-2759655.name: Bangsin Traditional Market
방신전통시장-2759655.description: Bangsin Traditional Market is at the Banghwa-dong five-way intersection near Gimpo Airport; the sign at its entrance reads 'Bangsin Traditional Market.' An alley-style market with several branching paths, it has around 123 shops offering a range of food and an atmosphere reminiscent of an '80s-era market, including a popular jokbal shop with a regular line. It's accessible via Gaehwasan Station (Line 5) or Sinbanghwa Station (Line 9).

화곡본동시장-2753917.name: Hwagok Bon-dong Market
화곡본동시장-2753917.description: Established in 1969 and recognized as a Gangseo-gu traditional market in January 2004, this market was selected for a 'first steps to specialization' program in 2018 and as a cultural-tourism market in 2019. It mainly sells raw agricultural and fisheries goods, a small alley-style market with around 55 shops in operation. It has recently added online grocery ordering, with delivery available in Seoul and Goyang.

영풍문고-종각종로본점-1304864.name: Youngpoong Bookstore Jonggak-Jongno Main Branch
영풍문고-종각종로본점-1304864.description: Youngpoong Bookstore's Jonggak-Jongno main branch, first opened in Jongno in 1992, is a multi-purpose cultural space combining books, stationery, a convenience store, and MUJI. It carries everything from the latest bestsellers to classics, academic texts, children's books, and imported titles across every genre, all in one place. Beyond books, it also carries stationery, gifts, and music, letting visitors shop for several things at once. It also hosts reading events, book signings, lectures, and other cultural programs, making it an especially appealing spot for book lovers. Centrally located in Jongno, it's easy to reach and has become a well-visited cultural landmark.

독산동-우시장-2743857.name: Doksan-dong Cattle Market
독산동-우시장-2743857.description: Doksan-dong Cattle Market, in continuous operation since 1974, is a specialist meat market slaughtering cattle and pigs to supply top-quality meat wholesale and retail. Beef and pork byproducts are supplied directly to processed-food makers and restaurants, with fresh meat and byproducts sourced daily from 73 slaughterhouses nationwide. In 2012, the market's merchants formed the Doksan-dong Cattle Market Merchants Association, which now runs its own festivals and events and practices a spirit of giving, believing that shared happiness grows the more it's shared.

고분다리전통시장-2741571.name: Gobundari Traditional Market
고분다리전통시장-2741571.description: Gobundari Traditional Market sits between Cheonho Market and Amsa Market. 'Gobundari' comes from the native Korean reading of Gokgyo-ri, the old name for Cheonho-dong. Dadok Dadok, a Gangdong-style multi-purpose cultural space at the heart of the market, serves as a resident rest area, and there's also a mural photo zone worth stopping at.

도곡시장-2782194.name: Dogok Market
도곡시장-2782194.description: Dogok Market, in Yeoksam-dong, Gangnam-gu, grew up organically as merchants gradually began setting up shop here in the 1970s. It's an alley-style market with shops lined along both sides of the street connecting the main road to nearby apartments, drawing heavy foot traffic since the apartment-complex retail area feeds directly into it. As surrounding apartment complexes were built, the market grew large enough to once support hundreds of merchants.

논현-가구거리-132235.name: Nonhyeon Furniture Street
논현-가구거리-132235.description: Nonhyeon-dong Furniture Street is a stretch between Nonhyeon Station (Line 7) and Hakdong Station packed with furniture businesses. It's been a furniture district since 1970, earning its name from that time, and was officially designated a specialized furniture-culture street by Gangnam-gu in 1996. Visiting Nonhyeon-dong Furniture Street, you can find every kind of furniture in one place — wedding furniture, craft furniture, mother-of-pearl lacquerware, kitchen furniture, office furniture, interior pieces, and imports. Its classic lighting fixtures underscore its reputation as Korea's premier furniture district.

만리시장-2761474.name: Manri Market
만리시장-2761474.description: Manri Market, behind Seoul Station in Yongsan-gu, is a 3-story general-shopping-complex-style traditional market, opened in 1968 with a 50-year history. In the early 1970s it was mostly street vendors, gradually forming into shop stalls to become today's market. At the time, the Manri-dong market was large enough to draw shoppers from other parts of the city. But with the rise of big-box stores, it has retained the look and feel of an old-fashioned market seemingly frozen in time, leading to its designation as a Seoul Future Heritage site in 2016.

오류시장-2777893.name: Oryu Market
오류시장-2777893.description: Oryu Market, in Oryu-dong, Guro-gu, is a traditional market built in 1968. It once thrived with over 250 shops. Decline set in gradually from the 1990s onward, and today only a handful of shops remain — rice-cake shops, dried-goods sellers, sesame-oil shops, produce and seafood vendors, and a few restaurants. Oryu-gol Jumeokgogi, a grilled-meat restaurant in the market, remains a well-known local favorite.

개봉중앙시장-2758193.name: Gaebong Central Market
개봉중앙시장-2758193.description: Gaebong Central Market, in Gaebong-dong, Guro-gu, was laid out as a designated market site in 1976. It enjoyed its heyday from the late 1980s through the early 1990s, and mainly sells household goods and general merchandise. Gaebong Central Market holds an annual beer festival, alongside other events like a Lunar New Year prize giveaway.

방산-종합시장-132241.name: Bangsan General Market
방산-종합시장-132241.description: Bangsan General Market, in Bangsan-dong, Jung-gu, is a traditional market specializing in industrial materials. It carries everything from printing, packaging, bookbinding, and craft materials to stationery and fancy goods, all in one place. Its dense cluster of small shops makes price comparison and custom purchasing easy, and it's a beloved practical supply source for small business owners, designers, and creators. A traditional market that has stayed steadily popular thanks to reasonable prices and a wide range of goods.

면목시장-2759985.name: Myeonmok Market
면목시장-2759985.description: Myeonmok Market runs through a residential neighborhood in Myeonmok-dong, Jungnang-gu, opened in 1968 and boasting the longest history of any market in the district. Around 35 shops sit together in a single-story shop-building-style market; with the neighborhood's high residential density and many longtime residents, the traditional market remains popular. Well-known noodle, naengmyeon, and sundae-guk (blood-sausage soup) restaurants and shops selling a range of goods draw plenty of visitors.

강남고속터미널-혼수상가-132201.name: Gangnam Express Bus Terminal Bridal Goods Market
강남고속터미널-혼수상가-132201.description: The Gangnam Express Bus Terminal Bridal Goods Market mainly sells bedding, curtains, and silk fabric as a specialist market for wedding preparation and home decor. Bridal shops have operated here since 1982, with around 250 bedding shops and 100 curtain specialists, plus about 40 dedicated sewing workshops. The remaining shops sell silk, hanbok, embroidery, fabric, and suiting material related to wedding preparation. High-end bridal bedding sets here sell for around 20% below typical retail prices, drawing many merchants and consumers from outside Seoul who pass through the terminal — the market even offers free delivery nationwide via express bus.

구로-중앙유통단지-132420.name: Guro Central Distribution Complex
구로-중앙유통단지-132420.description: The Guro Central Distribution Complex is a specialized trading district built independently by small-business merchants dealing in machine tools, industrial supplies, and electronic and computer parts. Planning for the complex began in 1984, led by merchants from the Cheonggyecheon shopping district, and construction was completed in 1996, with businesses moving in soon after. Around 4,000 shops occupy 6 buildings, and the huge scale means an equally wide range of products. It houses shops and offices dealing in furniture, electronics, mobile phones, and more, alongside convenient amenities like restaurants, stationery shops, and pharmacies. The Guro Central Distribution Complex is Asia's largest industrial-supply complex, functioning as both a commercial and industrial hub.

을지로-철제가구거리-132238.name: Euljiro Steel Furniture Street
을지로-철제가구거리-132238.description: Euljiro Furniture Street is a place to buy furniture affordably. What sets it apart from other furniture districts is its focus on commercial furniture. As steel furniture's once-strong popularity has cooled in recent years, general furniture shops carrying a broader mix have moved in, along with a growing number of well-known furniture brand stores. Steel furniture, cheaper and sturdier than wood, remains popular for office-automation setups. General consumers buying just one or two pieces of office furniture can often save around 10% compared to a neighborhood furniture shop. Many shops here also run their own factories, offering the advantage of buying direct at lower prices — mostly small manufacturers producing a single category, like chairs or desks, while sourcing furniture they don't make themselves from other factories to sell alongside their own. The street connects to a nearby lighting district and carries a range of interior-related furniture too. If Hwanghak-dong is where secondhand furniture is sold, Euljiro is where new furniture is sold — though labeled 'commercial,' much of it works just as well at home, and there's plenty to see in one place.

후암시장-2760240.name: Huam Market
후암시장-2760240.description: Huam-dong, at the foot of Namsan near Seoul Station, is one of Seoul's oldest neighborhoods, and Huam Market carries 60 years of history, with around 50 shops still doing brisk business. Despite its long history, a 2015 facility-modernization project added an arcade, lighting, refreshed signage, and repaved flooring, making for a more comfortable shopping experience, with shop directories organized by category to help visitors quickly find what they need. It's an 8-minute walk from Seoul Station (Line 4 and the Airport Railroad).

망원월드컵시장-2907085.name: Mangwon World Cup Market
망원월드컵시장-2907085.description: Mangwon World Cup Market, about a 10-minute walk from Mangwon Station (Line 6), is a traditional Mangwon-dong market established in 1975 and still open daily. It was modernized into an arcade-covered market in 2006. Around 50 shops sell produce, meat, bunsik (Korean snack food), and household goods, with a notable number of wholesale-focused shops. Its proximity to Seoul World Cup Stadium, the surrounding park, and the Han River gives it good accessibility. Mangwon-dong World Cup Market runs from 10am to 10pm, and parking is available, making it convenient to visit.

광장시장-한복매장-1013527.name: Gwangjang Market Hanbok Shops
광장시장-한복매장-1013527.description: The hanbok shops of Gwangjang Market specialize in traditional Korean dress. They offer a range of designs to suit every taste, from custom-tailored hanbok to trendy everyday hanbok in a variety of designs and colors. High-quality fabric and careful craftsmanship come together at reasonable prices, and custom-order service lets customers design a hanbok that reflects their own personal style. With techniques passed down through generations of skilled artisans and designs full of character, these shops have become hugely popular with both international visitors and younger generations alike.

영등포청과시장-2764375.name: Yeongdeungpo Fruit Market
영등포청과시장-2764375.description: Yeongdeungpo Fruit Market, opened in 1984, is a market specializing in fruit. In the 1980s it was the largest fruit wholesale market serving the Gangseo and Bucheon area. Around 250 shops sell domestic and imported fruit both wholesale and retail. Good transit access and a dense surrounding residential area keep it steadily busy.

고척근린시장-2743854.name: Gocheok Neighborhood Market
고척근린시장-2743854.description: This market blends the feel of a traditional and a modern market. Covering roughly 2,200㎡ with around 70 shops, it's a small-to-mid-size market where Zero Pay is accepted almost everywhere. In business since 1971, it's easy to find near Gocheok Neighborhood Park. Its arcade roof makes shopping comfortable regardless of weather, and it hosts a range of events — flea markets, support drives for elderly residents living alone — to stay a market residents genuinely want to visit.

구로시장-2592394.name: Guro Market
구로시장-2592394.description: As large housing developments and the Guro Industrial Complex grew up along the Gyeongin national road in Guro-gu starting in 1962, the area needed a market, leading to this planned development. Guro Market was the first traditional market established in Guro-gu, initially forming around fabric shops, hanbok and clothing stores, then rice-cake shops, sesame-oil shops, and a food alley. Guro Market still has many hanbok shops today — female workers from the Guro Industrial Complex often wore hanbok on their trips home for holidays and bought it as gifts for family, and many bought their wedding trousseau here too. Its fabric shops thrived enough that people once ranked Guro Market alongside Namdaemun and Dongdaemun markets. As fabric and hanbok shops lined both sides of the market, the strip became known as the 'silk road.' A 2015 modernization project installed a weatherproof arcade and refreshed the signage. Guro Market, in a neighborhood with a large Chinese population, carries ingredients not typically found at other traditional markets, alongside traditional Korean food, side dishes, produce, seafood, and clothing at low prices. It's also known for its food — stone-ground handmade tofu, thick red-bean porridge, tteokbokki, kalguksu served with barley rice, and the 40-year-old Umma-son Noodle Factory all offer great flavor for the price.

신성종합시장-2774440.name: Sinseong General Market
신성종합시장-2774440.description: Sinseong General Market, at the Junggok intersection in Gwangjin-gu, is a small alley market laid out along a two-lane road. Though modest in scale, it has a butcher shop, fruit stands, a fish shop, and side-dish shops selling a range of ingredients, along with kalguksu, sundae-guk, dakgangjeong, and mandu shops offering plenty of good food.

간격-드로잉스페이스-2989027.name: Gan-gyeok Drawing Space
간격-드로잉스페이스-2989027.description: Drawing Space Gan-gyeok, in Mangwon-dong, is a studio built to make art easy and freely accessible in everyday life. It runs one-day classes as well as a monthly regular class with open access. One-day classes run 3 hours; the regular class, paid for in a 4-week block, includes one weekly teaching session, and members can also drop in freely for open studio hours to create outside of class. Running since 2019, it has taught a wide range of members using a variety of materials, holding a monthly outdoor sketching session, figure and portrait drawing activities, and a biweekly Saturday-evening croquis session.

수유시장-2741592.name: Suyu Market
수유시장-2741592.description: Opened in 1966, Suyu Market is one of Seoul's five great traditional markets, made up of a building-style market (Suyu Market) and alley-style markets (Suyu Traditional Market, Suyu Jaerae Market). Streets are color-coded to help shoppers find their way, with shop names posted at each entrance. It also offers a contactless grocery-delivery service bundling meat, fish, vegetables, snacks, and other food for delivery.

암사종합시장-2741602.name: Amsa General Market
암사종합시장-2741602.description: Amsa General Market, in Amsa 1-dong, Gangdong-gu, is a large, lively traditional market. Its dense cluster of shops makes it feel like a market that has everything. A covered arcade means shoppers can browse comfortably rain or shine. Fresh produce, seafood, tasty side dishes, and bunsik keep the market appetizing just to walk through, with market snacks like tteokbokki and fried food being an absolute must-try. It's also conveniently close to Amsa Station.

길동복조리시장-2741605.name: Gil-dong Bokjori Market
길동복조리시장-2741605.description: Gil-dong Bokjori Market is a warm traditional market where the everyday life and traditions of Gangdong-gu residents remain very much alive. A practical, well-rounded space, it brings together fresh produce, seafood, meat, side dishes, and convenience food all in one place. Every alley is packed with delicious food and household goods, adding to the pleasure of shopping here. A covered roof means shopping is possible without worry, rain or shine.

종로꽃시장-2739481.name: Jongno Flower Market
종로꽃시장-2739481.description: Jongno Flower Market is a healing pocket of the city, filled with flowers and plants year-round. With a wide range of fresh-cut flowers, potted plants, artificial flowers, and gardening supplies, it's a popular destination for flower lovers. Its especially wide selection of rare and oversized succulents, hard to find elsewhere, makes it particularly popular with succulent enthusiasts. Knowledgeable, friendly merchants make it easy for beginners to pick out flowers too. Bustling from early morning and filled with fresh floral scents, the market offers both atmosphere and sentiment in equal measure.

영등포전통시장-2764364.name: Yeongdeungpo Traditional Market
영등포전통시장-2764364.description: Opened in 1956 and standing in the same spot ever since, Yeongdeungpo Traditional Market is the largest and oldest traditional market in southwestern Seoul, with around 300 shops and 400 street stalls in business. Yeongdeungpo Market and Yeongdeungpo Station were once the bustling center of a secondary downtown that never seemed to sleep. Today, with large department stores and marts nearby, that old vibrancy has faded, but the market still retains much of its old traditional character. The passage running from the market's central intersection toward Yeongdeungpo Rotary handles mostly retail, while the surrounding area is home to wholesale shops selling tools and stationery. Since 2018, a night market has run along the market's central passage and Sundae Alley, focused on food trucks and street food, and has been gaining popularity by word of mouth.

포방터시장-2751441.name: Pobangteo Market
포방터시장-2751441.description: Pobangteo Market grew up on the site of a former artillery training ground built to defend the capital after the Japanese invasions of the 1590s, and later used to defend Seoul during the Korean War — 'Pobangteo' meaning 'artillery defense site,' which gave today's market its name. Surrounded by Bukhansan and Inwangsan, it's a small market with around 90 shops. It has served as a filming location for movies and dramas, and after one of its restaurants was featured on a TV program, the number of visitors to the market has steadily grown.

신창시장-2751420.name: Sinchang Market
신창시장-2751420.description: Sinchang Market, in Changdong, Dobong-gu, forms a local commercial district alongside the nearby Changdong Market. It offers a range of fresh produce and seafood at affordable prices, along with a variety of food and household goods. It also offers free delivery within Dobong-gu, making grocery shopping easy.

중곡제일골목시장-2751414.name: Junggok Jeil Alley Market
중곡제일골목시장-2751414.description: Junggok Jeil Alley Market, in Junggok-dong, Jungnang-gu, is a traditional market serving as an everyday shopping destination for local residents.
