It sells fresh produce and seafood, along with regional specialty products. In 2005, it became the first market in Korea to introduce shared coupons and its own gift certificates, and it runs a delivery service for residents' convenience. A recent modernization project has also made for a more pleasant shopping environment.

송화벽화시장-2741624.name: Songhwa Mural Market
송화벽화시장-2741624.description: Songhwa Mural Market, near Ujangsan Station (Line 5), traces its roots — though the exact date is unclear — to residents selling produce they harvested themselves at the old terminus of city bus route 66 to supplement their income. Famous artworks reproduced as murals are installed throughout the market, giving shoppers plenty to look at while they browse. It has been named an outstanding market by the city of Seoul two years running, and offers free home delivery for purchases.

수유중앙시장-2741594.name: Suyu Jungang Market
수유중앙시장-2741594.description: Suyu Jungang Market, in Gangbuk-gu, is one of Seoul's five outstanding markets as designated by the city. It began as a building-style market and later grew small alley shops around it into today's form. A community-oriented traditional market, it carries a wide range of goods across produce, vegetables, fruit, processed food, and clothing. Suyu Jungang Market is also known for its warm hospitality and affordable prices.

슬로우파마씨-3060917.name: Slow Farmacy
슬로우파마씨-3060917.description: Slow Farmacy is a warehouse-style plant interior shop in Seongsu-dong — a must-visit destination for plant lovers. Its modest space is densely packed with greenery. High ceilings hold beautifully arranged hanging plants trailing down from above. Look for marimo moss balls, first discovered in Hokkaido, tiny succulents, the 'pineapple cactus' (Faucaria tigrina), beginner-friendly ferns, and cacti in fascinating shapes. Its signature terrarium sets and plant specimens are also on display in person, including moss terrariums beautifully arranged with figurines, and specimens preserved in solution so they can be admired for years.

퇴계로-오토바이상가-132198.name: Toegye-ro Motorcycle Market
퇴계로-오토바이상가-132198.description: Toegye-ro Motorcycle Market is found by exiting Chungmuro Station across from Daehan Theater and walking along the sidewalk toward Toegye-ro 5-ga, where a steady procession of motorcycles marks the district. It's home to around 40 motorcycle dealers, roughly 10 shops selling accessories and parts, and about 10 repair shops. As a wholesale district, prices don't carry the usual retail markup even for individual buyers — motorcycles typically sell for 5–10% below standard retail, and parts prices vary with supply. Daelim Honda and Hyosung Suzuki models make up the bulk of what's sold here, and most shops also carry imported bikes from Japan and the U.S.

프레젠트모먼트-2784912.name: Present Moment
프레젠트모먼트-2784912.description: Present Moment sells vintage objects and dolls. Stepping inside feels like discovering Santa's secret workshop, hidden quietly within everyday life for years — instantly transporting visitors back to childhood. The shop is filled with pieces old enough to belong in a museum. It also stocks postcards and wrapping supplies, making it an ideal spot to prepare a gift.

남대문인삼시장-132225.name: Namdaemun Ginseng Market
남대문인삼시장-132225.description: Namdaemun Ginseng Market refers to the cluster of ginseng shops within Namdaemun Market, with around 20 shops facing each other across the market's central passage. Both wholesale and retail, these shops let ordinary consumers buy high-quality ginseng at low prices — typically 20–30% below standard retail, depending on the product — because they deal directly with the farmers and processors who grow and prepare the ginseng. The Namdaemun Ginseng Distribution Center, on the 2nd floor of the Namdaemun Theater building, sells fresh ginseng along with processed products like ginseng tea, powder, and candied ginseng, plus red ginseng products from the Korea Ginseng Corporation, honey, reishi mushroom, traditional teas, brown rice, adlay, and vegetable enzymes among other health foods. Fresh ginseng prices rise and fall each year depending on the harvest.

청량리청과물시장-2759652.name: Cheongnyangni Fruit & Vegetable Market
청량리청과물시장-2759652.description: Cheongnyangni Fruit & Vegetable Market, operating since 1958, is a produce wholesale market with a long history, home to around 170 thriving shops. Produce grown in Gyeonggi-do and Gangwon-do converges here at Cheongnyangni before being resold across the country. As a wholesale market, it's busiest from midnight through the early morning hours, and beyond fruit, many shops sell vegetables, seafood, and food just like a regular market. Its location near Cheongnyangni Station makes it easy to reach.

삼익패션타운-1019638.name: Samik Fashion Town
삼익패션타운-1019638.description: Samik Fashion Town is a wholesale-shopping tourist zone within Namdaemun Market, the mecca of Seoul shopping. Spanning 5 basement and 10 above-ground floors, it houses around 1,500 shops. Opened in 1985, it was built to shed Namdaemun Market's aging image with a large, comfortable, dedicated shopping complex. Samik Fashion Town brings together women's, children's, and men's clothing, shoes, and accessories all in one building, offering a convenient shopping environment not just for wholesalers but for budget-conscious shoppers browsing a traditional market. Its 1st-floor children's-clothing market and 6th-floor dedicated shoe department are especially well known. The 2nd and 3rd floors hold women's clothing, the 4th accessories and general goods, the 5th men's clothing, and floors 7–8 discount outlets for name brands. Hours vary by floor, so it's worth checking before visiting.

숭인시장-2741591.name: Sungin Market
숭인시장-2741591.description: Sungin Market, near Mia Sageori Station, is a traditional old-style market. It sells a range of food and household goods at low prices, closely tied to the everyday lives of local residents. Its long history and warm, welcoming atmosphere leave a lasting impression on visitors. It's known for its tasty street food — bunsik, fried snacks, jokbal — and especially for its tteokbokki.

청오가방도매상가-132207.name: Cheongo Bag Wholesale Market
청오가방도매상가-132207.description: Known as Cheongo Bag Wholesale Market, this complex sits administratively in Jongno 5-ga and, together with nearby bag shops, is often referred to collectively as the Cheonggyecheon bag market. Shops that had thrived around Jongno 5-ga and Cheonggyecheon since the 1960s relocated to the Cheongo Building, with clothing shops taking the 1st and 2nd floors and bag-component wholesalers filling the basement and 3rd–4th floors. The Cheongo Bag Market not only wholesales its own factory-made original bag designs to retailers nationwide, but some shops also supply bags directly to department stores. While some shops carry a mix of bag types, many are specialty shops focused on just one or two categories — handbags, briefcases, luggage, school bags. Beyond kindergarten and after-school bag specialists, there are also shops dedicated to small items like fabric lunch bags.

대신시장-2753117.name: Daesin Market
대신시장-2753117.description: Daesin Market, in Singil-dong, Yeongdeungpo-gu, is a traditional market. Opened in 1965, it's a building-style market with nearly 60 years of history. Singil-dong faces Yeouido across the Saetgang side channel; the area was once a key transit point, home to a ferry crossing into Seoul, drawing people and goods that naturally gave rise to a market. Today, with dense apartment complexes and housing nearby, it draws steady foot traffic, continuing to serve as a warm, welcoming traditional market.

정릉아리랑시장-2758176.name: Jeongneung Arirang Market
정릉아리랑시장-2758176.description: This alley market sits in Jeongneung, one of Seoul's classic hillside neighborhoods, also known as Arirang Pass. Jeongneung Arirang Market takes its name from a Korean film that used the area as a filming location, and is also known as Arirang Alley Market. Since a doenjang-stew restaurant, a jijim pancake shop, and a handmade Hamburg-steak restaurant in the market were featured on an SBS variety show in 2019, it has become known as a market full of great restaurants, drawing many visitors. It's near the UNESCO World Heritage site Jeongneung and Heungcheonsa Temple, both worth visiting together.

노량진수산물도매시장-132216.name: Noryangjin Fisheries Wholesale Market
노량진수산물도매시장-132216.description: Noryangjin Fish Market traces its roots to 1927, when it began near today's Seoul Station on Uiju-ro — boasting over 90 years of history as Korea's largest inland seafood wholesale market. The wholesale market was rebuilt in Noryangjin in 1971, and in 2002 the fisheries cooperative Suhyup, working to boost fishermen's income and develop the industry, acquired the market and carried out a modernization project, reinventing it as Korea's premier seafood wholesale market where commerce and culture coexist. Handling 50% of the greater Seoul area's seafood trade, Noryangjin Fisheries Wholesale Market moves around 250–300 tons of seafood a day. Since prices are set by the day's incoming supply, it's worth checking auction prices on the website in advance; retail prices generally run 10–20% above auction prices. With wholesale and retail intermingled, the auctions starting at 1am offer plenty to watch — the 3am live-fish auction, in particular, captures the energetic spirit of the pre-dawn market and its infectious sense of vitality.

서울-중부시장-132217.name: Jungbu Market, Seoul
서울-중부시장-132217.description: Jungbu Market, in Jung-gu, Seoul, is a traditional market offering a wide range of goods and food. Its dense cluster of shops selling food, clothing, and daily necessities makes it a well-known destination for both shopping and eating. It's especially known for affordable dried-goods staples used in banchan cooking — laver, seaweed, yellow corvina, anchovies, dried squid, dried pollack, and dried filefish. The market's lively atmosphere and connection with local residents also offer a special glimpse of old Seoul.

세브도르-132218.name: Cave d'Or
세브도르-132218.description: Seoul's first dedicated liquor specialty shop opened its doors in September 1990. Cave d'Or has since become well known among drink enthusiasts. It displays and sells over 1,000 rare bottles — domestic folk liquor, soju, beer, wine, and spirits, alongside wine, whisky, cognac, gin, and vodka from Eastern and Western Europe, the U.S., Japan, China, Taiwan, and the former Soviet Union. The shop uses fixed pricing, generally cheaper than typical retail shops or department stores. Sales typically run after peak holiday seasons like Chuseok or Lunar New Year, though bulk group purchases can get below fixed pricing even during peak season.

밀리오레-동대문점-273758.name: Migliore Dongdaemun
밀리오레-동대문점-273758.description: Migliore Dongdaemun is a one-stop shopping destination where everything can be found in a single space. Dongdaemun's traditional market stretches from Jongno 5-ga Station to Dongdaemun subway station. In recent years, as the area has modernized, large fashion malls like Freya Town, Doota, and Migliore have sprung up. Dongdaemun Migliore combines the market's strengths — fashion clothing, a wide range of products, and low prices — with a department store's advantages — a modern building and a range of amenities. From B2 to the 9th floor, it houses every kind of fashion item: imported luxury goods, children's wear, maternity wear, women's and men's clothing, fashion accessories, traditional craft souvenirs, hanbok, and shoes. The 9th floor has a food court, offering plenty to eat and see. It's a 5-minute walk from Exit 14 of Dongdaemun History & Culture Park Station (Lines 2, 4, 5). Its proximity to Cheonggyecheon and Dongdaemun (Heunginjimun Gate) draws many domestic and international visitors.

롯데백화점-건대스타시티점-2979848.name: Lotte Department Store Konkuk Univ. StarCity Branch
롯데백화점-건대스타시티점-2979848.description: Offering something new and enjoyable every day, Lotte Department Store's Konkuk Univ. StarCity branch is a hip destination full of things to do. It carries a range of brands — Kyobo Book Centre on B1, Kangol and Discovery on the 5th floor, Nike on the 7th, Uniqlo on the 8th, and Hanssem Rehaus on the 9th. With plenty of restaurants as well, it's also a great spot for a date.

메종쥬-성수-부티끄-2996472.name: Maison JU Seongsu Boutique
메종쥬-성수-부티끄-2996472.description: Maison JU Seongsu Boutique's fragrances offer trendy, exceptional quality through a flexible reinterpretation of established conventions. Its lively designs, awash in varied color, carry a vintage pop-art sensibility, and the boutique features creative collaborations with leading French master perfumers of the new generation. Maison JU is designed for those seeking distinctive fragrances not easily found elsewhere. A range of bottle sizes lets visitors purchase and sample scents suited to their needs.

우이시장-2741590.name: Ui Market
우이시장-2741590.description: Opened in 1962, Ui Market is Gangbuk-gu's oldest market, offering a taste of the warm, nostalgic charm of an old-fashioned traditional market.

아이파크몰-고척점-3428365.name: IPARK Mall Gocheok Branch
아이파크몰-고척점-3428365.description: IPARK Mall Gocheok Branch, in Gocheok-dong, Guro-gu, is a mixed-use shopping mall — the second location of HDC IPARK Mall, opened in December 2022. Spanning basement level 3 to the 2nd floor, it houses a range of shops as a lifestyle center including Costco, a food court, and children's play facilities.

현대카드-바이닐앤플라스틱-2711768.name: Hyundai Card Vinyl & Plastic
현대카드-바이닐앤플라스틱-2711768.description: Hyundai Card Vinyl & Plastic sells over 10,000 vinyl records and CDs, and doubles as a hands-on space to see, hear, and touch real physical music rather than streaming. The thrill of digging through stacks of vinyl and CDs, the analog sound of a turntable and cassette player that turns even the faintest surface noise into music, and the joy of discovering new genres and artists through listening stations tucked throughout the space — Vinyl & Plastic is a space to fully immerse in and own the music that has otherwise become just background noise in everyday life.

모자이크-2989582.name: Mosaic
모자이크-2989582.description: Mosaic is a record shop specializing mainly in secondhand vinyl. A gathering place for people looking to find their own musical taste, it updates its online and offline shop with 150–200 newly stocked LPs every Sunday — staff personally listen through every LP and write a one-line review, reflecting a genuine devotion to music. Custom vinyl pressing is also available. Visitors can learn how to operate a turntable or get record recommendations across genres in-store, making it approachable even for beginners. The 2nd floor, a cozy attic-like space, serves hand-drip coffee, mint tea, and black mint tea. The space is fairly small, so weekday visits are recommended.

사당시장-2759106.name: Sadang Market
사당시장-2759106.description: Sadang Market, opened in 1987, sits along the main road between Namseong Station (Line 7) and the Isu Station intersection. A 3-story building-style general shopping complex, it has a mart, discount household-goods store, clothing shops, general goods, and clinics — a different feel from an alley-style traditional market, but still a neighborhood market covering everyday essentials. Clinics occupy the 2nd and 3rd floors. Despite the building's age, an on-site management office keeps it clean, and it continues to draw a steady stream of visitors.

종이잡지클럽-2940925.name: Print Magazine Club
종이잡지클럽-2940925.description: Print Magazine Club is, quite literally, a space to read and talk about print magazines. Its staff hand-select specialty and independent magazines from Korea and abroad, serving planners always in need of fresh ideas, and anyone looking to broaden their knowledge and interests or seeking a higher caliber of leisure — a space for both exploration and escape. The club runs both online and offline memberships. Online members receive that month's selected magazine by mail and free access to gatherings; offline members get unlimited use of the physical space, through a visit-and-seating pass.

롯데몰-김포공항점-1535690.name: Lotte Mall Gimpo Airport Branch
롯데몰-김포공항점-1535690.description: Lotte Mall Gimpo Airport Branch is Korea's first and largest lifestyle-format complex combining shopping, a hotel, entertainment, and a theme park. Covering 195,000㎡, it's Korea's largest mall of its kind, spanning 5 basement and 9 above-ground floors. Around the building's exterior is Sky Park, a 129,000㎡ green, ecological park, and the top of the department store's 6th floor has an observation deck where visitors can watch planes take off and land. It's easily accessed via Lines 5 and 9 and the Airport Railroad, all connected through underground passages.

랩포터리-2989593.name: Lab Pottery
랩포터리-2989593.description: Lab Pottery is a space where anyone can get comfortable working with clay. True to its name ('ceramics laboratory'), it runs a range of pottery-craft programs. From ordinary ceramic bowls to interior objects reflecting your own ideas and taste, the appeal of ceramic craft is that you can make almost anything you can imagine. Completing a single piece takes 3–4 weeks across six stages — shaping, drying, bisque firing, decorating, glazing, and the final firing — but the reward is worth the wait. Lab Pottery's programs are split into one-day classes and a regular course. One-day classes split into a 'wheel class' using a pottery wheel and a 'hand-building class' using coiling technique, capped at 6 individuals or 15 for groups, running about 1 hour 30 minutes. With 1-on-1 guidance designed for beginners to follow easily, it's approachable for elementary schoolers, seniors, and international visitors alike.

코오롱스포츠-솟솟618점-2943363.name: Kolon Sport Sotsot618 Branch
코오롱스포츠-솟솟618점-2943363.description: Sotsot618 is an outdoor lifestyle shop run by Kolon Sport, offering its own rental service. Located at Cheonggyesan Ipgu Station on the Sinbundang Line, it's easy to reach, and rentals help ease the cost burden of buying gear. One corner is filled with colorful thread for a name-tag-making experience — order your preferred text and emoji, and staff will make a custom tag on the spot, letting you pick the thread color, ring color, and font yourself. The finished, hand-stitched tag can be attached to a hiking backpack or trekking pole. A cafe runs behind the shop too, making it a great spot for a cool coffee after a hike.

신사상가-2752555.name: Sinsa Market
신사상가-2752555.description: Sinsa Market is found by walking from Exit 1 of Apgujeong Station toward the Apgujeong Hyundai Apartments, with around 80 shops. Completed in 1976, it hasn't undergone reconstruction or remodeling since, retaining nearly its original form as a classic old-style traditional market. A 40-year-old tteokbokki shop near the market's rear entrance is well known.

롯데몰-은평점-3447174.name: Lotte Mall Eunpyeong Branch
롯데몰-은평점-3447174.description: Lotte Mall Eunpyeong Branch, in Eunpyeong-gu, is a large mixed-use mall offering a range of shopping, dining, and leisure facilities. Its main amenities include a mix of brand stores, a food court, Hi-Mart, a bowling alley, a futsal field, Lotte Mart, and Lotte Cinema, with easy access by public transit. A place to enjoy shopping and leisure together in one spot.

작은공간-2783356.name: Jageun Gonggan (Small Space) Tteokbokki
작은공간-2783356.description: Jageun Gonggan is a jeukseok-tteokbokki (tabletop-cooked tteokbokki) specialist near Eungwang Girls' High School by Yangjae Station, in Gangnam-gu. A beloved tteokbokki spot in front of Eungwang Girls' High School for over 40 years, its walls and chairs are covered edge to edge with decades of graffiti left by generations of alumni, preserving those memories intact. The tteokbokki sauce comes in a choice of standard gochujang seasoning or jjajang (black bean sauce). The basic set includes broth with ramen noodles, jjolmyeon noodles, rice cakes, fish cakes, egg, and dumplings, with extra add-ins available. Cooked tableside as you eat, the flavor deepens the longer it simmers. Don't forget the classic finishing move — fried rice made with the leftover tteokbokki sauce. The dining room is fairly small; takeout and delivery are available.

으뜸횟집-2753157.name: Eutteum Hoetjip (Sashimi Restaurant)
으뜸횟집-2753157.description: Eutteum Hoetjip, near Gubeun-dari Station in Gangdong-gu, is a sashimi restaurant that lives up to its name ('the best'), holding firmly to the fundamentals. Every step — selecting fresh seafood, preparing it, and plating it — is handled cleanly and methodically. The texture and umami of the sashimi really come through, letting diners fully appreciate the charm of seasonal fish that changes with the time of year. Fresh ingredients, generous portions, and reasonable prices have made it a popular spot known for great value. Eutteum Hoetjip's real strength is its seafood course menu, letting diners enjoy a range of fresh seafood dishes as a full course rather than as individual à la carte items, for a richer, more varied meal.

청와옥-본점-2758163.name: Cheongwaok Main Branch
청와옥-본점-2758163.description: Cheongwaok's main branch, in Songpa-gu, is a sundae-guk specialist known for its striking blue-tiled-roof gate. Sundae-guk might bring to mind a modest, no-frills restaurant, but this one has the feel of an upscale traditional Korean dining hall. Its signature dishes are sundae (Korean blood sausage) and sundae-guk, plus a hinoki-served set menu that comes with boiled meat. It's across from the Soma Museum of Art at Olympic Park, at Exit 3 of Hanseong Baekje Station (Line 9).

오만지아-2758130.name: Omangia
오만지아-2758130.description: Omangia, in the UN Village area of Hannam-dong, is an Italian restaurant run by owner-chef Hwang Dong-hwi, a Grano alum. Featured in the Michelin Guide Seoul for three consecutive years (2018, 2019, 2020) and on the pasta episode of a popular Korean food TV show, it's also known for its stylish entrance and interior design and open kitchen. The restaurant is located in the basement.

풍년뼈다귀해장국-2758158.name: Pungnyeon Ppyeodagwi Haejangguk
풍년뼈다귀해장국-2758158.description: This restaurant in Seokchon-dong, Songpa-gu, specializes in ppyeo-haejangguk (pork-bone hangover soup). Open 24 hours, it serves generous bowls of well-simmered pork spine and thoroughly boiled ugeoji (dried cabbage leaves) in a large earthenware pot. It offers two menu items, ppyeo-haejangguk and ugeoji-tang, with the cabbage leaves piled atop the pork bones being especially popular. The restaurant's walls are covered edge to edge with messages left by customers. It's across the street from Gaksan Elementary School near Songpa Station (Helio City) on Line 8.

삼원가든-132892.name: Samwon Garden
삼원가든-132892.description: Samwon Garden, in Seoul, is a traditional Korean restaurant known by word of mouth for its scale — seating around 1,200 — and the quality of its food. Enjoying grilled meat in a traditional setting, it's a place where domestic and international dignitaries have been entertained, major companies have held important meetings, and residents have gathered to mark big celebrations. With around 40 private rooms, it can accommodate a wide range of dining groups, and also hosts outdoor garden weddings, corporate events, and banquets. Its signature dishes include traditional seasoned galbi and bulgogi, alongside Korean beef yukhoe, stir-fried live octopus, and grilled eel. Praised for striking an elegant balance between popular appeal and refinement in Korean barbecue culture, Samwon Garden delivers top service through premium ingredients and a skilled grilling team. Its traditional landscaped garden, offering a place to relax, is another point of pride.

썬더버드-청담점-2623187.name: Thunderbird Cheongdam Branch
썬더버드-청담점-2623187.description: Thunderbird, in Cheongdam-dong, proposes a better lifestyle through healthy ingredients and recipes. Its menu of salads, noodles, and rice bowls makes wholesome ingredients taste even better, alongside a range of vegan options, so everyone can enjoy a clean, satisfying meal. Its location near Apgujeong Rodeo Station makes it easy to reach, and its spacious, comfortable interior offers visitors a relaxing atmosphere.

제일콩집-402888.name: Jeil Kongjip (Bean Restaurant)
제일콩집-402888.description: Jeil Kongjip, in Gongneung-dong, Nowon-gu, is a longstanding restaurant specializing in soybean dishes. Using only domestic soybeans sourced from Hongcheon, Gangwon-do, ground by hand with a millstone before serving, its dishes have an especially rich, nutty, clean flavor. Grinding only as much as needed each day also keeps every dish fresh — part of the secret to its top-quality flavor. Its menu includes a range of soybean dishes: handmade tofu, bean-paste stew, cheonggukjang (fermented soybean stew), sundubu (soft tofu), tofu stew, and kongguksu (cold soybean noodle soup). In summer, its rich, clean-tasting kongguksu is easily its most popular dish. The rustic, homestyle cooking, clean and simple, evokes the comforting flavors of a mother's home cooking.

도일처-678899.name: Doilcheo
도일처-678899.description: Doilcheo, near the entrance to Gimpo Airport, is a Chinese restaurant that opened in 1966. Its signature dish is dongpo-yuk, pork belly simmered whole with star anise for 4 hours and served with bok choy and steamed flower buns. Beyond dongpo-yuk, it offers distinctive dishes like gochu ggongbau-gabeo (a sweet-and-sour cuttlefish dish resembling sweet-and-sour pork) and lapungi-malgi, chicken breast and vegetables rolled, fried, and tossed in a special chili sauce. Alongside traditional Chinese dishes, it also offers fusion dishes like stir-fried cuttlefish with chili peppers and cashews.

한미옥-2870750.name: Hanmiok
한미옥-2870750.description: Hanmiok started at its Seolleung location, gained popularity for its chadol gujeolpan (thin-sliced beef brisket platter) and samhap (three-way beef combination), and expanded to a Cheongdam branch near Exit 1 of Seolleung Station (Line 9, Suin-Bundang Line). Hanmiok pursues both the value and global reach of Korean cuisine through cooking with traditional cauldron lids and refined presentation. Its spacious interior has table configurations for varying group sizes plus private rooms, making it suitable for group events and family gatherings. Signature dishes include chaekkeut deungsim samhap (beef striploin combination), the Hanmiok set, chadol gujeolpan, and hanu mulhoe guksu (cold raw-beef noodle soup).

명문막국수-2495458.name: Myeongmun Makguksu
명문막국수-2495458.description: Myeongmun Makguksu is known for makguksu, a classic summer specialty noodle dish. It serves buckwheat makguksu and buckwheat-perilla kalguksu, alongside a range of other buckwheat dishes. Its sliced boiled pork, a nice pairing with the noodles, is similar to suyuk and can be enjoyed either alongside the noodles or dipped in the accompanying salted shrimp. From October through March, it also serves tofu dishes.

송원-133836.name: Songwon
송원-133836.description: Songwon, near Dongguk University Station in Jung-gu, is a Korean restaurant that has held its ground for over 40 years. A charcoal-grill specialist, it serves distinctively flavored soy-marinated galbi and bulgogi seasoned with over 20 natural ingredients. The menu includes yangnyeom galbi, bulgogi, a cauldron-rice set meal, galbitang, and dolsot bibimbap. Private rooms are available, making it a good spot for group gatherings. Centrally located and well used by locals, it's also easy for tourists to reach given its convenient transit access.

브래디스커피-2815891.name: Brady's Coffee
브래디스커피-2815891.description: Tucked into the far edge of Yeonnam-dong, this cozy cafe spans two connected floors in a small space, with the 1st floor as a bar, the 2nd as a cafe, and a 3rd-floor space as well. Its vintage interior gives the feeling of stepping into a cafe abroad. Every seat gets plenty of natural light, making it easy to get a great photo almost anywhere in the shop. All disposables used in the shop are made from eco-friendly materials, letting visitors enjoy their coffee with the environment in mind. The menu includes coffee drinks like Einspänner and various ades.

사운드키친-2858244.name: Sound Kitchen
사운드키친-2858244.description: Sound Kitchen, in Mapo-gu, is well known for its poke bowls. It serves warm salad bowls of super rice — made from brown rice, oats, and quinoa — topped with salmon poke or sous-vide chicken breast. Its mushroom bulgogi hummus bowl, blending clean hummus with sweet-savory bulgogi, is another recommended dish. Beyond salad bowls, the menu also includes mozzarella eggplant-mushroom rice, potato gratin, and chili tomato konjac tteokbokki.

다과상사-2814836.name: Dagwa Sangsa
다과상사-2814836.description: Dagwa Sangsa, in Yongsan-gu, is a vintage-style dessert cafe. Its signature drinks are a classic americano and cafe latte, with a choice of three coffee-bean profiles. Its vanilla bean latte, made by scraping real vanilla bean and steeping it in milk, and its salty caramel latte — a sweet-salty combination of brown sugar, cream, and a finishing touch of salt — are both popular. A range of desserts is also available, and Dagwa Sangsa's coffee beans can be purchased online.

백년가게-창성옥-2608909.name: [Century-Old Shop] Changseongok
백년가게-창성옥-2608909.description: [Selected as a 'Century-Old Shop' by the Ministry of SMEs and Startups in 2018] Now run by its third generation, Changseongok is known for its rich ppyeo jeongol (bone hot pot), made with meat-heavy pork bones and hearty dried cabbage, and its haejangguk (hangover soup) with rich broth and blood sausage. Its fried eggs, sold since it first opened over 70 years ago, are also a must-try. Open from 6am to 2am, it serves meals late into the night. Designated a Seoul Future Heritage site and featured on numerous food TV programs, it's known as one of Yongsan's three great haejangguk restaurants.

서강팔경-2733861.name: Seogang Palgyeong
서강팔경-2733861.description: Just inside the entrance, an old Hwangpo sailboat that once plied the Han River and marble flooring evoking the river itself set the tone, with a range of Han River-inspired interior touches throughout. By day the restaurant serves a variety of drinks; by night, whisky, wine, beer, and cocktails against a Han River backdrop. From the rooftop Sky Garden observation deck, views stretch to Namsan in the east, the Sangam World Cup Stadium and Haneul Park in the west, Namsan again to the south, and Bukhansan and Inwangsan to the north.

할머니의-레시피-2895145.name: Grandma's Recipe
할머니의-레시피-2895145.description: Grandma's Recipe, in Seongsu-dong, is near Exit 5 of Seoul Forest Station (Suin-Bundang Line). Set behind Seoul Forest, it has a great view through its windows. The overall feel is modern and clean. Its menu includes gochujang bulgogi, mushroom bulgogi, ssambap set, bibim bulgogi set, hanu tteokgalbi set, grilled fish set, gomppyeo-guk (bone soup), soy-marinated crab, and Ganggyeong jeotgal bibimbap, among others — a popular destination for well-crafted Korean food.

두레유-2814408.name: Dureyu
두레유-2814408.description: Dureyu is a modern Korean cuisine dining venue reinterpreting traditional Korean food in a fine-dining style. Owner-chef Yoo Hyun-soo trained across a variety of restaurant styles both in Korea and abroad, and served as head chef at the Korean Embassy in London during the 2012 London Olympics, overseeing Olympic-related luncheons and dinners — showcasing the beauty of Korean cuisine to the world on a global stage.

비올레타-2870210.name: Violeta
비올레타-2870210.description: Violeta, in Geumho-dong, Seongdong-gu, is a muffin specialty cafe that opened in 2018. Rather than standard flour, it uses only organic, high-quality ingredients for a healthier treat — flour, sugar, honey, and powders are all organic. Its handmade muffins, in a range of flavors, have a soft texture and rich flavor that brightens the mood. The shop's interior, rather than the cynical edge common to trendy cafes, is decorated in warm wood tones, giving the whole space a cozy, welcoming feel.

인더베이글-2819962.name: In the Bagel
인더베이글-2819962.description: In the Bagel, in Hoegi-dong, Dongdaemun-gu, is a favorite for authentic-style handmade bagels made with natural ingredients, low in calories, fat, and sugar. Located near Kyung Hee University, it also serves salads and sandwiches alongside its bagels. A range of handmade cream cheeses pair well with the bagels. Ordering with a drink comes with a discount, making it good value.

스시초심-2833461.name: Sushi Chosim
스시초심-2833461.description: Sushi Chosim, in Sanggye-dong, Nowon-gu, is a sushi omakase restaurant. It offers high-quality sushi omakase at reasonable prices for both lunch and dinner. Each dish comes with an explanation, and the restaurant operates on a reservation-only basis, letting diners enjoy their meal in a relaxed atmosphere — a good choice for a special occasion with family or a partner. The menu includes octopus, giant amberjack, grilled Spanish mackerel, and more.

모래내곱창-2900401.name: Moraenae Gopchang
모래내곱창-2900401.description: Moraenae Gopchang, in the restaurant alley across from Myongji University, serves delicious pan-seared vegetable gopchang (grilled beef/pork intestines), sundae-gopchang, and al-gopchang. It's a generous, good-value way to enjoy chewy gopchang. Signature dishes include stir-fried vegetable gopchang, stir-fried sundae gopchang, white al-gopchang, and red al-gopchang — a great place to try if you're curious about gopchang for the first time. Be sure to finish with the fried rice cooked in the leftover gopchang drippings, a beloved Korean dessert-course move. Dine-in orders require a minimum of 2 servings; takeout is available starting at 1 serving.

토라카츠-2869851.name: Tora Katsu
토라카츠-2869851.description: Tora Katsu, near Dongduk Women's University in Sangwolgok-dong, Seongbuk-gu, specializes in Jeju black-pork tonkatsu. The menu has four options: mixed, sirloin, premium sirloin, and tenderloin. The mixed katsu, letting diners try both the tender tenderloin and crispy sirloin cutlets, is the most popular dish. The curry served alongside the katsu is also popular. Using Jeju-raised black pork keeps the meat free of any gamey taste.

송이네-2833276.name: Songi-ne
송이네-2833276.description: Songi-ne, in Mangwon-dong, Mapo-gu, is a modest tteokbokki shop inside Mangwon Market with just a narrow bar counter and one table for three. Its tteokbokki has a moderate spice level and a generous amount of broth. Beyond tteokbokki, it also serves several types of hearty gimbap and fried snacks. Its gimbap comes in a range of varieties, from basic vegetable gimbap to more unusual options like fried-squid gimbap and scallion-doenjang gimbap. A good stop while exploring Mangwon Market.

후암편백-2808041.name: Huam Pyeonbaek
후암편백-2808041.description: Huam Pyeonbaek, in Huam-dong, Yongsan-gu, specializes in steamed dishes using Iberico black pork — considered one of the world's four great delicacies — cooked in a hinoki cypress frame to healthily render out excess fat. Beyond the hinoki-steamed dish, it also serves Iberico hot-plate dishes, shabu-shabu, mille-feuille nabe, and kimchi udon. Since everything is steamed, it also works well as a health-conscious meal, with a light, clean flavor rather than heavy seasoning.

와가리피순대-2807930.name: Wagari Pisundae
와가리피순대-2807930.description: Wagari Pisundae's main branch, in Yongdu-dong, Dongdaemun-gu near Sinseol-dong Station, is known for its generous pi-sundae (blood sausage made with a pig-intestine casing filled with blood and vegetables). Its signature dishes are pi-sundae and a sundae assortment platter including offal like small intestine and badger meat. Its spicy sundae-guk also makes for a solid meal. Beyond sundae-guk, the menu includes sulguk (a drinking-soup dish), doganitang (ox knee soup), and stir-fried octopus.

진성한우곱창-2821765.name: Jinseong Hanwoo Gopchang
진성한우곱창-2821765.description: Jinseong Hanwoo Gopchang, in Garak-dong, Songpa-gu, is a grilled-gopchang specialist serving same-day-slaughtered fresh gopchang alongside aged garlic sauce and house-made scallion kimchi, mustard-leaf kimchi, and baby radish kimchi. Its signature dish is Korean-beef gopchang packed with rich gop (intestine fat), alongside grilled Korean-beef daechang (large intestine) and makchang (abomasum). A rice dish finished on the grill with diced radish kimchi after the meat course is a popular closer, and its clean-tasting anchovy noodles are also well known.

댓잎갈비-본점-2859951.name: Daetnip Galbi Main Branch
댓잎갈비-본점-2859951.description: Daetnip Galbi's main branch, in Bogwang-dong, Yongsan-gu, is a grilled-galbi specialist near Exit 1 of Hannam Station (Gyeongui-Jungang Line). Though compact, it has its own parking lot and offers valet parking, with a public lot also available next door. The restaurant feels like a remodeled traditional house repurposed for dining. An outdoor garden offers seating for waiting guests. Inside, three walls are floor-to-ceiling windows, with both standard and floor-seating tables on a wooden floor; the 2nd floor has a Han River view through the windows too. The menu features daetnip galbi and daetnip chueotang (loach soup). The galbi comes pre-seared for a quick, easy meal, cooked over real charcoal. The chueotang comes with tofu and thin wheat noodles, along with garlic, cheongyang chili, and perilla powder to mix in. Side dishes come with free refills. All menu items are available to go.

성북동면옥집-2873293.name: Seongbuk-dong Myeonokjip
성북동면옥집-2873293.description: Seongbuk-dong Myeonokjip, in Seongbuk-dong, Seongbuk-gu, has been featured on TV multiple times. Its signature dishes are wang-galbijjim (braised beef short ribs) and naengmyeon. The braised galbi comes in three portion sizes — jin, seon, mi. Its seasoning overall isn't overly strong, making it approachable and comfortable to eat. The menu also includes wang-galbitang, hoe-naengmyeon, five-color mandu, sagol mandu-guk, boiled meat (suyuk), and an assorted jeon platter.

방목-2876684.name: Bangmok
방목-2876684.description: Bangmok, in Dongsomun-dong 2-ga, Seongbuk-gu, is a well-known grilled-meat restaurant near Hansung University. True to its location near a university, it offers generous, high-quality meat and meals at affordable prices. Its signature dish is juicy pork neck (mokssal), alongside pork belly and pork skin. Staff grill the meat tableside, making for an easy, relaxed meal. Its tangy kimchi-roll noodles, served alongside the meat, are also popular.

닭내장집-2873449.name: Dak Naejangjip
닭내장집-2873449.description: Dak Naejangjip, in Moraenae Market in Namgajwa-dong, Seodaemun-gu, is a chicken-offal specialist with the unmistakable feel of an old-school neighborhood joint. Chicken offal is the main draw, but the sizzling pan of chicken feet bubbling away right at the entrance also looks irresistible. After finishing the chicken offal, the fried rice made from the leftovers is a treat in itself. Alongside its role as an evening drinking spot, it also serves a chicken-offal set meal at lunch, drawing plenty of midday visitors too.

송가네감자탕-2778422.name: Songga-ne Gamjatang
송가네감자탕-2778422.description: Songga-ne Gamjatang, opened in 1988, is in Yeonnam-dong, Mapo-gu. Featured on TV multiple times, it's well known among locals. Its signature dish is gamjatang (pork-bone and potato stew). It also serves bossam and ppyeo-haejangguk. Open from morning to the early hours the next day on weekdays and 24 hours on weekends, it's available almost any time. The restaurant is close to Hongik Univ. Station (Line 2), near the Gyeongui Line Book Street, the Hongdae club district, and Sangsu-dong's cafe street.

르프리크-2778821.name: Le Freak
르프리크-2778821.description: Le Freak is a handmade burger specialist using only chicken patties, a standout even amid the many well-known restaurants of Seongsu-dong. Its signature dishes are its signature chicken burger and a rotating seasonal special burger, alongside fried chicken, truffle fries, and corn fritters, served with drinks. Burgers can be ordered at one of three spice levels. The red-hatted chicken character decorating the interior is a memorable touch, and the red chairs and wood-paneled walls give the place the feel of an American diner. It's a 5-minute walk from Exit 4 of Seongsu Station (Line 2).

악어떡볶이-2779132.name: Crocodile Tteokbokki
악어떡볶이-2779132.description: Crocodile Tteokbokki, near Hanyang University in Wangsimni, Seongdong-gu, is a bunsik shop serving spicy yet mild, soft, chewy rice tteokbokki alongside crispy fried snacks and sundae. Known for its rice tteok freshly milled each morning at a local rice mill, it grew even more popular after being featured on several TV programs. Its tteokbokki meal kit is now also available to buy online. There's no dedicated parking, and it's a 5-minute walk from Exit 6 of Wangsimni Station (Line 2).

철길왕갈비살-2778423.name: Cheolgil Wang Galbisal
철길왕갈비살-2778423.description: Cheolgil Wang Galbisal, in Changjeon-dong, Mapo-gu, is a well-known spot among locals. Its signature dishes are marinated and plain beef galbisal (rib finger meat), grilled over hot charcoal for exceptional flavor. Beyond galbisal, it also serves fresh pork belly, fresh pork neck, and Korean-beef yukhoe. Interestingly, its doenjang jjigae (soybean paste stew) is nearly as popular as the signature galbisal — its distinctively seasoned stew is well known, with some customers coming just for that. It's close to Hongik Univ. Station (Gyeongui-Jungang Line), putting it near Hongdae and Sinchon with plenty to do nearby.

용두동쭈꾸미-본점-2763804.name: Yongdu-dong Jjukkumi Main Branch
용두동쭈꾸미-본점-2763804.description: Jegi-dong, Dongdaemun-gu, is well known for its webfoot-octopus alley, and Yongdu-dong Jjukkumi's main branch stands out for serving its spicy jjukkumi alongside a thick curry sauce with tofu to help temper the heat. Its steamed egg and the fried rice made from the leftover sauce are also popular. This reputation has earned it spots on several TV food programs. It's about 200m from Exit 6 of Jegi-dong Station (Line 1), inside the Yongdu-dong jjukkumi alley. There's no dedicated lot, though about 2 cars can park beside the shop — given the tight space, public transit is recommended.

두에꼬제-403509.name: Due Cose
두에꼬제-403509.description: Due Cose, in Hannam-dong, Yongsan-gu, specializes in Italian food. Its signature dishes include a steak salad, carbonara pasta, and jalapeño pasta, alongside a range of soups, pizza, and risotto. The pizza is baked directly in a wood-fired oven for a crisp, thin crust. With a comfortable, warm atmosphere, it's a good spot for a date or family gathering. Due Cose has built a strong reputation in Hannam-dong and has been featured in various media.

하단-2469474.name: Hadan
하단-2469474.description: Hadan, in Seongbuk-dong, Seongbuk-gu, lets diners taste the skill of an owner from Hadan, South Pyongan Province, who has cooked North Korean food for over 20 years — the restaurant's name comes from the owner's hometown. It's a place to try North Korean cuisine, still unfamiliar to many. Taking off your shoes at the entrance sets a warm, welcoming tone, almost like visiting a grandmother's home. Its signature dishes are mandu-guk (dumpling soup) and mandu jeongol (dumpling hot pot), both simmered cleanly in clear broth. Its cold buckwheat kalguksu, made with a refreshing blend of beef broth and dongchimi (radish water kimchi) broth, is also popular, along with a savory mung-bean pancake that pairs nicely alongside it.

한국순대-서초구-2757738.name: Hanguk Sundae (Seocho-gu)
한국순대-서초구-2757738.description: Hanguk Sundae, in Yangjae-dong, Seocho-gu, is open 24/7 year-round, with a pojangmacha-like exterior true to a sundae-guk restaurant serving both hangover soup after drinking and food to pair with drinks. As its name suggests, sundae-guk is the signature dish, alongside popular sulguk and haejangguk. As a well-known Yangjae-dong institution, its walls are covered with visitors' signatures. Customers stream in steadily from morning to night. It's down an alley past Champodo Namu Hospital, out Exit 8 of Yangjae Station (Lines 3, Sinbundang).

푸주옥-2758120.name: Pujuok
푸주옥-2758120.description: Pujuok, in Yangcheon-gu, is a local favorite serving seolleongtang (ox-bone soup), doganitang, and boiled meat. Walking in, visitors can see broth simmering in a massive cauldron right at the entrance. Beyond seolleongtang and doganitang, it also serves gomtang with offal and kkori-gomtang (oxtail soup). Surrounded by Maebongsan and Gyenam Neighborhood Park, two of Yangcheon-gu's signature green spaces, it's a good spot for a walk after eating. It's across from Yangcheon High School near Sinjeong Negeori Station (Line 2). With long hours from morning to night, it's convenient to visit anytime.

성수족발-2373394.name: Seongsu Jokbal
성수족발-2373394.description: Seongsu Jokbal, in Seongsu-dong, is famous enough to be called one of Seoul's three great jokbal restaurants. With so many customers, there's usually a wait, and those who've tried it once tend to come back. As a jokbal specialist, its menu features only jokbal. Its seasoning has a sweet flavor that appeals to a wide range of tastes, with a plump, chewy texture. It's even better paired with the side dishes served alongside it, like bean-sprout soup and chive kimchi. With heavy crowds and a small dining space, takeout is recommended.

최수사-대게마을-2465041.name: Choisusa Snow Crab Village
최수사-대게마을-2465041.description: Choisusa Snow Crab Village, an authentic Japanese restaurant, serves upscale, flavorful snow crab in a stylish setting. Known for fresh ingredients and a clean interior, it also serves sashimi, sushi, and fresh raw fish alongside its crab. Given its business-district location, it's equipped with private rooms suited for business meetings, making it a good choice for group gatherings and year-end parties.

효뜨-2807589.name: Hyodde
효뜨-2807589.description: Hyodde is a Vietnamese restaurant with an exterior that immediately evokes Vietnam. Located down an alley not far from Sinyongsan Station, it's considered a longtime fixture of Yongridan-gil. It's also known as a filming location for 'The Roundup.' Hyodde has separate lunch and dinner menus, so visit at the right time for what you want to eat. Its rich chicken pho is delicious, and its most popular dish is fried chicken.

마구로센-한남점-2856413.name: Maguro Sen Hannam Branch
마구로센-한남점-2856413.description: Maguro Sen's Hannam branch is a Japanese restaurant tucked into a small back alley in Hannam-dong. It originally specialized in Japanese-style aged tuna sashimi, but as more customers asked to try a wider range of tuna cuts, it rebranded to focus on aged bluefin tuna sashimi and specialty cuts. The 1st floor is the main dining room and the basement an annex, with a spacious hall offering table configurations for different group sizes plus private rooms — good for gatherings and hosting guests. Its signature offering is a course menu with three options — A, B, and C. Courses A and B each include three rounds of sashimi, with the chef explaining each cut and the best way to enjoy it. Tuna sashimi is also available to go.

백년가게-장군숯불족발-2563380.name: [Century-Old Shop] General's Charcoal Jokbal
백년가게-장군숯불족발-2563380.description: Selected as a 'Century-Old Shop' by the Ministry of SMEs and Startups in 2018, General's Charcoal Jokbal has thrived in Nowon-gu for 30 years, a signature local favorite that turns first-timers into regulars. Its signature charcoal jokbal is boiled to tender perfection, then grilled twice more over charcoal for a smoky finish. Its popular spicy charcoal jokbal tosses the jokbal in the restaurant's special sauce before grilling over charcoal, taking on a smoky, spicy flavor. The charcoal-grilling step adds 10–15 minutes to the usual cook time. Its original cold jokbal, with a firm, chewy texture like sliced boiled pork, is a classic old-style cold jokbal that pairs especially well with salted shrimp.

장안동-먹깨비-간장게장-해물아구찜-2842680.name: Jangan-dong Meokkkaebi Ganjang Gejang Haemul Agujjim
